providers.description: Plenful is an AI-powered workflow automation platform for pharmacy and healthcare operations, founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco with an office in New York City. The platform automates complex, high-ROI administrative pharmacy workflows — 340B audit and optimization, 340B referral capture, rebate and Maximum Fair Price (MFP) reconciliation, benefits verification and prior authorization, and infusion order intake — using large language models and machine learning tuned to each organization's data. It ingests PDFs, flat files, APIs, HL7 feeds, and databases, supports unlimited organizational logic rules, and serves 100+ healthcare organizations including Prisma Health, Renown Health, Temple Health, Cencora, and Samaritan Health Services. Plenful is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Notable Capital (formerly GGV Capital), SUSA Ventures, TQ Ventures, and Waterline Ventures. Plenful ships an enterprise SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Vedanta Biosciences
providers.description: Vedanta Biosciences is a late clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered at 19 Blackstone Street in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded by PureTech Health together with a group of scientific co-founders who pioneered the modern understanding of cross-talk between the human microbiome and the immune system. The company develops a potential new category of oral Live Biotherapeutic Products built from rationally defined consortia of human commensal bacteria grown from pure clonal cell banks rather than donor-derived stool, and it maintains technical expertise in the manufacture of live organisms. Its lead program, VE303, is an eight-strain defined bacterial consortium in the global Phase 3 RESTORATiVE303 registrational study for the prevention of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection, following Phase 2 results showing a greater than 80% reduction in the odds of CDI recurrence versus placebo; VE202 is in development for inflammatory bowel disease and VE707 for prevention of multidrug-resistant organism infections. Vedanta has raised a $68 million Series D and a $106.5 million financing, and its programs are supported by non-dilutive awards from BARDA and CARB-X. Vedanta is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it runs a WordPress marketing and corporate site, publishes no developer portal, no SDKs, no GitHub organization and no machine-readable API contract, and an August 2026 probe of vedantabio.com found no OpenAPI, no /llms.txt, no MCP endpoint, no A2A agent card and an empty /.well-known/ discovery surface.

providers.name: Bayer
providers.description: Bayer is a German multinational pharmaceutical and life sciences company operating across pharmaceuticals, consumer health, and crop science. Bayer does not publish a single corporate-level public developer portal; integration is delivered through enterprise partner programs, the Bayer Crop Science Climate FieldView ecosystem (partner-gated APIs and certified-partner integrations), pharmacovigilance and clinical-trial data exchange, and EDI / x12 channels with distributors and pharmacy benefit managers.

providers.name: Diagonal Therapeutics
providers.description: Diagonal Therapeutics is a Watertown, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2022 by CEO Alex Lugovskoy in partnership with Atlas Venture, developing "clustering" agonist antibodies that switch broken signaling pathways back on rather than inhibiting them. Its DIAGONAL product engine pairs computational epitope filtering with experimental screening — generating roughly 200,000 candidate antibody sequences per target, clustering them by predicted shape, binning by receptor complementarity and assembling multispecific antibodies from those bins — to make agonist antibody discovery tractable. The lead program, DIAG723, is a first-in-class ALK1:BMPRII clustering agonist antibody that restores ALK1 signaling; it holds US FDA and EMA orphan drug designation for hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) and entered the Phase 1/2 DIAMOND trial (NCT07623525), with a first patient dosed in July 2026, alongside preclinical work in pulmonary arterial hypertension. The pipeline extends into hematology, hepatology, nephrology and cardiovascular disease. The company has raised roughly USD 255 million across a USD 128 million Series A (April 2024, co-led by BVF Partners and Atlas Venture) and an oversubscribed USD 125 million Series B (January 2026, co-led by Sanofi Ventures and Janus Henderson Investors). Diagonal is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: it operates a Next.js marketing site backed by a Sanity CMS, and publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Medzoomer
providers.description: Medzoomer is an on-demand prescription delivery platform that connects pharmacies, healthcare providers, and patients through a secure, HIPAA-compliant network of verified couriers. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Tampa, Florida, the company handles last-mile medication logistics, including controlled substances (Schedule II-V), with tamper-evident packaging, FDA/TSA-approved envelopes, and real-time order tracking. Pharmacies and couriers operate through dedicated web and mobile applications, and the platform is backed by Techstars, UnitedHealthcare Accelerator, and other investors. Medzoomer operates a private pharmacy integration API but publishes no public developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Vertex Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Vertex Pharmaceuticals is a global biotechnology company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, focused on scientific innovation to create transformative medicines for people with serious diseases. The company specializes in cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, beta thalassemia, APOL1-mediated kidney disease, pain, and other serious conditions. Vertex is committed to responsible sharing of clinical trial data with qualified researchers through formal data request processes.

providers.name: Comprehensive Pharmacy Services
providers.description: Comprehensive Pharmacy Services, now operating as CPS Solutions, LLC, is a healthcare company with more than 50 years of experience providing pharmacy and hospital solutions across the care continuum. It serves independent hospitals, health systems, integrated delivery networks (IDNs), and specialized health facilities with specialty pharmacy, pharmacy management, telepharmacy (24/7/365 support), 340B program compliance, supply chain management, rehabilitation services, and consulting. The company operates two proprietary SaaS platforms — CPS Optimizer for pharmacy management and TherigySTM for specialty pharmacy management — supported by 2,500+ healthcare professionals serving 800+ customers across the United States and Puerto Rico. No public API or developer program is currently published; this profile captures the company identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Inductive
providers.description: Inductive Bio is a New York-based AI drug discovery company building a virtual lab for small molecule optimization. It pairs medicinal chemists with AI to run millions of in silico ADMET experiments before synthesis. Its Beacon-1 models — trained on a pre-competitive, anonymized data consortium spanning thousands of drug programs — won consecutive first-place finishes in the 2025 Polaris/ASAP and 2026 OpenADMET blind ADMET prediction competitions, beating 370+ submissions including entries from Merck and NVIDIA. Products include the Compass software platform (accessible via API), the Indy AI chemistry assistant, the ADME-One high-throughput profiling service, and Embedded Experts. Founded in 2023 by Josh Haimson and Ben Birnbaum (both formerly Flatiron Health); SOC 2 compliant; backed by Obvious Ventures, a16z Bio+Health, Lux Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Character, and S32.

providers.name: Phil
providers.description: PHIL (PHILRx) is a healthtech company operating a digital hub and direct-to-patient platform that helps pharmaceutical brands maximize prescription starts, insurance coverage, affordability, and medication adherence. Its all-in-one platform connects pharma manufacturers, patients, and healthcare providers to streamline the prescription access experience, run affordable direct-to-patient and cash-pay programs, and improve commercial performance across the medication access journey. PHIL is a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: TandemAI
providers.description: TandemAI is an integrated drug discovery contract research organization (CRO) that combines proprietary AI and physics-based computational methods with in-house high-performance computing and extensive wet-lab operations to accelerate pharmaceutical research. Its cloud-enabled, data-centric, browser-based platform, TandemViz, spans hit finding, hit-to-lead and lead optimization, digital assays and workflows, medicinal chemistry and synthesis, biological assays, and a peptide platform. TandemAI is offered as an FTE-based service model that bundles wet-lab services with complimentary access to its AI and computational tools, or as a stand-alone SaaS software license. The company merged with Perpetual Medicines and is backed by Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Verisian
providers.description: Verisian is an AI infrastructure platform for clinical trials, giving pharmaceutical sponsors and CROs the information infrastructure required to deploy AI across their experts and processes. The platform provides full study traceability and automates statistical programming workflows: automating the validation of SDTM and ADaM analysis datasets (turning time-consuming QC double-programming into value-generating QA oversight), and generating complete define-XML files and draft reviewer's guides that are guaranteed consistent with the underlying analysis, so teams are submission-ready in hours. Verisian is cloud native, compatible with any statistical computing environment (SCE), storage, or compute, and integrates through simple file transfer with no complex API integration required. It serves statistical programmers, statisticians, data managers, medical writers, clinicians, and regulatory teams across in-house and CRO-outsourced operating models; Bayer is a named customer. There is no public developer API surface — the product is an enterprise application (app.verisian.com) accessed after sales onboarding.

providers.name: VetSource
providers.description: VetSource is a veterinary technology and pharmacy company founded in 2008 that delivers a suite of pharmacy, technology, and business services for the pet health industry. Its offerings span home-delivery prescription management (an online pharmacy and prescription workflow that lets veterinary practices prescribe and fulfill medications with compliance and revenue tools), the Vet2Pet client-engagement platform (a custom-branded app connecting practices with pet owners for communication, reminders, loyalty, and telehealth), and data/analytics services that provide industry benchmarking and practice performance insights. VetSource serves veterinary practices and pet owners across North America. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation is published; this profile captures the company identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Enjamb Labs
providers.description: Enjamb Labs builds an AI-agent platform for pharmaceutical drug development. Its browser-based "integrated research environment" runs specialized agents across the full R&D lifecycle -- clinical evidence synthesis, trial design and statistical programming, and regulatory submission preparation -- while connecting to the systems pharma teams already use (Benchling, Veeva, Medidata, SAS) so no data migration is required. The workspace bundles Word/Excel/PowerPoint editors, Python and R compute environments, and 100+ scientific integrations, and emphasizes auditability, traceability, and human review, keeping each output attached to its sources, files, code, and decisions. Backed by Y Combinator and Founders, Inc., Enjamb reports early usage across major pharmaceutical companies including Johnson & Johnson, Merck, AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, and Sanofi.

providers.name: Ionis Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Ionis Pharmaceuticals is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Ionis Pharmaceuticals API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Alto Pharmacy
providers.description: Alto Pharmacy is a San Francisco-based digital pharmacy and pharmacy-technology company (founded 2015 as ScriptDash) that combines a full-service licensed pharmacy with a proprietary pharmacy operating system, Alto OS. Alto fills retail, specialty and fertility prescriptions with same-day courier delivery, pharmacist care and automated benefits investigation, and it sells that stack to industry partners as Alto Hub+, Alto Dispensing and Alto Complete — hub services, dispensing and end-to-end pharmacy-as-a-service for pharmaceutical manufacturers, health plans, health systems and digital health companies. Alto markets intake, transfer and Surescripts-based integrations to those partners, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable specification; technical access runs through its partnerships team.

providers.name: Converge Bio
providers.description: Converge Bio is a generative-AI platform for life sciences that accelerates drug development across discovery, molecular design, and manufacturing. It trains Bio-LLM foundation models directly on biological languages (DNA, RNA, and protein sequences) and delivers them through the Converge Computational Lab, whose applications include ConvergeAB (AI antibody design across IgG/VHH/bispecific formats), ConvergeGEO (protein gene-expression optimization across CHO/HEK293/E. coli and other cell systems), ConvergeCELL (virtual cell simulation for target and biomarker discovery), and a Patent Extractor for mining antibody sequences. The platform is delivered to biotech and pharmaceutical customers under a Request Access engagement model; there is no public developer API, SDK, or self-serve documentation surface today. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners ($25M Series A, January 2026); founded 2023.

providers.name: Healthera
providers.description: Healthera is a United Kingdom digital-health and patient-engagement company, founded in 2015 by Cambridge University students and headquartered in Cambridge, England. It runs a patient-facing pharmacy app and website for ordering NHS prescriptions and medicines online and booking pharmacy services (Pharmacy First, treatments, vaccinations), alongside a pharmacy-facing SaaS "Patient Experience Platform" used by 1,700+ community pharmacies to manage repeat prescriptions, bookings, marketing, and delivery. In November 2022 Healthera became the first pharmacy app to integrate with the NHS Electronic Prescription Service (EPS), and it connects to NHS Digital / NHS England systems plus third-party platforms such as myGP, eConsult, Cegedim Rx Pharmacy Manager, Medpoint, Royal Mail, and Uber for same-hour delivery. Healthera markets custom integration APIs to pharmacy and brand partners, but as of this review it publishes no public developer portal, no self-serve API documentation, and no machine-readable contract; its api.healthera.co.uk "Healthera Core" host is a private backend and exposes no FHIR CapabilityStatement. Integration is partner-gated rather than self-serve.

providers.name: DXY
providers.description: DXY (丁香园) is China's leading digital healthcare technology company, founded in 2000 in Harbin and headquartered in Hangzhou. It operates a "D+C" dual strategy: a professional physician community and clinical toolset (drug reference "用药助手", clinical case database, medical education, and the "Insight" pharmaceutical data analytics platform) alongside consumer health services under the "丁香医生" (Dingxiang Doctor) brand. DXY also runs the Biomart / 丁香通 life-sciences supplies marketplace. Its Medical Data Open Platform (open.dxy.cn) exposes standardized healthcare data services — newly-approved drugs, drug SKU and drug search, disease search, and hospital/institution search — as REST/JSON APIs under api.dxy.cn for pharmaceutical, medical, and health-tech partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Antheia
providers.description: Antheia, Inc. is a Menlo Park, California synthetic-biology company that manufactures biosynthetic key starting materials (KSMs) and active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) for essential medicines. Founded on Christina Smolke's Stanford research, Antheia engineers yeast strains that reconstruct long, complex plant biosynthetic pathways and ferment sugar into molecules previously obtainable only through agricultural cultivation, compressing production timelines from years to weeks. Commercial products include fermentation-derived thebaine, oripavine and scopolamine, with a development pipeline of 70+ KSMs and APIs spanning neurology, gastrointestinal and oncology programs. NOTE FOR THE CATALOG: Antheia's "APIs" are Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, not web APIs — the company publishes no developer API, SDK, or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: Imbria Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Imbria Pharmaceuticals is a private, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in the Boston area that is developing novel cardiovascular therapies targeting cardiac energy metabolism. Its lead candidate, ninerafaxstat, is a first-in-class partial fatty acid oxidation (pFOX) inhibitor designed to shift myocardial substrate utilization toward glucose oxidation, generating more ATP per unit of oxygen consumed and improving cardiac metabolic efficiency without affecting heart rate, rhythm, ejection fraction or blood pressure. Ninerafaxstat is in the global FORTITUDE-HCM Phase 2b trial (NCT07023614) for symptomatic non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM), which has no approved treatments, and holds FDA Orphan Drug Designation for that indication; a Phase 2b in cardiometabolic HFpEF is planned. The company is backed by RA Capital, SV Health Investors, Deep Track Capital, Catalio Capital Management, AN Ventures and Cytokinetics. Imbria is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor, and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Jazz Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Jazz Pharmaceuticals is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Jazz Pharmaceuticals API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Opna Bio
providers.description: Opna Bio is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on oncology, developing novel small-molecule and targeted-degrader therapeutics against key regulators of cancer, including the Hallmarks of Cancer. Its pipeline features OPN-6602 (an EP300/CBP inhibitor in Phase 1 for multiple myeloma, granted FDA Fast Track designation), zavabresib (OPN-2853, a BET inhibitor with Orphan Drug designation for myelofibrosis), multi-functional protein degraders, and additional programs targeting hematologic malignancies and solid tumors. The company operates from South San Francisco and San Diego, California, and Lausanne, Switzerland.

providers.name: Pedestal Health (formerly Target RWE)
providers.description: Pedestal Health, formerly Target RWE (and NoviSci), is a Durham, North Carolina real-world evidence and health-data company serving life sciences organizations and health systems. It generates regulatory-grade real-world evidence from large-scale observational data and longitudinal patient cohorts across hepatology, dermatology, and gastroenterology (including the TARGET-NASH, TARGET-Derm, and TARGET-Gastro registries), supporting clinical development, regulatory strategy, and care delivery. The company operates as a data, research, and services provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched from the company's public website (targetrwe.com now redirects to pedestalhealth.com).

providers.name: Peel Therapeutics
providers.description: Peel Therapeutics is an evolutionary-medicine biotechnology company headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, with research teams in the United States and Israel. Co-founded in 2015 by pediatric oncologist Dr. Joshua Schiffman, the company translates molecules that evolution has already validated in nature into therapeutics for patients with cancer and inflammatory disease. Its founding program is built on elephant p53 (EP53) — elephants carry roughly forty copies of the p53 tumor-suppressor gene against the human two — delivered as liposomal protein nanoparticles, alongside PEEL-224, a TOP1 inhibitor in clinical development. Discovery runs on the company's proprietary, internal Darwin.AI platform and the Darwin Biobank, a comparative-oncology sample collection. Peel is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: QurAlis
providers.description: QurAlis Corporation is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded on December 12, 2016 in Cambridge, Massachusetts by Drs. Kasper Roet, Kevin Eggan and Clifford Woolf together with Q-State Biosciences, and staffed by neurodegenerative biologists out of Harvard Medical School and Harvard University. The company develops precision medicines for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and other neurodegenerative and neurological diseases, built on the discovery — published in Nature Neuroscience by co-founder Kevin Eggan's lab — that loss of normal TDP-43 function drives a decrease in STATHMIN-2 (STMN2) expression and impairs neuronal repair. Its lead candidates are QRL-201, a first-in-class molecule intended to restore STMN2 expression in ALS (ANQUR trial), and QRL-101, a potentially best-in-class selective Kv7.2/7.3 ion channel opener for hyperexcitability-induced disease progression in ALS as well as epilepsy and pain; a third program targets UNC13A cryptic-exon mis-splicing. Therapies are built on the proprietary FlexASO® anti-sense oligonucleotide splice-modulator platform. QurAlis publishes a corporate site covering its story, pipeline, platform, people, patient resources, presentations and press releases, but runs no developer program: no API documentation, no SDKs, no developer portal, no GitHub organisation and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Scimplify
providers.description: Scimplify is a Bengaluru-based advanced specialty chemicals company that combines deep chemical expertise, software, and global manufacturing capacity to make complex chemical supply predictable at scale. Founded in 2023, it operates as a contract research (CRO) and contract manufacturing (CMO) organization across the specialty-chemicals lifecycle, serving pharmaceutical, agrochemical, flavors & fragrances, industrial, beauty & personal care, food & nutrition, dyes & pigments, oleochemicals, flame retardants, and critical-metals industries. Its integrated Scinode platform, IONS R&D and ATOMS manufacturing ecosystems, and Scira AI agentic layer coordinate discovery, sourcing, and production. Scimplify publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its web, content, and domain-security surface.

providers.name: Terremoto Biosciences
providers.description: Terremoto Biosciences is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company based in South San Francisco, California, building a covalent drug discovery and development engine around lysine-based covalency. Founded in 2022 by veterans of Principia Biopharma and backed by OrbiMed and Third Rock Ventures across Series A ($75M), Series B ($175M) and Series C ($108M) financings, the company designs highly selective small-molecule medicines aimed both at improving on known drug targets and at reaching targets previously considered undruggable. Its lead program, TER-2013, is an AKT1-selective inhibitor granted FDA Fast Track designation for breast cancer, with additional work in oncology and hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia. Terremoto is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable API contract, and its public web surface is a corporate marketing site covering science, pipeline, news and careers.

providers.name: TrueBinding
providers.description: TrueBinding, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotherapeutic company founded in 2016 and headquartered at 4701 Patrick Henry Drive, Santa Clara, California. It develops humanized monoclonal antibodies against Galectin-3 to resolve chronic inflammation ("inflammaging"), led by TB006, which has completed Phase 1b/2a work in Alzheimer's disease and holds an FDA IND clearance for a Phase 2A trial in Parkinson's disease, with additional research programs across ALS, glioblastoma, autism spectrum, stroke, metabolic disease and oncology. Alongside its own pipeline the company sells contract development and manufacturing (CDMO) services from its Santa Clara facility - antibody discovery, cell-line and process development, cGMP monoclonal antibody and media/buffer manufacturing, vivarium and toxicology studies, histology and imaging, clinical drug product logistics, and cGMP training and audit preparation. TrueBinding ships no software product and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable API contract; its web presence is a Squarespace marketing and patient-access site.

providers.name: Kymera Therapeutics
providers.description: Kymera Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered at 500 North Beacon Street in Watertown, Massachusetts, pioneering targeted protein degradation as a way to build oral small-molecule medicines against targets that conventional inhibitors cannot reach. Rather than blocking a protein's activity, Kymera's degraders recruit the body's own protein-disposal machinery so that a binding event alone is sufficient to eliminate the disease-driving protein, an approach the company describes as a disease-agnostic modality. Its wholly-owned pipeline is led by KT-621, a once-daily oral STAT6 degrader in Phase 2 for Type 2 inflammatory diseases including atopic dermatitis, asthma, COPD and chronic spontaneous urticaria, and KT-579, a first-in-class oral IRF5 degrader in Phase 1 for lupus, Sjogren's syndrome and rheumatoid arthritis. Partnered programs include the oral IRAK4 degrader KT-485/SAR447971 with Sanofi and the CDK2 molecular glue degrader KT-200 with Gilead Sciences. Kymera publishes no public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web, investor, patient and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AbbVie
providers.description: AbbVie is a research-based biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, manufactures, and markets advanced therapies in immunology, oncology, neuroscience, and other specialty areas. AbbVie's portfolio includes treatments for autoimmune diseases, various cancers, neurological disorders, and aesthetics through the Allergan Aesthetics portfolio.

providers.name: AstraZeneca
providers.description: AstraZeneca is a British-Swedish multinational pharmaceutical and biotechnology company focused on oncology, cardiovascular, renal, metabolism, and respiratory therapies. AstraZeneca does not publish a general developer portal or commercial public APIs; technology integration is delivered through enterprise partner programs, clinical trial data portals such as clinicaltrials.gov and the Vivli platform, and EDI/x12 channels used by distributors and pharmacy benefit managers.

providers.name: Catalent
providers.description: Catalent is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Catalent API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Biosplice Therapeutics
providers.description: Biosplice Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 2008 by Osman Kibar and known until its 2020 rename as Samumed, LLC (samumed.com still redirects to biosplice.com). The company develops first-in-class small-molecule therapeutics that act on novel components of the Wnt signaling pathway and on the regulation of alternative pre-mRNA splicing. Its lead program is lorecivivint, an investigational intra-articular knee injection for osteoarthritis, positioned against a stated unmet need of "over 50 million US patients suffer from osteoarthritis, with no drugs available to arrest the disease"; the candidate has completed Phase 3 study and a New Drug Application has been submitted to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Programs outside lorecivivint — neurology, diabetes and oncology — are developed by the company's affiliate TenaRx, Inc. The company is led by Erich Horsley (Chief Executive Officer) with Osman Kibar as Founder and Executive Chairman, Yusuf Yazici as Chief Medical Officer, Phil Wilson as Chief Financial Officer and Scott W. Bulcao as Chief Legal Officer. Biosplice is a drug-discovery and clinical-development organization, not a software vendor: biosplice.com is a small ASP.NET corporate site covering mission, board, management, advisors, programs, publications, news and careers, and the company publishes no developer program of any kind — no API, no SDK, no developer portal, no GitHub organization and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Nawah Scientific
providers.description: Nawah Scientific is MENA and Africa's first Cloud Lab, providing analytical testing and R&D services to the region's life science, food, agricultural, and pharmaceutical sectors. Through its online platform researchers and companies can request laboratory analyses, submit and track samples, and access remote scientific instrument time and data services. Headquartered in Egypt with expansion across Saudi Arabia and Rwanda, Nawah operates as a research engine backed by 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile currently tracks the company's public web presence; no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer documentation surface has been identified at this time.

providers.name: Adicet Bio
providers.description: Adicet Bio, Inc. (Nasdaq: ACET) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company with offices in Redwood City, California and Boston, Massachusetts, discovering and developing allogeneic "off-the-shelf" gamma delta T cell therapies engineered with chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) for autoimmune disease and cancer. Its lead candidate, prulacabtagene leucel (prula-cel), is an anti-CD20 gamma delta CAR T cell therapy in development for B cell-mediated autoimmune diseases, alongside ADI-212 for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Adicet publishes a corporate website covering its science platform, clinical pipeline, leadership and careers, plus a vendor-hosted investor relations portal. It operates no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface of any kind; this profile records that absence rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Adlai Nortye
providers.description: Adlai Nortye is a global clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, headquartered in Hangzhou, China with US operations in New Jersey, developing differentiated immuno-oncology and precision-targeted cancer medicines. Its pipeline covers two therapeutic areas: precision RAS pathway targeted therapies — the oral pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor AN9025 and the CEACAM5-targeting antibody-drug conjugate AN4035 built on the company's proprietary RASiCA (RAS Inhibitor Conjugated Antibody) platform — and next-generation PD-1/L1 pathway modulating immunotherapies including AN8025, a multi-functional T-cell and antigen-presenting-cell modulating fusion protein, plus the oral EP4 antagonist AN0025 (palupiprant). The company is listed on Nasdaq under the ticker ANL. Adlai Nortye publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Day One Biopharmaceuticals
providers.description: Day One Biopharmaceuticals is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company developing and commercializing targeted therapies for people of all ages living with life-threatening diseases, with an initial focus on pediatric and rare cancers. Its lead product OJEMDA (tovorafenib) is an FDA-approved treatment for relapsed or refractory pediatric low-grade glioma, and its pipeline includes DAY301 and the antibody-drug conjugate Emi-Le. Headquartered in Brisbane, California, the company was acquired by and is now part of the Servier Group as of March 2026. Day One was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; it maintains a corporate and investor-relations web presence but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic surface.

providers.name: Rapport Therapeutics
providers.description: Rapport Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: RAPP) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts with research operations in San Diego, California, founded in 2022 and taken public in a $174 million IPO in June 2024. Rapport develops precision small-molecule medicines for central nervous system disorders using its proprietary RAP technology platform, which pairs human genetics with functional proteomics to identify receptor-associated proteins that confer neuroanatomical specificity — the goal being drugs that act only where the disease circuit lives rather than across the whole brain. Its lead clinical candidate, RAP-219, is a selective negative allosteric modulator of TARP-gamma-8-associated AMPA receptors in development for focal onset seizures, peripheral neuropathic pain and bipolar disorder, behind two discovery-stage nicotinic acetylcholine receptor programs targeting alpha-6 (chronic pain) and alpha-9-alpha-10 (hearing disorders). Rapport is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: the RAP platform is an internal discovery capability and the company publishes no developer program, no public API and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: ltztherapeutics
providers.description: LTZ Therapeutics is a clinical-stage immunotherapy biotechnology company developing novel myeloid engager therapeutics for cancer treatment. Its platform focuses on the direct engagement of myeloid cells with target cells to boost anti-tumor immunity, with lead candidate LTZ-232 receiving FDA IND clearance in July 2026 for advanced metastatic colorectal cancer and other solid tumors. The company operates from Redwood City, USA and Shenzhen, China. It is a portfolio company of Qiming and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; it publishes no developer API surface.

providers.name: Ostro
providers.description: Ostro (Veeva Ostro) is an AI-powered brand engagement platform for life sciences. Founded in 2019 as RxDefine and legally incorporated as Rise Healthcare Tech, Inc., the Miami-based, remote-first company turns a pharmaceutical brand's existing PRC/MLR-approved content into compliant, two-way conversational AI across web, email and SMS. Its products are Navigate (web engagement), Airmark (conversational email for HCPs), Prompt (SMS) and Tailor (brand-website intelligence), unified in September 2025 into a single digital experience. The platform is grounded exclusively in approved content and is designed not to generate novel responses, which is how it clears promotional-review requirements. Veeva Systems (NYSE: VEEV) acquired Ostro on 2026-03-10 for approximately $100M and runs it as an independent unit whose capabilities are being folded into Veeva Commercial Cloud. Ostro publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract; its only machine-readable surface is an llms.txt served at its own website root.

providers.name: Ring Therapeutics
providers.description: Ring Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company founded by Flagship Pioneering that develops targeted vector conjugate medicines built on the human commensal virome. Its Anellogy platform harnesses anelloviruses — commensal viruses that co-exist with the human immune system — to generate gene delivery vectors with tissue-specific tropism and the potential to be redosed. Ring has sequenced thousands of anelloviruses into what it describes as the largest anellovirus database assembled to date, and has raised more than $250 million across Series A, B and C financings. The company is a therapeutics developer rather than a software provider: it publishes a corporate site, a press release stream and a scientific publications list, and operates no public API, developer portal or SDK.

providers.name: Terray Therapeutics
providers.description: Terray Therapeutics is an AI-native, chemistry-first biotechnology company building an integrated full-stack platform for small molecule drug discovery. Its EMMI platform (Experimentation Meets Machine Intelligence) pairs a proprietary ultra-miniaturized microarray assay system and fully automated lab with a family of machine learning models: COATI, a chemistry foundation model trained on roughly a billion molecules that encodes molecules into a latent space; reinforcement-learning generative models for synthesizable de novo design; TerraBind for potency prediction; and EMMI Select for uncertainty-aware molecule selection. Terray reports a proprietary target-molecule interaction dataset of more than 17 billion measurements growing by about a billion per quarter, and runs multi-target discovery collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Gilead, Calico and Odyssey Therapeutics, with investment from NVIDIA. Terray publishes several of its research code libraries as open source on GitHub (COATI, COATI-LDM, TerraMax) but operates no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: TRexBio
providers.description: TRexBio, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered at 681 Gateway Blvd in South San Francisco, California, founded in 2018 and seed funded by SV Health Investors, that discovers and develops immunoregulatory biologics based on tissue regulatory T cell (Treg) biology. Its Deep Biology Platform combines human tissue samples, computational biology and immunobiology expertise to map how tissue Tregs behave in disease and to identify and characterize novel targets for inflammatory, autoimmune and other immune-mediated conditions. Disclosed programs include TRB-061, the CD30 agonist TRB-071, TRB-081, and the Lilly-partnered TRB-051, with Phase 1 trials expected to initiate in 2027. The company announced an $84 million Series B in November 2024 and closed a further $50 million financing in January 2026; investors include Eli Lilly and Company, Pfizer Ventures, Johnson & Johnson, SV Health Investors and Polaris Partners. TRexBio publishes no developer program, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable API contract. trex.bio is a WordPress marketing site whose only machine-readable surfaces are the WordPress core REST API, a Yoast-generated llms.txt, and an OAuth-protected WordPress MCP adapter endpoint — CMS infrastructure rather than a product API.

providers.name: W. R. Grace
providers.description: W. R. Grace & Co. is a global producer of specialty chemicals and specialty materials, providing catalysts and process technologies to refining, petrochemical, and other manufacturers. Grace operates in two segments: Catalysts Technologies (fluid catalytic cracking catalysts, additives, and process technologies) and Materials Technologies (silica-based engineered materials for pharmaceutical, food, coatings, and industrial applications). Grace's Fine Chemical Manufacturing Services division provides active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) development and manufacturing for the pharmaceutical industry. W. R. Grace does not offer a public developer API for software integration.

providers.name: AbelZeta Pharma
providers.description: AbelZeta Pharma is a global clinical-stage cell therapy company discovering, developing, and manufacturing T-cell-based immunotherapeutics for cancer and immunological diseases. Its pipeline centers on Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR)-T cell technology across hematologic malignancies, solid tumors, and inflammatory and immunological conditions. Backed by Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China), AbelZeta develops personalized immune cell therapies that empower patients' own immune systems to address unmet medical needs, with operations in the United States (Maryland) and China. AbelZeta does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's corporate web presence and identity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Affinia Therapeutics
providers.description: Affinia Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company in Waltham, Massachusetts pioneering next-generation adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapies. Using AI and structural modeling to rationally design novel capsids that better target tissues for improved safety and effectiveness, Affinia develops therapeutic cargoes for devastating rare and prevalent diseases of the heart and the nervous system. Its lead program, AFTX-201, targets BAG3-associated dilated cardiomyopathy and is being evaluated in the UPBEAT trial. Affinia Therapeutics is a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). This company profile carries no public API surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network for identity and demand signal.

providers.name: Alcresta Therapeutics
providers.description: Alcresta Therapeutics is a specialty pharmaceutical company developing enzyme-based products that improve fat absorption and digestive health for people with rare and chronic conditions. Its lead product, the RELiZORB (immobilized lipase) cartridge, uses the company's patented iLipase microbead technology to mimic pancreatic lipase and hydrolyze fats in enteral (tube) feeding formulas, helping patients with exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, cystic fibrosis, short bowel syndrome, and critical-care nutrition needs absorb fatty acids they otherwise could not. Alcresta is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. The company operates a corporate and product marketing website but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications at this time.

providers.name: Alloy Therapeutics
providers.description: Alloy Therapeutics is a biotechnology ecosystem company operating as a Product Development Organization that partners across discovery, preclinical, and clinical development. It combines proprietary AI/ML, real-world data, and tech-enabled scientific services across multiple therapeutic modalities, including monoclonal and bispecific antibodies, TCR mimics, genetic medicines (cyclic RNA and oligonucleotide design), and cell-therapy pharmacology. Alloy is known for its transgenic antibody-discovery platforms (the ATX-Gx mouse series) and licenses reagents, platforms, and services to pharmaceutical and biotech partners rather than exposing a public developer API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Apnimed
providers.description: Apnimed is a late-stage clinical-stage pharmaceutical company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing novel oral drug therapies for sleep-related breathing disorders. Its lead candidate AD109 (Oxnimbi) is a fixed-dose combination of an anti-muscarinic and a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, designed to improve upper-airway muscle activity and treat an underlying neuromuscular cause of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) rather than manage it mechanically. The company was founded in 2017, partners with Shionogi through the Shionogi-Apnimed Sleep Science (SASS) joint venture, and had a New Drug Application for AD109 accepted by the FDA in 2026. Apnimed is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: asieris
providers.description: Asieris Pharmaceuticals is a China-based biopharmaceutical company developing innovative therapies in genitourinary tumors and women's health. Its focus areas span urologic oncology (bladder cancer diagnosis and treatment), women's health, and breast and gynecologic oncology, with marquee assets Vesique (APL-1202) for bladder cancer and Cevira (APL-1702), a non-invasive photodynamic therapy for cervical precancerous lesions. The company runs three proprietary R&D platforms (TIMN, TAIDD, DDC). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; as a biopharma company it publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: At-Home-Doc
providers.description: At-Home-Doc (now branded MetaDoc) is a Qatar-based healthcare SuperApp operated by Medihealth Solutions (MOPH Licence No. 2066) offering round-the-clock virtual and in-person medical care. Patients book on-demand video consultations, in-network clinic appointments, or home doctor visits through the app, alongside pharmacy delivery, lab-at-home services, family insurance packages, and a Med Coins loyalty rewards program. The platform bundles Meta Doc (virtual clinics for practitioners), Meta Patient (a patient community), and Medi Shop into a single consumer healthcare experience delivered over iOS and Android. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Cerevance
providers.description: Cerevance is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics for central nervous system (CNS) disorders. Its proprietary NETSseq platform profiles gene expression across specific human brain cell types from post-mortem tissue to identify previously undiscovered, cell-type-specific drug targets, powering a pipeline of small-molecule candidates for Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, epilepsy, and other neurodegenerative and psychiatric conditions. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV; profiled in the API Evangelist network. Cerevance publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: Condorsoftware
providers.description: Condor Software builds AI-powered financial intelligence software for life sciences R&D organizations, unifying clinical, operational, and financial data to manage complex clinical trial finances. The platform connects data from existing systems (CROs, ERP, CTMS, EDC, procurement), automates AI-powered accruals, invoice reconciliation, and financial close, and delivers board-ready forecasts, scenario planning, and portfolio dashboards for pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device companies. Condor advertises 90%+ forecast accuracy, faster month-end close versus spreadsheets, and a compliance-by-design architecture co-developed with Big 4 accounting firms. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published at this time; integrations with systems such as Veeva, Medidata, SAP, and Oracle NetSuite are delivered through the product. Backed by Felicis; raised a $24M Series A.

providers.name: Connect Biopharma
providers.description: Connect Biopharma is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, dedicated to transforming care for patients with inflammatory diseases such as asthma and COPD. Its lead drug candidate, rademikibart (CBP-201), is an antibody targeting IL-4Ra in Phase 2 clinical development for acute asthma and COPD exacerbations. Surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network, the company operates in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology sector and publishes no public developer portal, API, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Escient Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Escient Pharmaceuticals is a San Diego, California clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing first-in-class, oral small-molecule therapeutics targeting Mas-related G protein-coupled receptors (MRGPRs) along the neurosensory-inflammatory axis. Its lead programs are EP262, an MRGPRX2 antagonist for mast-cell-mediated diseases such as chronic spontaneous and inducible urticaria and atopic dermatitis, and EP547, an MRGPRX4 antagonist for cholestatic and uremic pruritus. The company was backed by New Enterprise Associates (NEA) and was acquired by Incyte Corporation on May 30, 2024. Escient operates a corporate marketing website only and publishes no public API, developer program, or machine-readable API specification; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Expert Intelligence
providers.description: Expert Intelligence is an AI company building analytical automation for pharmaceutical drug-development laboratories. Its platform turns raw instrument data into signed, regulatory-grade results and surfaces lab-wide trends across instruments, methods, and sites. Two integrated products anchor the offering: EI Flow automates batch analysis by converting instrument output into SOP-aware, signed, explainable results that reach LIMS systems in minutes so analysts review only exceptions, and EI Signal unifies historical data across instruments, methods, and sites to surface drift and anomalies before release. The company promotes exception-based review for higher accuracy, a Limited Sample Model (LSM) approach that needs only 30-50 expert examples, and instrument-agnostic deployment across cloud, on-premises, or hybrid environments. Backed by Sierra Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from a VC portfolio and enriched from the company's public website; no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs were found at enrichment time.

providers.name: Frontage Laboratories
providers.description: Frontage Laboratories is a global contract research organization (CRO) providing integrated, science-driven drug discovery and development services across the pharmaceutical and biotechnology lifecycle. Its services span drug discovery (chemistry, biology, ADME/toxicology screening, pharmacology), drug development (DMPK, preclinical safety and toxicology, clinical trial support), laboratory testing (bioanalysis, genomics, central lab, biomarkers), CMC (product development, formulation, analytical services, manufacturing), and agrochemical support. Frontage operates roughly 28 sites across North America, Asia-Pacific, and Europe with about 2,200 employees. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Frontage publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or programmatic integration surface, so this profile captures company identity and web properties only.

providers.name: Hemab Therapeutics
providers.description: Hemab Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with a US presence in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing prophylactic antibody-based therapeutics for serious, underserved bleeding and thrombotic disorders. Its modality-agnostic approach uses monoclonal and bispecific antibodies to stabilize coagulation proteins, prevent their premature breakdown, and direct them to sites of injury. The clinical pipeline targets Glanzmann Thrombasthenia (sutacimig, HMB-001), von Willebrand Disease (HMB-002), Factor VII deficiency and heavy menstrual bleeding. Hemab publishes a corporate marketing site, an investor relations site, and audience-specific sections for patients, caregivers and healthcare providers. It operates no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, machine-readable specification, SDK, or webhook surface on any host it controls.

providers.name: Ideaya Biosciences
providers.description: IDEAYA Biosciences is a clinical-stage precision medicine oncology company headquartered in South San Francisco, California (NASDAQ IDYA), focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing targeted therapeutics for genetically defined cancer patient populations. Its research spans PKC inhibition in uveal melanoma, antibody-drug conjugate and DNA-damage-response combinations, synthetic-lethal MTAP-pathway programs, and KAT6/7 epigenetic inhibition, led by the investigational candidate darovasertib in registrational uveal melanoma trials. The company maintains a corporate and investor-relations web presence and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Impelpharma
providers.description: Impel Pharmaceuticals is a commercial-stage pharmaceutical company developing first-in-class intranasal drug treatments for central nervous system (CNS) disorders with high unmet medical needs. Its proprietary Precision Olfactory Delivery (POD) technology targets the vascular-rich upper nasal cavity to achieve more rapid and consistent bioavailability than conventional delivery. Its lead product, Trudhesa (dihydroergotamine mesylate) nasal spray, is approved for the acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults. Impel was backed by Norwest Venture Partners (co-led its 2018 Series D) and later filed for bankruptcy in December 2023. This is a patient- and science-facing pharma company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Infinant Health
providers.description: Infinant Health (formerly Evolve Biosystems) is a privately held life-sciences company in Sacramento, California, spun out of the Foods for Health Institute at the University of California, Davis after more than a decade of research into the infant gut microbiome. Its foundational discovery is B. infantis EVC001, a strain of Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis that metabolizes human milk oligosaccharides and has largely disappeared from infants in industrialized countries. The company commercializes that strain as Evivo, a consumer infant probiotic sold direct-to-consumer and through retail, and is developing INF108 as a drug candidate intended to reduce necrotizing enterocolitis in premature infants. Infinant Health is a biotechnology and consumer-health manufacturer rather than a software company: it publishes clinical trials, peer-reviewed publications and investor material, but no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract could be found on any of its hosts.

providers.name: Kirilys Therapeutics
providers.description: Kirilys Therapeutics is a multi-asset precision oncology company developing targeted therapeutic treatments for cancer patients. Led by co-founder and CEO BT Slingsby, MD, PhD, MPH, the company is building a pipeline of precision medicines and is backed by Catalys Pacific, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and UBE. Kirilys was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a clinical-stage biotech, Kirilys publishes a corporate marketing website (company, news, and contact pages) but exposes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or machine discovery surface at this time.

providers.name: Orasis Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Orasis Pharmaceuticals is an ophthalmic pharmaceutical company with offices in the United States and Israel, focused on treatments for presbyopia — the age-related loss of near vision that affects roughly two billion people worldwide. Its lead product, QLOSI (pilocarpine hydrochloride ophthalmic solution) 0.4%, is a preservative-free, single-use-vial prescription eye drop approved by the FDA in October 2023 and commercially available in the United States, with a follow-on candidate (BESKA) submitted for approval in Australia. The company is backed by life-sciences investors including Sequoia Capital, Johnson & Johnson Innovation and Arboretum Ventures. Orasis sells a regulated pharmaceutical product, not software: it operates a corporate marketing site plus product sites for patients (qlosi.com) and eye care professionals (qlosiecp.com), and publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: POMS
providers.description: POMS Corporation develops POMSnet Aquila, a Manufacturing Execution System (MES) purpose-built for pharmaceutical, biotech, cell and gene therapy, and medical device manufacturers. The platform delivers FDA-compliant electronic batch records (EBR), production execution, review-by-exception, and plant-floor integration with ERP and equipment systems, deployed on-premise or in the cloud. POMS also offers the POMSnet Falcon EBR analytics dashboards. Founded around its first MES implementation in 1988 and headquartered in Redmond, Washington, POMS sells enterprise software to regulated life-sciences manufacturers rather than publishing a public developer API. Surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead, this profile is enriched from the company's public web presence; no public API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found.

providers.name: Pretzel Therapeutics
providers.description: Pretzel Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company developing first-in-class medicines that target mitochondrial biology and cellular energy regulation. Its pipeline spans neurological, muscular atrophy, metabolic, and rare disease indications, applying novel mitochondrial modulation approaches to conditions driven by dysfunctional cellular energy production. Backed by GV, the company operates as a therapeutics developer and publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company record and life-sciences lead.

providers.name: Rénibus Therapeutics
providers.description: Rénibus Therapeutics is a privately held clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Southlake, Texas, developing treatments for cardio, renal and metabolic disease. Its pipeline is led by veverimer, a non-absorbed polymer in Phase 3 for metabolic acidosis in chronic kidney disease, and RBT-1 (stannic protoporfin / iron sucrose), a first-in-class intravenous pharmacologic preconditioning agent given 24-48 hours before non-emergent cardiac surgery to reduce post-operative complications, which holds FDA Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track designations and completed the pivotal Phase 3 PROTECT trial. The company publishes a corporate marketing site, a news and events feed, an expanded access policy and patient information, but operates no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: SwipeRx
providers.description: SwipeRx (operated by mClinica Pte. Ltd., formerly mClinica Pharmacy Solutions) is the leading community and B2B commerce platform for pharmacies across Southeast Asia. Delivered as a mobile application, it connects a network of more than 300,000 pharmacy professionals and 50,000 retail pharmacies in Indonesia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand and Cambodia. The platform combines professional networking, accredited continuing professional development (CPD) education, industry news, a drug directory, adverse-event reporting, and B2B medicine purchasing (the Belanja marketplace) into a single app that digitizes a historically fragmented pharmacy supply chain. SwipeRx publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; its api.swiperxapp.com host is an undocumented private backend serving the mobile app.

providers.name: Tigermed
providers.description: Tigermed (Hangzhou Tigermed Consulting Co., Ltd.) is a leading global contract research organization (CRO) providing integrated drug and medical device development services across the full clinical lifecycle. Its capabilities span preclinical development (medicinal chemistry, compound screening, toxicology, and bioanalytical services), clinical development (medical writing, clinical monitoring, regulatory affairs, and data management), and integrated services including central laboratories, pharmacovigilance, medical imaging, quality assurance, and real-world and post-marketing studies. The company reports 11,000+ global employees, 180+ offices and locations, and 4,000+ customers, supporting the development of 170+ innovative drugs. Tigermed was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer, API, or technical platform surface.

providers.name: Vividion Therapeutics
providers.description: Vividion Therapeutics is a San Diego-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company that discovers and develops precision small-molecule medicines for previously undruggable disease targets. Its proprietary chemoproteomics platform pairs covalent chemistry with proteome-wide screening to map druggable pockets across the human proteome, driving a pipeline in oncology and immunology (including VVD-214, a WRN helicase inhibitor for MSI-high cancers). Vividion was acquired by Bayer in 2021 and operates as an independent subsidiary. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund; this profile has been enriched and carries no public developer or API surface (a corporate/scientific website only).

providers.name: Zai Lab
providers.description: Zai Lab is an innovative, research-based, commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company based in China and the United States, founded in 2014 with headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts and Shanghai. The company discovers, develops, and commercializes transformative medicines for conditions with significant unmet patient needs across oncology, immunology, neuroscience, and infectious disease. As a fully integrated biopharma, Zai Lab spans early-stage discovery through development, regulatory approval, manufacturing, and commercialization. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of HongShan and Qiming Venture Partners. Zai Lab publishes a corporate and investor web presence but exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Albemarle
providers.description: Albemarle Corporation is a global specialty chemicals company and leading provider of lithium, bromine, and other essential elements. Operating from its global headquarters in Charlotte, NC, Albemarle serves customers in approximately 70 countries with world-class hard-rock and brine lithium resources, state-of-the-art lithium conversion facilities, advanced lithium material and process development, bromine production facilities, and the US's only producing lithium resource in Silver Peak, NV. The company serves critical markets including electric vehicle batteries, energy storage, flame retardants, pharmaceutical ingredients, catalysts, and specialty chemicals, employing approximately 7,800 people and holding over 1,500 active patents worldwide.

providers.name: Sware (fka BTR)
providers.description: Sware (formerly BTR) is a life sciences software company providing AI-driven GxP validation for regulated life sciences and pharmaceutical organizations. Its Res_Q SaaS platform combines a decade of validation intelligence with a Data Cloud and AI agents that automate validation work, surface insights, and keep every decision explainable, traceable, and reversible. A companion product, GxPNext, delivers agentic validation built for software development so teams can embed GxP validation directly into their applications, ship faster, and simplify customer audits. Sware serves quality, regulatory, and engineering leaders across software validation, AI/ML validation, plant and equipment validation, and medical device / SaMD development, and publishes SOC 2 and ISO 9001 certifications. It is backed by Insight Partners. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI is available today (the Res_Q API page is password-gated), so this profile captures the company's public identity, compliance posture, and domain-security probe.

providers.name: Blink Health
providers.description: Blink Health is a healthcare technology company that operates BlinkRx, a digital pharmacy platform connecting patients, prescribers, and pharmaceutical manufacturers to simplify prescription access, fulfillment, and affordability. The platform streamlines the path from a provider writing a prescription to a patient receiving medication at a transparent price, with copay support, home delivery, and manufacturer-sponsored programs. Backed by 8vc, Blink Health runs consumer-facing prescription-savings tools and a provider/pharma-facing BlinkRx offering. No public developer API program or documentation was found during enrichment; a live undocumented API host exists at api.blinkhealth.com.

providers.name: Casma Therapeutics
providers.description: Casma Therapeutics is a privately held clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2018 and headquartered at 201 Brookline Ave, Suite 1401, Boston, MA. Casma develops novel cellular degradation medicines built on the autophagy pathway — the conserved process cells use to clear damaged components. Its PHLYT (Phagosome-Lysosome Targeting) platform initiates target-specific autophagic degradation of disease targets independent of size or complexity, reaching beyond single proteins to organelles, protein aggregates and large signaling complexes, with programs spanning oncology, inflammation, neurodegeneration and metabolic disease. Casma was named to the Fierce 15 list in 2019. The company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs or machine-readable API contract; it is catalogued here as a company profile only.

providers.name: City Therapeutics
providers.description: City Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered at 399 Binney Street in Kendall Square, Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2024 by pioneers of RNA interference including John Maraganore, Phillip Zamore, Kotaro Nakanishi, Yukihide Tomari and Mark Keating. The company engineers next-generation RNAi trigger molecules — including its proprietary cleavage-inducing tiny (city) RNAs — and pairs them with precision targeting ligands designed to deliver siRNAs beyond the liver into ocular, CNS and other extrahepatic tissues. Its pipeline includes CITY-FXI, a Factor XI-targeting candidate for thromboembolic disease, and CITY-RBP4 for Stargardt disease and geographic atrophy, alongside undisclosed hepatic, ocular and CNS programs. City Therapeutics raised a $135M Series A in October 2024 and a $99.5M Series B in June 2026, and holds research collaborations with Biogen and Bausch + Lomb. City Therapeutics publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable interface; it is catalogued here as a company profile only.

providers.name: Lycia Therapeutics
providers.description: Lycia Therapeutics is a South San Francisco, California biotechnology company developing a new class of targeted protein degradation medicines built on its proprietary lysosomal targeting chimera (LYTAC) platform, which originated in the Stanford University laboratory of Nobel laureate Carolyn Bertozzi, Ph.D. LYTAC molecules bind a disease-driving extracellular protein and shuttle it into the cell for destruction by the lysosome, allowing Lycia to pursue circulating and membrane-bound proteins that conventional small molecules and antibodies have been unable to drug. The company is led by President and Chief Executive Officer Aetna Wun Trombley, Ph.D., is backed by Versant Ventures, Redmile Group, Venrock, RTW and Blue Owl among others, and has partnered with Eli Lilly and Company to discover and develop LYTAC degraders. Lycia is a privately held, research-stage therapeutics company; it publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Nuvig Therapeutics
providers.description: Nuvig Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered at 3450 Hillview Avenue, Palo Alto, California, developing next-generation immunomodulators for chronic autoimmune and inflammatory disease. Its lead investigational candidate, NVG-2089, is an engineered Fc fragment designed to selectively engage type II Fc receptors and harness an endogenous regulatory mechanism that resolves autoimmune dysregulation while preserving normal immune function; the first patient was dosed in a Phase 2 trial in chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) in May 2025. The company announced a $161 million Series B financing in December 2024. Nuvig is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, GitHub organization, or machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its public web surface is a corporate WordPress site covering science, pipeline, team, news and careers, from which the only machine-readable artifact published is a Yoast-generated llms.txt.

providers.name: Syntis Bio
providers.description: Syntis Bio is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Boston, Massachusetts developing oral therapies that use the small intestine as a delivery site. Its SYNT platform (Synthetic Tissue-lining) applies a mussel-inspired polydopamine polymer coating transiently to specific tissues in the GI tract, sustaining therapeutic activity for up to 24 hours before being naturally cleared. The platform is being applied to nutrient exclusion for obesity, gut-restricted enzyme replacement for rare metabolic disorders such as homocystinuria and maple syrup urine disease, and oral bioavailability enhancement for peptides and biologics. Lead candidate SYNT-101 is a once-daily oral pill intended to mimic aspects of gastric bypass by transiently blocking nutrient absorption in the duodenum. The company was co-founded in 2022 by MIT's Robert Langer and Giovanni Traverso with CEO Rahul Dhanda. Syntis Bio is a therapeutics developer and publishes no public API, developer program, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Valo Health
providers.description: Valo Health is a Boston-based drug discovery and development company that combines real-world human data, artificial intelligence, advanced causal inference and predictive chemistry to identify and validate therapeutic targets. Its work is organized around two stated capabilities: Human Causal Biology, which applies AI/ML and statistical genetics to large-scale human datasets and validates findings in human tissue, and Closed-Loop Chemistry, which pairs integrated computational modeling with laboratory work to engineer novel small molecules. The company, launched out of Flagship Pioneering and historically associated with its Opal Computational Platform, operates a shared risk-and-reward partnership model with pharmaceutical companies including Novo Nordisk, Merck KGaA, Pfizer and Lundbeck, advancing early-stage R&D while partners lead clinical development. Valo Health is a private biotechnology company that publishes no developer program, no public API and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Editas Medicine
providers.description: Editas Medicine is a clinical-stage genome editing company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing durable, precision CRISPR-based gene editing medicines for people with serious diseases. The company works across in vivo and ex vivo approaches and holds foundational CRISPR/Cas9 and Cas12a intellectual property, advancing a pipeline that has included programs in sickle cell disease, beta-thalassemia and inherited retinal disorders. Editas Medicine trades on Nasdaq under the ticker EDIT and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). As a life-sciences research and therapeutics organization it publishes a corporate and investor-relations web presence rather than a public developer API, so this profile captures its identity, web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Kailera Therapeutics
providers.description: Kailera Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the next generation of obesity and cardiometabolic care through a diversified pipeline of GLP-1 based therapies. Founded in 2024 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, its lead candidate ribupatide (KAI-9531) is a once-weekly injectable GLP-1/GIP receptor dual agonist in a global Phase 3 program, alongside oral small-molecule GLP-1 candidates and tri-agonist programs licensed in part from Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals. Kailera has raised a $400M Series A and a $600M Series B led by Bain Capital, and priced its IPO in April 2026 (NASDAQ: KLRA). This is a corporate/portfolio company profile in the API Evangelist network; Kailera publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Numan
providers.description: Numan (trading as Vir Health Limited) is a UK-based digital healthcare and telemedicine company offering convenient, clinician-led care direct to consumers. Its services span weight-loss programmes (including GLP-1 medications such as Mounjaro and Wegovy), men's health (erectile dysfunction, hair loss, testosterone), women's health (menopause support), at-home blood tests and diagnostics, supplements, and one-off doctor consultations, delivered through its website and iOS/Android app. Numan is regulated by the Care Quality Commission and operates a GPhC-licensed pharmacy. It is a portfolio company of Anthemis. As of this enrichment pass Numan publishes no public developer API, SDKs, MCP server, or partner integration surface.

providers.name: Aer Therapeutics
providers.description: Aer Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in the Research Triangle Park / Raleigh area of North Carolina, developing novel treatments for muco-obstructive lung diseases such as COPD, asthma, cystic fibrosis, and non-CF bronchiectasis. A spinout from Dr. John Fahy's laboratory at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF), the company's lead candidate, AER-01 (fexlamose), is an inhaled small-molecule mucolytic designed to break down and liquefy the dense mucus plugs that obstruct airflow in the lungs. Aer closed a $36 million Series A backed by life-science investors including Canaan, OrbiMed, Hatteras Venture Partners, and Pappas Capital. Aer Therapeutics is a private, research-focused therapeutics company and does not publish a public developer platform, API, or SDKs; this profile captures its corporate identity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aktis Oncology
providers.description: Aktis Oncology is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation precision radiopharmaceuticals for the treatment of cancer. The company has built a proprietary miniprotein radioconjugate platform that pairs tumor-targeting miniproteins with targeted alpha-particle emitters, aiming to reach solid-tumor types that have been difficult to address with existing radiopharmaceutical therapies. Aktis focuses on patient populations with significant unmet medical need, advancing a pipeline of targeted alpha-based therapeutic candidates. The company operates from Boston, Massachusetts, with an additional site in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina. Aktis Oncology was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; it is a biotechnology company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Angitia Biopharmaceuticals
providers.description: Angitia Biopharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2018, headquartered at 3027 Townsgate Road, Westlake Village, California, with research and development operations in Guangzhou, China. It discovers and develops biologic therapeutics for serious musculoskeletal diseases, including osteoporosis, osteogenesis imperfecta, bone metastasis, osteoarthritis and muscle disorders. Its clinical pipeline is led by AGA2118 and AGA2115, bispecific antibodies targeting sclerostin and DKK1, alongside AGA111 in lumbar interbody fusion. The company closed a $120 million Series C financing in December 2024 led by Bain Capital Life Sciences. Angitia is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, developer portal, SDK, machine-readable specification, or technology platform of any kind. Its only machine-readable public surface is an XML sitemap and a robots.txt carrying Cloudflare-managed Content-Signal directives that reserve AI training rights.

providers.name: Attralus
providers.description: Attralus is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Francisco, California, developing transformative medicines for patients with systemic amyloidosis. Its proprietary pan-amyloid removal (PAR) platform pairs a pan-amyloid binding peptide with a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody so the resulting fusion protein binds amyloid deposits across every amyloidosis type and stage and recruits the immune system to clear them. The lead candidate, zamubafusp alfa (AT-02), is a pan-amyloid depleter in a Phase 1/2 open-label extension study and has received U.S. FDA Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of AL amyloidosis; a next-generation PAR program (IV and subcutaneous) and a research-stage neurodegeneration program targeting Abeta, tau and alpha-synuclein aggregates follow behind it. Attralus' molecular imaging agents AT-01 (124-iodine evuzamitide) and AT-05 (99mTc-p5+14) were acquired by Bayer in January 2026. The company was launched in 2020 with a Series A from venBio Partners and has since raised additional rounds including a $56 million financing led by Alpha Wave Ventures with participation from Bristol Myers Squibb. Attralus is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable API contract of any kind (every OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, A2A and /.well-known/ path probed on its hosts returns 404, and no api/developer/docs subdomain resolves).

providers.name: Avalynpharma
providers.description: Avalyn Pharma is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing inhaled therapies for rare and serious respiratory diseases, with a focus on idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and other interstitial lung diseases. Its inhaled-delivery pipeline includes AP01 (inhaled pirfenidone), AP02 (inhaled nintedanib), and AP03 (a fixed-dose combination), aiming to deliver antifibrotic medication directly to lung tissue to improve efficacy while reducing systemic side effects. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, the company is a therapeutics developer and publishes no public API or developer surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: BlossomHill Therapeutics
