providers.description: AbCellera (NASDAQ: ABCL) is a Vancouver-based antibody discovery and development company that integrates biology, computation, and engineering to develop antibody-based medicines. Its technology platform combines high-throughput single-cell antibody screening, GPCR and ion-channel capabilities, bispecifics, antibody-drug conjugates, structure-based design, and AI for sequence and structure analysis. The company operates a hybrid business model with a co-development partner network (40+ partners and 100+ antibody drug programs since 2015) alongside a growing wholly-owned pipeline that includes ABCL635 (non-hormonal vasomotor symptoms), ABCL575 (atopic dermatitis), ABCL688 (autoimmunity), and ABCL386 (oncology), plus 20+ discovery programs. AbCellera does not publish a public API or developer portal; capabilities are delivered through partner collaborations and contract terms.

providers.name: Atomwise
providers.description: Atomwise pioneered the use of deep convolutional neural networks for structure-based drug discovery, with its AtomNet platform applying AI to virtual screening of small molecules against protein targets. The company ran the Artificial Intelligence Molecular Screen (AIMS) academic collaboration program, partnered with biotech and pharma companies on discovery contracts, and built an internal pipeline of small-molecule programs. As of 2026, atomwise.com redirects to Numerion Labs (numerionlabs.ai), reflecting an apparent rebrand or successor entity that positions itself as an AI superplatform exploring drug-like chemical space with programs in immune and inflammatory diseases. Atomwise never exposed a public commercial API; AtomNet screening was delivered to partners as a service. The legacy GitHub organization (github.com/atomwise) hosts no public repositories.

providers.name: Publix Super Markets
providers.description: Publix Super Markets is one of the largest employee-owned supermarket chains in the United States, headquartered in Lakeland, Florida. It operates grocery stores, pharmacies, delivery, catering, and online ordering services across the southeastern United States. Publix is a Fortune 500 company. No public developer APIs or developer portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Abinitio Bio
providers.description: Abinitio Bio builds AI foundation models for biopharmaceutical manufacturing, positioning itself as the intelligence layer for drug manufacturing. Its first model, Echo, predicts manufacturing outcomes to assess manufacturability from day one through process scale-up — evaluating molecules early to reduce aggregation and regulatory liabilities, recommending optimal cell lines, media formulations, and bioprocess parameters, predicting process behavior across scales and operating conditions, and delivering lab-validated candidate molecules, processes, and characterization data ready for commercial scale-up. Founded in 2026 in Boston and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026), MIT's Researcher-to-Entrepreneur Accelerator, and Fifty Years' 5050 Program. The company operates a B2B model with pharmaceutical companies and CDMOs and does not currently publish a public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Astraea
providers.description: Astraea is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) clinical trial automation platform that gives pharmaceutical sponsors, biotechs, and CROs an AI operating system for clinical development. Founded by Joshua Wang and Sanmay Sarada, the platform orchestrates specialized AI agents across the full biometrics lifecycle - standards mapping, data normalization, CDISC mapping, SDTM and ADaM dataset generation, TFLs/TLFs, SAP, eCRFs, Define-XML, QC, and submission documents - turning a protocol and raw study data into FDA-submission-ready output. Astraea is positioned as sponsor-run software rather than a CRO: it runs inside the customer's own secure environment so clinical data never reaches Astraea's servers, with 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and audit-ready, standards-native traceability. The company reports serving 10+ global pharma and biotech sponsors with 30-50% faster reporting cycles.

providers.name: Avistone
providers.description: Beijing Avistone Biotechnology Co., Ltd. is a commercial-stage innovative biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Beijing, China, focused on the research, development, and commercialization of first-in-class and best-in-class oncology therapies. Founded in 2012 (originally Beijing Pearl Biotechnology) and renamed Avistone in 2018, the company has two approved cancer drugs on the market: Vebreltinib (万比锐®), a MET inhibitor approved for non-small cell lung cancer and glioma indications and included in China's National Reimbursement Drug List, and Andamertinib (安比锐®), an EGFR exon 20 insertion inhibitor approved in 2026 for advanced NSCLC. Avistone maintains a pipeline of additional candidates (ANS01 through ANS09) across solid-tumor indications and is backed by IDG Capital. The company publishes no public developer API or programmatic surface; this profile captures its corporate and investor identity.

providers.name: DermBiont
providers.description: DermBiont, Inc. is a Boston, Massachusetts clinical-stage dermatology therapeutics company founded in 2017 that develops targeted topical treatments addressing the root cause of skin disease rather than its symptoms. Its lead program SM-030 is a first-in-class topical PKC-beta inhibitor in development for melasma and other hyperpigmentation disorders of the skin, targeting excess melanin production; earlier programs included SM-020 for seborrheic keratosis and the live-bacterial DBI-001 and DBI-002 candidates for atopic dermatitis, tinea pedis and onychomycosis. The company describes an in-house discovery platform for microbiome-based therapeutics built on terabytes of DNA sequencing data from human skin samples across healthy individuals and patients, paired with a proprietary computational biology platform that identifies functions gained and lost by the skin microbiome. That computational platform is internal research tooling, not a product: DermBiont sells drug candidates and partnering opportunities, publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind, and its website is a Squarespace-hosted corporate site.

providers.name: Elevation Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Elevation Pharmaceuticals was a San Diego specialty pharmaceutical company founded in 2008 by Cam Garner, Bill Gerhart, and Ahmet Tutuncu to develop next-generation aerosol/inhalation therapies for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It raised a $30 million Series A in 2010 backed by Canaan Partners, TPG Growth, Care Capital, and Mesa Verde Venture Partners, and was acquired by Sunovion Pharmaceuticals in August 2012. The company is no longer independently operating; its domain now resolves to Sunovion nameservers and it publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Canaan Partners portfolio record.

providers.name: Fable Therapeutics
providers.description: Fable Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company developing protein-engineered biologics for obesity and metabolic disease. Its lead candidate, FBL-140, is an infrequently dosed monoclonal antibody antagonizing the activin receptor type II (ActR2) pathway to reduce body weight and fat while preserving lean muscle mass and improving cardiometabolic health, with clinical trials expected to begin in early 2027. The company is also advancing a combination therapy pairing ActR2 antagonism with an incretin mimetic. Fable Therapeutics is a deep-tech portfolio company backed by DCVC. It operates as a traditional drug-development company and does not currently publish any public API, developer documentation, or technical platform.

providers.name: Good Manufacturing Practices
providers.description: A system of processes, procedures, and documentation that ensures products are consistently produced and controlled according to quality standards, commonly used in pharmaceutical, food, and medical device manufacturing. Proper implementation reduces legal and operational risk while supporting audit readiness.

providers.name: Maxion Therapeutics
providers.description: Maxion Therapeutics is a UK biotechnology company developing protein therapeutics using its proprietary KnotBody technology, which fuses venom-derived knottin miniproteins with antibodies to drug previously untreatable ion channel- and GPCR-driven diseases across autoimmune, inflammatory, and related therapeutic areas. Maxion is a preclinical-stage drug-discovery company, not an API or developer-platform provider; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-tracking purposes and has no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Novira Therapeutics
providers.description: Novira Therapeutics was a biopharmaceutical company developing direct-acting antivirals for chronic hepatitis B (HBV), notably HBV capsid assembly modulators. It was acquired by Johnson & Johnson (Janssen) in 2015 and no longer operates as an independent entity. Its domain (noviratherapeutics.com) is now run on Johnson & Johnson DNS and mail infrastructure with no public website, developer portal, or API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners; the enrichment pipeline confirms there is no API or developer surface to catalog.

providers.name: Plantner Inc.
providers.description: Plantner Inc. (PLANTNER) is a South Korean biotechnology company specializing in the extraction and manufacturing of alginic acid, a biodegradable marine-derived biomaterial. Operating as a bio-industry platform provider, Plantner supplies alginic acid-based solutions across medical devices (wound dressings, nutraceuticals), pharmaceuticals (gastroprotective agents, drug-delivery systems), cosmetics (modeling masks, hydrogels), advanced biotech (bio-ink, organoids, delivery carriers), and agriculture (controlled-release fertilizers, mulching films, eco-friendly herbicides). Headquartered in Seoul with an R&D center in Suwon, the company is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a materials/biotech manufacturer and does not currently publish a developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: sinocelltech
providers.description: Sinocelltech (Beijing Sino Cell Biotechnology Group Co., Ltd.; Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market code 688520) is a biopharmaceutical research and development company founded in 2002 by Dr. Xie Liangzhi. It develops and commercializes recombinant protein and monoclonal antibody therapeutics across oncology, autoimmune disease, and infectious disease, together with preventive vaccines including a recombinant 14-valent HPV vaccine and COVID-19 vaccines. The company has multiple marketed products in China and a pipeline of clinical-stage candidates. It publishes no public developer platform, API, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Soufflé Therapeutics
providers.description: Soufflé Therapeutics is a genetic medicine company developing nucleic acid (siRNA) therapeutics that use proprietary cell-specific ligand-conjugation technology to target and deliver treatments to specific cell types. Its initial programs address muscle and heart disorders, with first therapies targeting Facioscapulohumeral Muscular Dystrophy (FSHD) and genetically-driven cardiomyopathies, with clinical trials expected to begin in 2026. The company is headquartered in Watertown, Massachusetts and was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners. It is a therapeutics/pharmaceutical company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: McKesson
providers.description: McKesson is a Fortune 500 healthcare company providing wholesale medical supplies and equipment, pharmaceutical distribution, and healthcare technology solutions. No public developer APIs are currently documented.

providers.name: 858 Therapeutics
providers.description: 858 Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in San Diego, California, developing first-in-class and best-in-class small-molecule therapies that target tumor dependencies in DNA damage response (DDR) pathways. Its lead program, ETX-19477, is an oral, potent, and selective PARG (poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase) inhibitor being evaluated in a Phase 1/2 study for patients with advanced solid tumors, exploiting cancer-cell vulnerabilities tied to replication stress and defects in replication-fork protection. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a clinical-stage therapeutics company it publishes a corporate and scientific web presence but no public developer, API, or documentation surface, so API artifacts are not applicable.

providers.name: Aculys
providers.description: Aculys Pharma, Inc. is a Japanese clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on neurological and psychiatric diseases where there is high unmet medical need. The company works to eliminate Japan's drug lag and drug loss by bringing innovative medicines already approved in Western markets to Japanese patients as early as possible. Its lead product is Spydia (diazepam nasal spray), Japan's first domestically developed intranasal anti-seizure agent, approved in June 2025 and administrable outside medical facilities. Originally funded by SoftBank Vision Fund (Series C, March 2025), Aculys was acquired by and became part of the Viatris Group in October 2025. Aculys publishes no public developer program, API, or technical documentation surface; this profile is maintained for network completeness and identity.

providers.name: Arrakis
providers.description: Arrakis Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company pioneering RNA-targeted small molecules (rSMs) as a new class of genetic medicines. Its rSM platform enables orally available small molecules to bind RNA and modulate previously undruggable biological pathways, with an industrialized discovery toolkit spanning multiple modalities. The lead proprietary program targets Type 1 Myotonic Dystrophy (DM1) at the root cause of the disease, alongside a pipeline of proprietary and partnered programs. A GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company in the life-sciences sector, Arrakis was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes a corporate and scientific website but no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Athos Therapeutics
providers.description: Athos Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Torrance, California developing precision small-molecule therapeutics for autoimmune and chronic inflammatory diseases, led by co-founder and CEO Dr. Dimitrios Iliopoulos. Its AI/ML discovery platform integrates multi-omic patient data — genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, epigenomics, metabolomics and microbiomics — collected with global hospital systems to identify novel drug and gene targets, and produced ATH-063, an AI-generated G9A methyltransferase inhibitor advancing in inflammatory bowel disease. The computational side of the business is commercialized through Chiron AI Labs (formerly AthosOmics.AI), a deliberately no-code omics analysis SaaS suite (Athos-Multi, Athos-T, Athos-P, Athos-G, Athos-PM) that is pre-launch and gated behind a demo waitlist. Athos publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: InventisBio
providers.description: InventisBio Co., Ltd. (Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market: 688382) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in the Pudong New Area of Shanghai, China, with operations in New Jersey, United States. Built on independent R&D capabilities, InventisBio discovers and develops innovative small-molecule and targeted therapies for oncology, autoimmune, and metabolic diseases to address unmet medical needs. The company has advanced multiple drug candidates into clinical trials, including late-stage Phase III programs in non-small cell lung cancer and breast cancer, alongside earlier-stage assets targeting KRAS G12C, synthetic-lethal pathways, hyperuricemia/gout, and plaque psoriasis. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. InventisBio is a research-driven pharmaceutical company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Mevo
providers.description: Mevo is a Brazilian healthtech company whose stated mission is to "descomplicar a saúde" (simplify healthcare) through a digital platform that connects doctors, patients, and pharmacies. Its products include Mevo Receita Digital (electronic/digital medical prescriptions replacing paper scripts), and Mevo Farma / Mevo Dispensação (online medication purchase, dispensing, and partner-pharmacy fulfillment with delivery). Mevo sells to hospitals, health operators, clinics, and telemedicine platforms as a B2B partner. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation portal is currently published; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and Prosus Ventures.

providers.name: Nectero Therapeutics
providers.description: Nectero Therapeutics (also operating as Nectero Medical) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing a novel, minimally invasive treatment to stabilize growth and prevent rupture of mid-sized abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA). Its lead investigational therapy is delivered as a single endovascular procedure intended to remodel and strengthen the aneurysm wall, offering an alternative to watchful waiting or open surgical repair. The company is backed by Norwest Venture Partners and other life-sciences investors, and maintains a corporate marketing and news presence. It does not publish a developer program, public API, SDKs, or any machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Orchestra
providers.description: Orchestra is an agentic operations platform for drug development and life sciences R&D organizations. The software helps biotech and pharmaceutical teams unify planning, automate operations, and reduce the risks that derail breakthrough science by creating centralized roadmaps across leadership, programs, and scientific groups, applying AI agents to operational automation, and delivering data-driven decision support across scenarios, planning, and CRO management. Orchestra is a portfolio company of 8vc and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a marketing and product site only and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Organon
providers.description: Organon & Co. is a Fortune 500 global healthcare company focused on improving the health of women throughout their lives. Spun off from Merck in 2021, Organon's portfolio spans women's health, biosimilars, and established medicines across more than 140 markets worldwide. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Organon. No public developer APIs or documentation portal have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Rubedo Life Sciences
providers.description: Rubedo Life Sciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company discovering and developing precision medicines that target the biological drivers of aging and age-related diseases. Its proprietary ALEMBIC drug-discovery platform identifies and validates senescent ("zombie") cells that accumulate with age and drive chronic disease, enabling the design of selective senolytic therapeutics. The company's lead candidate, RLS-1496, is a first-in-class selective GPX4 modulator that has produced positive Phase 1 dermatology results (plaque psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, skin aging) and Phase 1b/2a data in actinic keratosis. Rubedo is backed by Khosla Ventures and operates as a therapeutics company rather than a software/API provider — this profile carries no developer or API surface.

providers.name: SonoThera
providers.description: SonoThera, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered at 201 Haskins Way in South San Francisco, California, founded in 2022 to make genetic medicine deliverable without a viral vector. Its RIPPLE platform pairs an intravenously administered lipid-and-microbubble formulation with an externally applied diagnostic ultrasound probe: the acoustic energy transiently permeabilizes cell membranes in the targeted organ so a nucleic-acid payload enters only where the probe is pointed, an approach built on the roughly 35 million ultrasound contrast-agent doses given safely each year in cardiac imaging. A companion payload engineering platform, PORE, carries DNA and RNA constructs, gene editing and gene silencing cargo of varied size and format. The company holds an exclusive license to GE HealthCare's Optison and Sonazoid microbubble products for use with the platform, and has raised approximately $186 million — a $60.75 million Series A and an oversubscribed $125 million Series B — from ARCH Venture Partners, Johnson & Johnson, Illumina Ventures and Eli Lilly, to push lead programs in Duchenne muscular dystrophy and autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease into the clinic, with preclinical work in Alport syndrome and hemophilia A. It was co-founded by Kenneth Greenberg (CEO), Steve Feinstein (Chief Scientific Officer) and Michael H. Davidson (Executive Chairman). SonoThera sells therapeutics, not software: it runs no developer program, publishes no API, SDK or machine-readable specification, and maintains no public source-code organization.

providers.name: Tessera Therapeutics
providers.description: Tessera Therapeutics is an early-stage life sciences company, founded and backed by Flagship Pioneering, pioneering Gene Writing — a new category of genetic medicine designed to write therapeutic messages into the genome to treat and potentially cure disease at its source. Its Gene Writing platform uses mobile genetic elements delivered via lipid nanoparticles to insert genes and exons, make small insertions and deletions, or change single or multiple DNA base pairs, with applications spanning sickle cell disease, in vivo CAR-T, HIV, and other monogenic, metabolic, autoimmune, and neurodegenerative diseases. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a health-tech portfolio lead; Tessera is a therapeutics developer and does not currently publish a public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Aumet
providers.description: Aumet is a MENA-based healthtech company building an AI-first procurement and pharmacy operating system for healthcare. Its platform connects pharmaceutical manufacturers, distributors, and pharmacies through a B2B marketplace and a suite of pharmacy software: Pulse (point-of-sale, inventory, and smart reordering for individual pharmacies), Chain (multi-branch pharmacy management), and Enterprise (solutions for government health systems and hospitals). The platform adds AI-powered demand forecasting, procurement automation, price transparency, and analytics, and reports serving 12,000+ pharmacies and 1,000+ suppliers across Jordan, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia with over $1B in gross merchandise value and millions of transactions annually. Aumet is backed by 500 Global and Techstars.

providers.name: Alpha Biopharma
providers.description: Alpha Biopharma is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Shanghai, China, with an additional office in Beijing. The company focuses on the clinical development and commercialization of global innovative drugs across oncology and immunotherapy, spanning medical affairs, clinical operations, regulatory affairs and commercialization. Its lead product is Zorifertinib (formerly AZD-3759, marketed as Zorifer), a next-generation EGFR TKI designed for EGFR mutation positive advanced NSCLC patients with central nervous system metastases, which received NMPA approval in November 2024 as the first EGFR-TKI indicated for lung cancer with brain metastases. Alpha Biopharma also partners with Wugen Inc. on universal off-the-shelf memory NK and CAR-T cell therapies. The company raised a Series A led by Qiming Venture Partners. Alpha Biopharma publishes a corporate marketing website only and operates no public API, developer portal, or software platform.

providers.name: Ankyra Therapeutics
providers.description: Ankyra Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing "anchored" immunotherapies for cancer and immune-mediated diseases. Its proprietary platform tethers immune-modulating drugs to aluminum hydroxide so that treatment concentrates locally at the disease site, broadening the therapeutic window while reducing systemic toxicity and dosing frequency. The lead candidate, ANK-101, is an anchored IL-12 therapy in clinical evaluation for patients with advanced solid tumors. Ankyra is backed by investors including Google Ventures (GV), Mithril, Polaris Partners, Sands Capital, and Fidelity. The company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical platform; this profile exists in the API Evangelist network for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Atropos Health
providers.description: Atropos Health is a Stanford-spinout, New York / Bay Area real-world evidence (RWE) company founded in 2020 by Nigam Shah, Brigham Hyde, and Saurabh Gombar to close the medical "evidence gap" by converting routine healthcare data into publication-grade observational studies in minutes instead of months. Its flagship platform GENEVA OS (Generative Evidence Acceleration Operating System) is a federated, cloud-agnostic operating system that installs behind the customer's firewall, ingests longitudinal patient records as in-memory patient-timeline objects, and exposes a Temporal Query Language (TQL) and Advanced Cohort Engine (ACE) for rapid observational analyses without moving PHI. On top of GENEVA OS, Atropos offers ChatRWD, a conversational chat-to-database application that generates full observational studies from natural-language clinical questions, the Atropos Evidence Agent (an agentic AI deployed at Stanford Health Care and developed in collaboration with Microsoft to surface RWE directly inside clinical workflows and notes), Green Button (the original on-demand consult-style evidence service that gave rise to the company), Forge (study automation), and Alexandria, marketed as the world's largest body of precision evidence-based findings with 33M+ entries used for clinical decision support and LLM training. The company sells into health systems (pharmacy, research informatics, value-based care, GME) and life sciences (brand planning, HEOR, medical affairs, R&D, commercial analytics, precision-medicine AI/ML), is backed by Valtruis, Emerson Collective, Breyer Capital, McKinsey Ventures, Cencora Ventures, Presidio Ventures, Merck Global Health Innovation, Samsung Next, and others, and partners with Stanford Health Care, Mayo Clinic Platform, and Microsoft. Atropos has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release; GENEVA OS, TQL, ACE, ChatRWD, and the Evidence Agent are proprietary enterprise software delivered under contract to health-system and life-sciences customers, and the company's public GitHub org contains only forks (FAISS, HELM, security-policy-templates, terraform-aws-github-runner) and a small number of internal research notebooks rather than any shippable client library.

providers.name: BioTheryX
providers.description: BioTheryX is a private, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, discovering and developing first-in-class targeted protein degraders — both bifunctional degraders and molecular glues — for cancer and inflammatory disease. Its proprietary PRODEGY platform is built on Cereblon-binding expertise carried over from founders who worked on FDA-approved Cereblon modulators. The lead program BTX-9341, a dual CDK4/CDK6 degrader, is in Phase 1 for HR+/HER2- breast cancer, alongside BTX-10908 targeting SOS1 for pan-KRAS mutant cancers and PDE4 degraders for inflammatory conditions; the company also partners with Incyte on molecular glue degrader discovery. BioTheryX is a therapeutics developer with no public developer program: probes on 2026-08-02 returned 404 for /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs, /llms.txt and every /.well-known/ discovery path on biotheryx.com, and there is no api./developer./docs./portal. subdomain, GitHub organization, or published SDK.

providers.name: CytomX Therapeutics
providers.description: CytomX Therapeutics is a clinical-stage, oncology-focused biopharmaceutical company based in South San Francisco, California, pioneering a novel class of masked, conditionally activated biologic therapeutics built on its proprietary Probody platform. The Probody technology is engineered to remain inactive in healthy tissue and to become selectively unmasked and activated within the tumor microenvironment, with the goal of producing more potent, less toxic cancer medicines. The company's pipeline spans antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), T-cell engaging bispecific antibodies, and immunotherapies, advanced both internally and through partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies. CytomX is a publicly traded company (Nasdaq CTMX). This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners; as a biopharmaceutical research organization CytomX does not publish a public developer API, so this profile carries company identity and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: BociMed
providers.description: Shanghai BociMed Pharmaceutical Research Co., Ltd. (上海博志研新药物研究有限公司) is a Chinese pharmaceutical CRO/CDMO founded in 2012 in the Zhangjiang Pharmaceutical Valley, Shanghai, with an R&D headquarters in Zhangjiang, a production base in Lingang, and a clinical subsidiary in Chengdu. BociMed offers small-molecule chemistry, CMC and process development, a portfolio of drug delivery technology platforms (oral, injectable, nasal, pulmonary, transdermal, ocular, implant, liposome and exosome), clinical research and SMO services, global regulatory registration consulting, and commercial API, intermediate and solid-dosage manufacturing. It is a laboratory and manufacturing services business rather than a software vendor: it publishes a marketing website in Chinese and English and no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Hummingbird Bioscience
providers.description: Hummingbird Bioscience is a clinical-stage precision biotherapeutics company headquartered at The Galen, Singapore Science Park, with US operations, discovering and developing antibody-based medicines — including next-generation antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) — for hard-to-treat cancers and autoimmune disease. Its Rational Antibody Discovery (RAD) platform pairs computational target and epitope modelling with proprietary immunization strategies and Abvantage mice, and is combined with in-house linker-payload chemistry to engineer epitope-specific, high-affinity antibodies. Clinical programs include HMBD-001 (anti-HER3 monoclonal antibody) and HMBD-501 (HER3-targeted ADC, first patient dosed January 2026); HMBD-002 (anti-VISTA) was licensed to Percheron Therapeutics in 2025 and further antibodies were licensed to Immunome. The company sells drug programs and partnerships, not software: it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Auransa
providers.description: Auransa Inc. is a clinical-stage, AI-native biopharmaceutical company based in Palo Alto, California, founded in 2014 by Pek Lum. Auransa uses its proprietary SMarTR Engine — a hypothesis-free machine learning platform that mines human disease data such as RNA transcriptome and gene-expression profiles — to discover novel small-molecule therapeutics without starting from a predefined drug target. The company has analyzed more than 500,000 gene-expression profiles across roughly 70 diseases to identify molecular disease subtypes and match them to candidate compounds. Its lead program, AU-409, is a first-in-human Phase 1 candidate for liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma), with additional pipeline work in heart-safe chemotherapy and other oncology indications. Auransa is a DCVC / DCVC Bio portfolio company, also backed by Lux Capital, 11.2 Capital, and Harmonix Fund. Auransa is a private drug-discovery company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its identity and web presence in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: MAYD
providers.description: MAYD (Meds At Your Doorstep) is a Berlin-based on-demand medication delivery service building a digital healthcare platform for Europe. Founded in 2021 by Hanno Heintzenberg and Lukas Pieczonka (previously McMakler), MAYD partners with local pharmacies to deliver over-the-counter and prescription medications to consumers' doors in about 30 minutes, 365 days a year, across German cities including Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Frankfurt, Cologne and Düsseldorf. The company operates a consumer mobile app and website (getmayd.com) and raised a ~EUR 30M Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners in January 2022, with participation from Target Global, 468 Capital and Earlybird Venture Capital. MAYD is a consumer-facing (B2C) delivery business and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or partner API surface; it is a Stripe payments customer for its checkout and billing.

providers.name: Ndata
providers.description: nData (ndata.cz) is a European pharmaceutical software company operating since 2005 that builds GxP-compliant, AI-assisted systems for the pharma lifecycle: portfolio and project management (ePM), regulatory affairs (eRA), quality control planning (eQCP), artwork and packaging management (eAW), controlled documentation (eDOCS), clinical trial documentation / eTMF, plus eLAB (R&D lab operations), and eGO and eTRANSFER (launching Q3/2026). Its public web presence is a marketing and product-catalog site; nData publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specifications. Note: this repo was seeded as a bain-capital-ventures ai-infrastructure portfolio stub, but the ndata.cz surface is a pharmaceutical GxP software vendor — the portfolio match appears to be a mismatch.

providers.name: Panacea
providers.description: Panacea is an AI-native FDA regulatory services firm (Y Combinator Spring 2026, operating as withpanacea.com) that pairs experienced ex-FDA regulatory consultants with a proprietary AI platform to accelerate medical device and pharmaceutical companies through FDA approval. Panacea supports the full range of U.S. regulatory pathways - 510(k), De Novo, PMA, IDE, IND, NDA, BLA, ODD, Pre-Subs, and BDD - handling regulatory strategy, pre-FDA meetings, and submission authoring through to clearance and approval. The company differentiates on milestone-based, outcome-aligned pricing rather than hourly billing, claiming results roughly 60% faster than traditional firms while keeping 100% expert oversight. Panacea is a professional services / consulting company; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Alexion Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Alexion Pharmaceuticals was a global biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, focused on developing life-transforming therapies for rare diseases. Founded in 1992, the company pioneered complement inhibition therapy and developed leading treatments for rare hematological and neurological conditions including Soliris (eculizumab) and Ultomiris (ravulizumab). AstraZeneca acquired Alexion in July 2021 for $39 billion, and the company now operates as Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease. The combined entity maintains research programs in complement biology, hematology, nephrology, neurology, metabolic disorders, cardiology, and ophthalmology. Alexion's GitHub organization (alxndgb) hosts research tools including genomic data analysis platforms, precision medicine knowledge graphs, and rare disease target discovery systems.

providers.name: Relay Therapeutics
providers.description: Relay Therapeutics is a clinical-stage precision-medicine company in Cambridge, Massachusetts that discovers and develops small-molecule therapeutics for cancer and genetic disease. Its proprietary Dynamo platform combines computational and experimental approaches — motion-based drug discovery, protein-motion simulation, structural biology, and biophysics — to drug targets that have historically been difficult to reach. The company advances a pipeline of oncology and precision-medicine candidates. Relay Therapeutics was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network. As a biotechnology / drug-discovery company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; this profile captures its corporate identity and web properties.

providers.name: ABM Therapeutics
providers.description: ABM Therapeutics (ABM) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2015, operating from San Diego, California and Zhangjiang, Pudong, Shanghai. It discovers and develops small-molecule targeted therapies for primary brain cancers including glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) and for brain metastases arising from melanoma, lung cancer and breast cancer. Its lead program, ABM-1310, is a brain-penetrant, selective BRAF V600 inhibitor that received US IND clearance in November 2019 and is in Phase 1 clinical study. ABM publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification; its only public surface is a corporate, investor and clinical-news website. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist harvest backlog from a secondary-market listing under the ticker-style slug "abmtx".

providers.name: AbTis
providers.description: AbTis Co., Ltd. (앱티스) is a South Korean biotechnology company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Yongin-si, Gyeonggi-do, inside the Dong-A Socio Holdings R&D Center. It develops AbClick, a third-generation site-selective antibody conjugation platform that attaches payloads to the Fc Lys248 residue of native IgG antibodies with no enzyme and no Fc engineering, giving a controlled drug-to-antibody ratio and batch-to-batch consistency across ADC, DAC, AOC, ARC, ISAC and dual-payload designs. AbTis licenses the platform, runs collaborative research and fee-for-service ADC development, and advances its own pipeline led by AT-211, a Claudin 18.2-targeting MMAE ADC. Acquired by Dong-A ST in 2023, it now operates as that company's ADC-specialised subsidiary. Its product is licensed chemistry and drug intellectual property, not software: it runs no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Acelot, Inc.
providers.description: Acelot, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in South San Francisco, California, developing first-in-class small-molecule therapies for neurodegenerative diseases with high unmet need. Its lead candidate, ACE-2223, is designed to target misfolded and aggregated TDP-43 and restore the protein's healthy form and function, addressing pathology central to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD). Acelot's discovery work is powered by Resolute, an internal integrated drug-discovery platform combining AI-driven computational chemistry with structural and biological insight to drug historically intractable protein targets. Acelot publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification; its four public GitHub repositories are forks of third-party cheminformatics tooling.

providers.name: Allorion Therapeutics
providers.description: Allorion Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2020 by Qiang Ding and Fang Li, developing novel small-molecule therapies for cancer and autoimmune disease. Operating from Natick, Massachusetts and Guangzhou, China, Allorion applies mutant-selective and isoform-specific medicinal chemistry across a pipeline that includes ARTS-011 (a TYK2 inhibitor), ARTS-021 (a CDK2 inhibitor targeting CCNE1-amplified tumors), and ARTS-023/AVZO-023 partnered with Avenzo Therapeutics, alongside an exclusive option and global license agreement with AstraZeneca for an allosteric EGFR L858R inhibitor. The company is a drug-discovery organization backed by Qiming Venture Partners and INCE Capital; it markets internal data and high-throughput screening platforms but publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Arzeda
providers.description: Arzeda Corp is a Seattle, Washington protein design company — "The Protein Design Company" — founded in 2008 by David Baker (2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry), Alexandre Zanghellini and colleagues out of the University of Washington Institute for Protein Design. Its Intelligent Protein Design Technology combines physics-based computational protein design, generative AI and an agentic design-build-test-learn loop over fifteen years of proprietary in-house experimental data to create designer enzymes and proteins that do not exist in nature, then scale them to commercial production. Commercial programs span food and beverage (ViaLeaf Reb M / ProSweet Reb M stevia sweeteners with MANE), home and personal care enzymes (Unilever), advanced materials (W. L. Gore & Associates) and pharmaceutical biologics (Takeda), alongside DARPA and NSF funded work on AI-driven protein design and cell-free biomanufacturing. Arzeda co-founded the OpenFold consortium for open-source protein structure prediction. It sells designed molecules and joint development programs, not software, and publishes no public developer program, API or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: AusperBio
providers.description: AusperBio — AusperBio Therapeutics, Inc. in the United States and Ausper Biopharma Co., Ltd. (杭州浩博医药有限公司) in Hangzhou, China — is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2019 that develops oligonucleotide and targeted delivery technologies, with an initial focus on achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B infection. Its proprietary Med-Oligo antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) platform pairs novel ASO design and optimization with targeted delivery conjugation chemistry, and its Au-HALO hepatocyte-targeting delivery technology extends the same modular approach to siRNA. The lead candidate AHB-137 is an unconjugated ASO that completed enrollment in two Phase II trials and received China CDE clearance to enter Phase III; a second clinical candidate, AHB-171, is a hepatocyte-targeted siRNA. The company has raised more than $200M across Series B, B+ and B2 rounds from investors including Qiming Venture Partners, HanKang Capital, CDH Investments, Sherpa Capital, YuanBio Venture Capital and Genesis Capital. AusperBio sells therapeutics, not software: it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract. Its only machine-readable surface is the private Spring Boot CMS backend that renders ausperbio.com, whose springdoc API description is correctly locked behind authentication.

providers.name: Chiral Quest
providers.description: Chiral Quest (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. (凯瑞斯德生化（苏州）有限公司) is a Chinese pharmaceutical CDMO specializing in chiral chemistry. The company operates asymmetric catalytic hydrogenation, enzyme-catalyzed biosynthesis, flow chemistry, and process innovation technology platforms, using proprietary catalysts to develop and manufacture chiral drug molecules, key raw materials, regulatory starting materials (RSMs), and advanced GMP intermediates for global pharmaceutical companies. Founded around its asymmetric hydrogenation catalyst technology, Chiral Quest merged with Jiangxi Longlai in 2012 and with Suzhou Pengxu in 2020; the group employs more than 800 people including a research team of roughly 150. Suzhou is the parent company and R&D center, Jiangxi Longlai is the manufacturing base, and the company maintains offices in the United Kingdom and the United States. Chiral Quest is a brochure-site company with no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable data surface.

providers.name: Cirius Therapeutics
providers.description: Cirius Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held clinical-stage pharmaceutical company based in Grand Rapids, Michigan, developing oral therapies for chronic metabolic diseases driven by insulin resistance, including Type 2 Diabetes, Type 1 Diabetes, obesity and gestational diabetes. Its lead candidate, azemiglitazone (CIR-0602K / MSDC-0602K), is a next-generation insulin sensitizer that inhibits the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC) to re-balance mitochondrial metabolism, improve glycemic control, preserve lean muscle mass and shift visceral fat to subcutaneous and brown adipose tissue, including in combination with GLP-1 receptor agonists such as tirzepatide. The company publishes a corporate marketing website only; it operates no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Insilico Medicine
providers.description: Insilico Medicine is a clinical-stage biotechnology company applying generative AI and robotic automation to drug discovery and development. Its Pharma.AI software suite includes PandaOmics (target discovery from multi-omics data), Chemistry42 (generative chemistry with retrosynthesis, property prediction, and ADMET), Generative Biologics, inClinico (clinical trial outcome prediction), Science42 DORA (research assistant), Nach01, and PreciousGPT-family models for life sciences. The company runs its own therapeutic pipeline spanning oncology, fibrosis, and inflammation, with programs targeting TNIK, USP1, QPCTL, PHD, MAT2A, TEAD, ENPP1, KAT6 and others through Phase II. Insilico monetizes through Pharma.AI software licensing, partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies, and progression of its in-house assets. Pharma.AI tools are commercial SaaS products accessed via web UI; the company publishes open-source research code on GitHub (GENTRL, fcd_torch, BiAAE, DD-VAE, DORA) but does not expose a public commercial API.

providers.name: Isomorphic Labs
providers.description: Isomorphic Labs is a London-based AI-first drug discovery company spun out of Google DeepMind in 2021 and operating as an Alphabet subsidiary. Founded and led by Sir Demis Hassabis, the company applies frontier AI — including derivatives of the Nobel-winning AlphaFold system and its proprietary Unified Drug Design Engine — to accelerate the design of small-molecule and biologic therapeutics across oncology, immunology, and other therapeutic areas. The Drug Design Engine is positioned as a target- and disease-agnostic, multi-modality platform that combines predictive and generative models with a curated proprietary life-science "Dataverse" and large-scale GPU infrastructure. Isomorphic Labs monetises through strategic pharmaceutical research collaborations — disclosed deals include Novartis (January 2024, expanded February 2025), Eli Lilly, and Johnson & Johnson (January 2026) — and through its own internal therapeutic pipeline. The company closed a $600M external Series B investment round in March 2025. Isomorphic Labs does not operate a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release of its Drug Design Engine; external researcher access to AlphaFold-family models is provided separately by Google DeepMind via the free AlphaFold Server (alphafoldserver.com) for non-commercial use, and via the open-source AlphaFold 3 inference code released by DeepMind. The Isomorphic Labs GitHub organisation hosts only a small number of forks of internal Kubernetes and configuration-management tooling.

providers.name: MWI Veterinary Supply
providers.description: MWI Veterinary Supply, a subsidiary of AmerisourceBergen, is a leading distributor of animal health products to veterinarians across the United States and the United Kingdom, providing pharmaceuticals, vaccines, supplies, diagnostics, and practice management software to veterinary practices.

providers.name: OrsoBio
providers.description: OrsoBio is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2021 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, developing first-in-class oral therapies that restore energy homeostasis in patients living with severe metabolic disorders — obesity, type 2 diabetes, severe dyslipidemias, lipodystrophies and MASH. The name is drawn from the metabolic adaptability of bears ("orso" in Italian). Its pipeline is led by three mitochondrial protonophores — TLC-6740, TLC-1180 and TLC-1235 — intended to increase energy expenditure and improve metabolic and cardiovascular health, alongside an LXR inverse agonist (TLC-2716) for severe hypertriglyceridemia and MASH, an ACC2 inhibitor (TLC-3595) for insulin sensitivity in type 2 diabetes, and an ACMSD inhibitor to augment NAD+ biosynthesis in metabolic and inflammatory liver and kidney disorders. The company closed an oversubscribed $67 million Series B in September 2024, co-led by Ascenta Capital and Woodline Partners with participation from Samsara BioCapital, Enavate Sciences and Longitude Capital. OrsoBio publishes a corporate site covering its science, pipeline, team, board, publications, events and press releases, but runs no developer program: no API documentation, no SDKs, no developer portal, no GitHub organisation and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. The only machine-readable surface on orsobio.com is the site's own WordPress CMS route index, which the site's robots.txt explicitly disallows at /wp-json/ and which is therefore not harvested or catalogued here.

providers.name: Qnovia
providers.description: Qnovia, Inc. is a clinical-stage pharmaceutical and drug-device company developing inhaled therapeutics built on its proprietary RespiRx aseptically pre-filled, portable vibrating-mesh nebulizer platform. Its lead asset, the RespiRx Nicotine Inhaler (QN-01), is a prescription smoking-cessation therapy that cleared FDA IND review and has dosed patients in a U.S. Phase 1 study; a cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) program is advancing toward a second IND. The device is Bluetooth Low Energy connected and pairs with Neblit AI, a cloud-connected companion app and machine-learning platform that tracks dose events and delivers behavioral interventions, which the company positions as a digital therapeutic layer over the pharmacotherapy. Founded in 2018 as Respira Technologies and rebranded to Qnovia in 2022, the company is led by founder and CEO Mario Danek, operates R&D and manufacturing in Newport Beach/Irvine, California and an R&D facility in Richmond, Virginia, and has raised roughly $50 million to date. Qnovia publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable contract; its corporate site is a client-rendered single-page application whose only HTTP API is a private backend serving its own contact, careers and investor-portal forms.

providers.name: Asymchem
providers.description: Asymchem (Asymchem Laboratories (Tianjin) Co., Ltd.) is a global contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) with more than 25 years of experience delivering integrated, cGMP-compliant services across the pharmaceutical value chain. Its single-source model spans route scouting, process research and development, scale-up, and commercial manufacturing for small molecules, peptides, oligonucleotides, chemical macromolecules, biologics, and synthetic biology, and is known for green chemistry and continuous flow chemistry. Headquartered in Morrisville, North Carolina with major R&D and manufacturing operations in China, the U.S., and the U.K., Asymchem employs roughly 9,000 people and is publicly listed (002821.SZ / 6821.HK). Surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network. Note: "API" in Asymchem's context refers to Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient manufacturing, not a public web/developer API — the company publishes no developer API surface.

providers.name: Nouscom
providers.description: Nouscom AG is a private, clinical-stage immuno-oncology company developing next-generation neoantigen-targeted cancer immunotherapies, founded in 2015 by Riccardo Cortese and Alfredo Nicosia, with headquarters in Basel, Switzerland and research and manufacturing operations in Rome, Italy. Its proprietary viral vector platform — great ape adenovirus and MVA vectors able to encode large neoantigen payloads together with other immunomodulators — is used to build both off-the-shelf and personalized cancer vaccines. The lead program, NOUS-209, targets 209 shared frameshift neoantigens for cancer interception in Lynch Syndrome carriers and for the treatment of dMMR/MSI metastatic colorectal cancer in combination with pembrolizumab; its second clinical program, NOUS-PEV, is a personalized immunotherapy for advanced solid tumors. Nouscom raised an oversubscribed EUR 67.5 million Series C in November 2023, co-led by Andera Partners, Bpifrance (InnoBio 2) and M Ventures. Nouscom is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable API contract, and is profiled here as an identity-only record.

providers.name: Accutar Biotechnology
providers.description: Accutar Biotechnology Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Cranbury, New Jersey, founded in 2015 and previously based in Brooklyn, New York, with operations in Shanghai. It applies deep learning to small-molecule drug discovery and runs its own oncology pipeline, including the AC0682 and AC0176 protein degraders in Phase 1 trials. Its computational platform is a set of in-house AI products used in its own preclinical workflow and offered to partners: ChemiRise (retrosynthesis), Orbital (neural-network docking), Virtual Screen, Intelligent-SAR, Chemi-Net (ADME prediction) and the PatentOne AI suite (InsightOne, GenusOne). Accutar publishes no developer program: no public API, developer portal, reference documentation, machine-readable specification or SDK exists on any host it operates. Access to the AI products is arranged by email enquiry for a trial or demo.

providers.name: Akston Biosciences
providers.description: Akston Biosciences Corporation is a privately held biotechnology company headquartered in Beverly, Massachusetts, founded in 2011 by the team from SmartCells, Inc. and led by CEO Todd Zion, Ph.D. Akston designs, develops and manufactures protein therapeutics built on its proprietary Ambifect Fc-fusion protein platform, with a pipeline focused on companion-animal (veterinary) medicine: PD-L1 monoclonal antibody oncology candidates (AKS-701d, AKS-619d), a long-acting GLP-1 for feline weight management (AKS-562c), an IL-31 targeting therapy for canine pruritus (AKS-699), and NGF-targeting candidates for osteoarthritis pain. Its veterinary insulin program was sold to Dechra in 2024, and human programs continue through the Vakston and Diamune Therapeutics subsidiaries. The company announced a manufacturing expansion in Shreveport, Louisiana. Akston is a therapeutics developer and manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes a corporate marketing site and no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Alume Biosciences
providers.description: Alume Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company in La Jolla, California, developing nerve-targeted fluorescent agents for precision surgery. Its lead candidate, bevonescein (ALM-488) — a peptide-dye conjugate co-invented by the late Nobel Laureate Dr. Roger Tsien and surgeon Dr. Quyen Nguyen — is administered intravenously roughly an hour before an operation so surgeons can see nerves illuminated in the surgical field and avoid inadvertent nerve injury. The compound has FDA Fast Track designation, is in Phase 3 pivotal trials in head-and-neck surgery, and the company has stated it plans a New Drug Application submission in 2026. Alume is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Antiva Biosciences
providers.description: Antiva Biosciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing topical therapeutics that target oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) infections and the precancerous cervical lesions they cause, aiming to stop cervical cancer before it starts with at-home, non-surgical treatment. Its lead candidate, ABI-2280, is a topical antiviral in Phase 1b/2 clinical development for high-risk cervical HPV infection, and the company frames its work in support of the World Health Organization's global Cervical Cancer Elimination Initiative. Antiva is backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners and GV, and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile awaiting further enrichment.

providers.name: Ark Biopharmaceutical
providers.description: Ark Biopharmaceutical (爱科百发, Ark Biosciences) is a Shanghai-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery and development of innovative therapies for respiratory diseases and pediatric conditions. Its pipeline includes AK0529 (ziresovir) for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, AK0901 for ADHD, AK3280 for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, AK0610 for RSV prevention, and AK0705 for COPD. The company is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As a drug-development company it publishes a corporate website, R&D pipeline, and news center, but exposes no public developer platform, API, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Covance (Fortrea)
providers.description: Covance was a contract research organization (CRO) acquired by Labcorp in 2015 and rebranded as Labcorp Drug Development in 2021. In 2023, the clinical development business was spun off as Fortrea, an independent CRO headquartered in Durham, North Carolina, operating in 90+ countries and serving the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device industries with clinical trial management, central laboratory, and bioanalytical services. No public API or developer portal is currently published; integrations are arranged through sponsor and partner agreements.

providers.name: Cullgen
providers.description: Cullgen Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 2018 and focused on first-in-class targeted protein degradation medicines. Its proprietary uSMITE (ubiquitin-mediated, small molecule-induced target elimination) platform harnesses the body's own ubiquitin-proteasome system to selectively degrade disease-causing intracellular proteins, including targets considered undruggable by conventional small molecules, and the company extends that chemistry into degrader-antibody conjugates (DACs). Its lead TRK degrader program has entered Phase 1 clinical dosing, and the company has partnered with Astellas and taken investment from AstraZeneca. Gyre Therapeutics completed an all-stock acquisition of Cullgen valued at approximately $300 million on 4 May 2026. Cullgen publishes a corporate marketing website only: profiling on 2026-08-04 found no developer portal, documentation, machine-readable API contract, package registry presence, or public code repositories.

providers.name: Dizal Pharma
providers.description: Dizal Pharma (Dizal (Jiangsu) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering and developing novel medicines in oncology and immunology. Originating in 2017 from research capabilities established in China, the company operates research and development across Shanghai and Wuxi (Jiangsu), China, and is listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market (ticker 688192). Dizal's most advanced programs include sunvozertinib (DZD9008), an oral EGFR exon 20 insertion inhibitor for non-small cell lung cancer marketed as Zegfrovy, and golidocitinib (DZD4205), a selective JAK1 inhibitor developed for relapsed/refractory peripheral T-cell lymphoma. Dizal Pharma was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm HongShan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). As a pharmaceutical developer it publishes a corporate marketing and investor-facing website but does not expose a public developer platform, API program, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time; this profile captures the company identity for the network.

providers.name: Elektrofi
providers.description: Elektrofi is a Boston-based biopharmaceutical formulation technology company reinventing how biologic therapies are delivered to patients. Its Hypercon ultra-high-concentration microparticle platform and Elektroject process turn monoclonal antibodies, therapeutic proteins, and other large-molecule drugs into stable, syringe-injectable formulations suited to small-volume, at-home subcutaneous self-administration instead of intravenous infusion. The company has partnered with Eli Lilly and Janssen Biotech (Johnson & Johnson) on multi-target drug-delivery collaborations, and was acquired by Halozyme Therapeutics in November 2025. Elektrofi is a biotechnology company and does not publish a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company entity within the network.

providers.name: Gate Bioscience
providers.description: Gate Bioscience is a preclinical biotechnology company founded in 2021 and headquartered in Brisbane, California, creating a new class of small-molecule medicines called Molecular Gates. Molecular Gates selectively eliminate disease-causing extracellular proteins at their origin inside the cell by binding the secretory translocon, the channel through which proteins exit the cell, so targeted proteins are degraded rather than secreted. The company's proprietary Molecular Gate Discovery Platform pairs a privileged library of molecules with bespoke secretion-focused assays and deep secretory-pathway biology to pursue more than 1,000 diseases linked to extracellular proteins. Gate Bioscience is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) Bio + Health, GV, Versant Ventures, ARCH Venture Partners, Forbion and Eli Lilly, and has raised roughly $134M across Series A and an oversubscribed $65M Series B. As a therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation; this profile is an API Evangelist network company record maintained for the portfolio graph.

providers.name: Monte Rosa Therapeutics *
providers.description: Monte Rosa Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering molecular glue degrader (MGD) medicines. It pairs its QuEEN discovery engine — integrating artificial intelligence, machine learning, and structural biology — with proprietary chemistry to design small molecules that selectively degrade disease-causing proteins previously considered undruggable, across oncology and immunology, with collaborations including Novartis and Roche. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation; this profile captures its web presence and probed domain-security surface.

providers.name: OMass Therapeutics
providers.description: OMass Therapeutics is an Oxford, UK biotechnology company developing medicines for immunological and rare diseases. It harnesses proprietary biochemistry, native mass spectrometry and custom chemistry through its OdyssION drug discovery platform to interrogate drug targets and how they interact with their native biological ecosystem, separate from the confounding complexity of the cell. The company operates a corporate and scientific web presence (science, pipeline, publications, news and blog) and, as a therapeutics company, publishes no public developer or API surface. Backed by GV and other life-sciences investors.

providers.name: Ouro Medicines
providers.description: Ouro Medicines is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in South San Francisco, California, defining the future of treatment for people with immune-mediated diseases. Its pipeline centers on T cell engager programs for autoimmune conditions, including the lead candidate OM336 (evaluated in the AIC-1001 clinical trial), alongside an expanded access policy. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As a therapeutics developer, Ouro Medicines publishes a corporate and scientific website but no public developer program, API, or technical documentation surface. Recent company news includes a definitive agreement for Gilead Sciences to acquire Ouro Medicines to advance its first-in-class T cell engager program for autoimmune diseases.

providers.name: Trishula Therapeutics
providers.description: Trishula Therapeutics is a privately held, clinical-stage immuno-oncology company developing cancer immunotherapies that target immune-evasion mechanisms in the tumor microenvironment. Its lead candidate, TTX-030, is a first-in-class monoclonal antibody that inhibits CD39, an enzyme in the adenosine pathway that tumors exploit to suppress anti-tumor immunity; TTX-030 has advanced into Phase 2 clinical trials, including studies in metastatic pancreatic cancer. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. It is a therapeutics company with a corporate web presence and no public API, developer, or software product surface.

providers.name: Virtuoso Therapeutics
providers.description: Virtuoso Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company advancing a pipeline of novel bispecific antibodies to treat cancer. Using a differentiated approach to antibody engineering, the company designs molecules intended to overcome the limitations of existing therapies and to address major hurdles facing emerging classes of oncology treatments. Virtuoso is a venture-backed portfolio company of Canaan Partners. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; the company currently publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Be Biopharma
providers.description: Be Biopharma (Be Bio) is a Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in October 2020 by Longwood Fund together with B cell engineering researchers David Rawlings, M.D. and Richard James, Ph.D. of Seattle Children's Research Institute. The company develops engineered B Cell Medicines (BCMs) — a patient's own B cells engineered to produce a therapeutic protein — for genetic disease, cancer and other serious conditions. Its lead candidate, BE-101, inserted a functional Factor IX gene into primary human B cells for hemophilia B and held FDA Orphan Drug and Fast Track designations; a second program, BE-102, targeted hypophosphatasia. The company raised $82M in October 2024 and $92M in a January 2025 Series C, dosed the first participant in the Phase 1/2 BeCoMe-9 trial in July 2025, and terminated that trial in June 2026 for stated strategic business reasons. Be Biopharma is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it has never published a developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Celgene
providers.description: Celgene Corporation was a global biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of innovative therapies for cancer and immune-inflammatory diseases. Celgene was acquired by Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) in November 2019 and its operations are now consolidated under BMS. No public developer API has been identified; engagement is organized through BMS clinical trials, study connect, and investigator-sponsored research portals.

providers.name: Denali Therapeutics
providers.description: Denali Therapeutics is a South San Francisco-based biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, and delivers therapeutics for people living with serious neurodegenerative and lysosomal storage diseases. Its proprietary Transport Vehicle (TV) platform is engineered to cross the blood-brain barrier so that large-molecule therapies can reach the brain and body. Denali maintains a public GitHub organization publishing open-source computational-biology and cheminformatics research tools (archs4, basechem, napari-mito-hcs), but publishes no public developer API. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences portfolio company of GV.

providers.name: Elion Therapeutics
providers.description: Elion Therapeutics is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company developing treatments for life-threatening invasive fungal infections (IFIs). Formerly known as Sfunga Therapeutics, the company was founded on the belief that mechanistic insight into natural products enables targeted optimization of them. Its lead candidate, SF001, is a next-generation polyene antifungal — a rationally designed analog of amphotericin B intended to retain broad fungicidal activity while mitigating the systemic toxicity that limits the parent molecule. SF001 received FDA Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) and Fast Track designations in 2023 and has advanced from a first-in-human single-ascending-dose study into multiple-ascending-dose evaluation. Elion closed an $81 million Series B in June 2024 led by Deerfield Management and the AMR Action Fund, with participation from Illinois Ventures. Elion is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API contract, and this profile records that absence rather than any API surface.

providers.name: Exscientia
providers.description: Exscientia was an Oxford UK-based AI-driven precision medicine and drug design company, founded in 2012 as a spin-out from the University of Dundee. Its platform combined generative chemistry (Centaur Chemist) with patient tissue-based screening (EVE, an automated single-cell platform for testing drug candidates directly against patient-derived tumor samples) to design small-molecule drug candidates faster and at lower cost than conventional pharma R&D. Notable firsts included EXS-21546 (an A2A antagonist developed with Evotec), DSP-1181 (the first AI-designed molecule to enter human clinical trials, with Sumitomo Dainippon Pharma), and DSP-0038 (a dual 5-HT1A/5-HT2A modulator for Alzheimer's psychosis). Exscientia maintained active pharma partnerships with Sanofi, Bristol Myers Squibb, Bayer, Sumitomo, and Merck KGaA. Exscientia was acquired by Recursion Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: RXRX) in an all-stock deal that closed in November 2024; the combined company operates under the Recursion brand and the legacy exscientia.ai website now redirects to recursion.com. The Exscientia name persists primarily through its GitHub organization, which continues to host open-source scientific Python packages for molecular predictive modelling (molflux), physics-based ML potentials (physicsml), antibody structure prediction (abodybuilder3), and biomolecular simulation (biosimspace) used by the wider computational chemistry and structural biology community. Exscientia did not expose any public commercial APIs, SDKs, or developer products before or after the merger; platform access was always delivered through collaborative drug-discovery agreements.

providers.name: Novartis
providers.description: Novartis AG is a Swiss multinational pharmaceutical corporation headquartered in Basel, Switzerland, and one of the largest pharmaceutical companies in the world by revenue. The company focuses on innovative medicines across oncology, immunology, neuroscience, cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic disease areas. Novartis does not publish a public external developer API. The company does maintain an Open Source Science programme that releases scientific computing libraries, Drupal modules, and informatics tooling on GitHub for use by the research community.

providers.name: Novo Nordisk
providers.description: Novo Nordisk A/S is a Danish multinational pharmaceutical company headquartered in Bagsværd, Denmark, and the world leader in diabetes care. The company also develops treatments for obesity, rare blood disorders, and growth-hormone therapy, including its widely known GLP-1 medicines Ozempic, Wegovy, and Rybelsus. Novo Nordisk does not publish a public commercial developer API. The company maintains a research GitHub organization (novonordisk-research) that releases open-source scientific computing libraries and an SDK for the Waters Empower Web API (OptiHPLCHandler) used in pharmaceutical analytical chemistry workflows.

providers.name: Pharmazz
providers.description: Pharmazz, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Willowbrook, Illinois, founded and led by pharmacologist Dr. Anil Gulati. The company discovers, develops and commercializes first-in-class therapeutics for critical care and neurovascular medicine, built around two lead small-molecule candidates: centhaquine (Lyfaquin), a resuscitative agent for hypovolemic shock that holds marketing authorization from the Drugs Controller General of India and is licensed to Dr. Reddy's Laboratories for the Indian market, and sovateltide (Tycamzzi), an endothelin-B receptor agonist for cerebral ischemic stroke. Additional pipeline programs target septic shock, acute kidney injury, cardiac arrest, acute spinal cord injury, hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and Alzheimer's disease. Pharmazz is a drug-development company, not a software vendor; its public web presence is a corporate and investor brochure site and it operates no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Quintiles Transnational Holdings
providers.description: Quintiles Transnational Holdings was a Fortune 500 contract research organization (CRO) that provided biopharmaceutical development and commercial outsourcing services to the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device industries. In October 2016, Quintiles merged with IMS Health to form IQVIA, a leading provider of advanced analytics, technology solutions, and contract research services to the life sciences industry. The legacy Quintiles entity no longer operates as an independent company and does not maintain a public API program; all developer-facing capabilities are now part of IQVIA.

providers.name: Recursion Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Recursion Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: RXRX) is a Salt Lake City-based AI-enabled drug discovery company that operates the Recursion Operating System (Recursion OS), a vertically integrated platform combining automated wet-lab cellular phenomics, transcriptomics (Trekseq), proteomics, ADME, chemistry, and patient data with machine learning to map biology and design drug candidates. The platform runs on BioHive-2, a NVIDIA-built supercomputer ranked among the top global systems and dedicated to biopharma workloads, and is fed by 50+ petabytes of proprietary biological and chemical data. In November 2024 Recursion completed the acquisition of Exscientia, folding Exscientia's generative AI chemistry, Centaur Chemist, and clinical pipeline into the combined company; Recursion now runs more than 10 clinical and preclinical programs (REC-4881 for FAP, REC-3565 MALT1 inhibitor, REC-1245 RBM39 for biomarker-enriched solid tumors and lymphomas, REC-617 CDK7 inhibitor, REC-994 for cerebral cavernous malformation, REC-2282 for NF2- mutated meningiomas, REC-4209 for IPF, REC-7735 for HSD obesity), 10+ advanced discovery programs, and 10+ partnered programs across Roche (Genentech), Bayer, Sanofi, and Merck KGaA (Darmstadt). Recursion does not currently expose paid commercial APIs to external developers; assets and data access are delivered through licensing, scientific collaborations, and the MapApp web product. Externally, Recursion ships substantial open tooling: the RxRx family of open phenomics datasets (RxRx1, RxRx2, RxRx3, RxRx3-core, RxRx19a, RxRx19b) hosted at rxrx.ai and Hugging Face, the OpenPhenom-S/16 foundation model (released on Hugging Face and Google Cloud's Model Garden, with Phenom-Beta on NVIDIA BioNeMo), the MolE molecular foundation model, the gflownet library for graph and molecular generative modeling, SynFlowNet/synflownet-boltz for retrosynthesis-aware molecular design, maes_microscopy (NeurIPS 2023 spotlight masked autoencoders for cell microscopy), and rxrx1-utils for the NeurIPS 2019 CellSignal competition. The combination positions Recursion as a Tier-2 AI drug discovery provider with no commercial API surface but a meaningful open-source and open-model presence aimed at the computational biology research community.

providers.name: Scorpion Therapeutics
providers.description: Scorpion Therapeutics is a clinical-stage precision oncology biotechnology company founded in 2020 and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. It pursued what it called Precision Oncology 2.0 — integrating target discovery, medicinal chemistry and translational medicine to produce mutant-selective small-molecule cancer drugs — led by STX-478, an oral mutant-selective PI3K-alpha inhibitor in Phase 1/2 trials for breast cancer and other advanced solid tumors, and STX-721, a covalent EGFR/HER2 exon 20 inhibitor. In January 2025 Eli Lilly agreed to acquire Scorpion and its PI3K-alpha program in a transaction valued at up to $2.5 billion, with the non-PI3K-alpha pipeline and staff spun into a separate independent company. Scorpion is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification, and its own domain now redirects to the acquirer's announcement.

providers.name: Tearclear
providers.description: TearClear Corp. is a clinical-stage ophthalmic pharmaceutical company founded in 2015 that develops a preservative-removing drug delivery platform: a chemical filter built into a conventional multi-dose eye-drop bottle that captures benzalkonium chloride (BAK) at the point of instillation, so the medication stays preserved in the bottle but reaches the ocular surface preservative-free. Its lead candidate TC-002 (latanoprost ophthalmic solution 0.005%) met the primary and all secondary endpoints in the CLEAR Phase 3 pivotal glaucoma trial, with TC-001 (timolol), TC-003 (brimonidine/timolol) and TC-004 (brimonidine) behind it. TearClear ships drug products and delivery hardware, not software: it operates no developer program and publishes no API, SDK or machine-readable contract, and its own corporate domain no longer resolves to a served website.

providers.name: Allergan
providers.description: Allergan was a global pharmaceutical company that developed, manufactured, and commercialized branded therapeutics, devices, and biologic products across medical aesthetics, eye care, central nervous system, and gastroenterology. The company was the maker of Botox (botulinum toxin), Juvederm (injectable filler), CoolSculpting, Alphagan, Vraylar, Linzess, and Ubrelvy. AbbVie completed its $63 billion acquisition of Allergan in May 2020. The company now operates as Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company.
