Allergan Data Labs, the digital innovation arm, built the Alle loyalty platform serving over 3 million users across nearly 20,000 medical offices and spas in the US, using machine learning for personalized consumer engagement in medical aesthetics. Allergan Aesthetics does not maintain a public developer API program.

providers.name: Sirum
providers.description: SIRUM (Supporting Initiatives to Redistribute Unused Medicine) is a nonprofit and the country's largest redistributor of surplus prescription medication. It connects unused, in-date medicine from manufacturers, wholesalers, pharmacies, and nursing homes with patients who cannot afford their prescriptions, operating under drug-donation laws across the United States. SIRUM runs a logistics and matching platform that routes donated medication to community partners and individuals in need, aiming to close the gap for the tens of millions of Americans who skip prescribed medication because of cost. Surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Acceleron
providers.description: Acceleron is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Accro Bioscience
providers.description: Accro Bioscience (Suzhou) Limited, trading as Accropeutics, is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2017 with operations in Suzhou, China and New York. It develops small-molecule therapeutics against regulated cell death — necroptosis, pyroptosis and ferroptosis — targeting the cell-death-to-inflammation loop behind inflammatory, fibrotic, autoimmune and oncology disease. Its pipeline is led by AC-101, an oral selective RIPK2 inhibitor in Phase Ib for ulcerative colitis with FDA clearance for a Phase II multi-regional IBD study; AC-201, a TYK2/JAK1 pseudokinase inhibitor licensed to Fosun Pharma for Greater China as FXS5626; and AC-003, a RIPK1 inhibitor in Phase Ib for acute graft-versus-host disease with FDA Orphan Drug Designation. It closed a $50M Series C led by OrbiMed in May 2026. Accro Bioscience sells drug candidates, not software: it runs no developer program and publishes no API, SDK or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: aceatherapeutics
providers.description: ACEA Therapeutics (aceatherapeutics.com) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing innovative small-molecule and antibody-drug-conjugate treatments across oncology, autoimmune, and antiviral therapeutic areas, with product candidates including Olgotrelvir, Abivertinib, AC0058, STI-6129, and AC0939. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a pharmaceutical company oriented toward patients, physicians, and investors, ACEA Therapeutics publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or technical integration surface at this time; this profile captures its verifiable web/domain footprint only.

providers.name: Adcentrx Therapeutics
providers.description: Adcentrx Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in San Diego, California, developing next-generation antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and protein conjugate therapeutics for cancer and other life-threatening diseases. Its proprietary i-Conjugation technology platform pairs stable conjugation chemistry and protease-cleavable linkers with novel small-molecule payloads; the clinical pipeline includes ADRX-0706 (Nectin-4) and ADRX-0405 (STEAP1). The company was surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market). It publishes a corporate and investor-relations website only — no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind was found.

providers.name: Allena Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Allena Pharmaceuticals is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Areteia Therapeutics
providers.description: Areteia Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company, formerly based in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, operating in the life-sciences sector. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company is no longer operating: areteiatx.com serves only a closure notice directing asset and general inquiries to contact addresses, and the company publishes no developer portal, API, documentation, SDKs, or other technical developer surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; retained for network completeness with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Aria Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Aria Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company that applies artificial intelligence and machine learning to drug discovery, using a computational platform to identify and advance small-molecule therapeutic candidates for complex, inflammatory, and immunological diseases. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Aria operates as a therapeutics developer rather than a software or API provider. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company profile; an enrichment pass found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or other programmatic developer surface for the company at this time.

providers.name: Atara Bio
providers.description: Atara Biotherapeutics is a clinical-stage allogeneic (off-the-shelf) T-cell immunotherapy company developing transformative therapies that harness T cells to fight cancer and autoimmune conditions, and is the first company to receive regulatory approval for an allogeneic T-cell immunotherapy. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Kleiner Perkins and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes a corporate website but no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation was found; this profile carries identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Aviceda Therapeutics
providers.description: Aviceda Therapeutics is a private, late-stage clinical biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts that describes itself as the world leader in glyco-immune checkpoint therapeutics. It develops immune-mediated therapies built on a glyco-mimetic nanoparticle platform that targets the interaction between sialic acids on cell surfaces and Siglec immune receptors in order to modulate aberrant inflammation. Its lead asset, AVD-104, is an intravitreally administered sialic-acid-coated nanoparticle being evaluated in the Phase 2/3 SIGLEC trial for geographic atrophy secondary to age-related macular degeneration. Aviceda is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: BeiGene
providers.description: BeiGene (rebranded as BeOne Medicines in 2025) is a global oncology biopharmaceutical company founded in 2010, developing and commercializing cancer therapies worldwide. Its portfolio spans blood cancers and solid tumors, led by BRUKINSA (zanubrutinib), a BTK inhibitor, alongside programs in protein degradation (CDACs) and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). The company is listed on NASDAQ (BGNE), HKEX, and the Shanghai STAR Market, with a global footprint across 30+ countries (beonemedicines.com). Surfaced as a portfolio company of Hillhouse; no public developer portal, API, or SDK program is currently published.

providers.name: BioOrbit
providers.description: BioOrbit is a London-based in-space manufacturing company, founded in 2023, that uses microgravity to crystallise protein-based biologic drugs at scale. Its autonomous BOX hardware — a compact, microwave-sized manufacturing unit designed to operate in low-Earth orbit — grows highly ordered crystalline forms of therapeutic proteins that reduce viscosity, enabling treatments normally given intravenously (including cancer therapies) to be reformulated as subcutaneous, self-injectable products. Co-founded by Dr Katie King and Dr Leonor Teles, BioOrbit raised the world's largest seed round for in-space manufacturing (~£9.8M / $13.2M) co-led by LocalGlobe and Breega with Seedcamp, Auxxo, Type One, 7percent and angels, and is supported by the UK Space Agency, ESA BIC and ESA BSGN. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Seedcamp portfolio company; it publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: BlackThorn Therapeutics *
providers.description: BlackThorn Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2015 and headquartered in South San Francisco, focused on discovering and developing targeted therapeutics for brain diseases and central nervous system (CNS) disorders such as major depressive disorder and schizophrenia, using a precision-medicine platform. It was backed by gv (Google Ventures) and later combined into Neumora Therapeutics, whose corporate site now resolves at neumoratx.com. This is a life-sciences company profile: it operates no public developer API, SDK, or agent surface, so API-oriented artifacts are not applicable beyond a domain-security probe of the corporate host.

providers.name: Cabinet Health
providers.description: Cabinet Health is an end-to-end supply chain platform for private-label over-the-counter (OTC) medicines. The company develops, sources, manufactures, and delivers OTC products across 70+ active ingredients in tablet, softgel, capsule, liquid, powder, gummy, and chewable formats to retailers, wholesalers, and online marketplaces, emphasizing sustainable, refillable packaging and quality assurance at scale. Cabinet also produces its own certified B Corp consumer brand sold on Amazon and Target. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer or API surface has been found for this provider.

providers.name: Cencora
providers.description: Cencora (formerly AmerisourceBergen, renamed August 2023) is a leading global pharmaceutical solutions organization that connects manufacturers, providers, pharmacies, and patients across the healthcare supply chain. Cencora operates an Axway-based central EDI platform exchanging over 800,000 EDI messages daily with more than 23,000 trading partners and a Cell and Gene Therapy (CGT) Integration Hub for real-time data exchange with biopharma and provider platforms. No public developer API portal has been identified.

providers.name: Centreherbs (Beijing Shengtaier Biotechnology)
providers.description: Centreherbs is the brand of Beijing Shengtaier Biotechnology Co., Ltd., a veterinary pharmaceutical company founded in 1999 and headquartered in the Daxing Biopharmaceutical Industrial Park, Beijing, China. An integrated research, development, production, and distribution organization for animal health, it specializes in veterinary traditional Chinese medicine preparations, animal vaccines for poultry and livestock, plant-based premixed feed additives, and pet health products, backed by four wholly-owned subsidiaries and an internal biotech research institute. It is a healthcare portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. The company operates a corporate marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Cerexa
providers.description: Cerexa was a privately held biopharmaceutical company founded in the mid-2000s (its cerexa.com domain was registered in March 2005) to develop anti-infective therapies for serious, drug-resistant bacterial infections in the hospital setting. Its lead program was ceftaroline fosamil, a fifth-generation cephalosporin antibiotic active against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), in-licensed from Takeda Pharmaceutical Company and carried forward by Forest Laboratories; the compound was approved by the FDA on October 29, 2010 and marketed as Teflaro in the United States and Zinforo in Europe. Cerexa was backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners, and its programs ultimately passed through Forest Laboratories into the Actavis/Allergan combination (Forest Laboratories was acquired by Actavis on July 1, 2014) and on to AbbVie. Cerexa no longer operates as an independent company and has no developer surface: it publishes no API, no SDKs, no GitHub organization and no documentation, and its historical cerexa.com domain is now registered and operated by AbbVie, 301-redirecting to AbbVie's Allergan page. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Chimerix
providers.description: Chimerix, Inc. was a biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Durham, North Carolina, focused on developing medicines for serious and life-threatening diseases. It is best known for brincidofovir (TEMBEXA), an antiviral approved by the U.S. FDA in 2021 as a smallpox medical countermeasure, and for dordaviprone (ONC201), an investigational small-molecule therapy for H3 K27M-mutant diffuse glioma, a form of brain cancer. Chimerix was a publicly traded company (NASDAQ: CMRX) and was acquired by Jazz Pharmaceuticals in 2025, primarily for dordaviprone; the chimerix.com domain now redirects to jazzpharma.com. As a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, Chimerix does not operate a public developer program or API surface — this profile tracks it as a company entity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ChronicleBio
providers.description: ChronicleBio is a biotechnology company working at the intersection of human data and drug discovery, with the stated mission of translating human data into disease-defining medicines. It operates in the healthcare and life-sciences sector and was surfaced through the electric-capital portfolio. As of this profile, ChronicleBio publishes a corporate marketing website but no public developer surface: enrichment found no API documentation, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, MCP server, or changelog. Domain security was probed live (TLS 1.3, HSTS, SPF, and a DMARC quarantine policy present; DNSSEC and CAA absent).

providers.name: cn
providers.description: cn is the China-region web presence (cn.ausperbio.com) of AusperBio Therapeutics (Hangzhou Ausper Bio / 杭州浩博医药有限公司), a Phase II clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming HBV treatment toward a functional cure and advancing oligonucleotide therapeutics. AusperBio leverages its proprietary Med-Oligo ASO platform with targeted delivery technologies to apply antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapeutics across viral infections, metabolic conditions, genetic disorders, and immune diseases; its lead candidate AHB-137 is an unconjugated ASO advancing through Phase II/III trials for chronic hepatitis B. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; the company publishes a marketing website but no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: colandpharma
providers.description: colandpharma was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no public surface to profile: colandpharma.com is registered (created 2007-09-21, renewed through 2027-09-21, Gname.com registrar) and delegates to share-dns nameservers, but the zone publishes no A/AAAA, MX, TXT, SPF, DMARC or CAA records. The apex and the www, api, docs and developer subdomains do not resolve, and the authoritative nameserver itself returns no host records, confirming a dormant or parked domain rather than a transient outage. There is consequently no website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog. This record is retained as a lead; re-run enrichment if the domain is ever brought online.

providers.name: Corsair Pharma
providers.description: Corsair Pharma, Inc. is a privately held clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing proprietary prodrugs of treprostinil for the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Its lead program, the TRX-248 transdermal system, is an investigational once-daily patch that delivers an inactive treprostinil prodrug across the skin for conversion to active drug in the liver, aiming to combine the efficacy and titration profile of parenteral prostacyclin therapy with non-invasive once-daily dosing. The company completed its preclinical program, announced positive Phase 1 results for TRX-248 in June 2026, closed a $23M Series B led by New Rhein Healthcare Investors, and has entered a strategic collaboration with United Therapeutics to advance novel treprostinil prodrugs. Corsair Pharma is a drug developer, not a software vendor: its public web presence is a five-page marketing and investor-news site with no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: CTRL Therapeutics
providers.description: CTRL Therapeutics (cTRL Tx) is a Chicago-based preclinical biotechnology company developing next-generation cell therapies for solid tumors. The company harnesses circulating tumor-reactive lymphocytes (cTRLs) - a rare, potent T cell population found in the blood and naturally equipped to fight cancer - to engineer polyclonal cell therapies that avoid invasive tumor-tissue surgery. From a single blood draw, CTRL's proprietary IsoQore cell-sorting platform isolates millions of migratory, tumor-reactive cTRLs via novel markers, aiming to simplify the discovery, manufacturing and administration of solid-tumor cell therapy. CTRL launched in 2023 with a $10M seed financing led by General Catalyst, with participation from Intermountain Health and FACIT. This profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company operates a corporate website and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Decibel Therapeutics *
providers.description: Decibel Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on gene therapies for hearing loss and balance disorders. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain, decibeltx.com, 301-redirects to regeneron.com, consistent with the company having been acquired/absorbed by Regeneron; Decibel maintains no independent public developer portal, API, documentation, or other developer surface. This profile is retained as a network lead and carries only infrastructure-level (domain security) probe data.

providers.name: Diplomat Pharmacy
providers.description: Diplomat Pharmacy was an independent provider of specialty pharmacy services that helped patients with chronic and complex conditions access and manage specialty medications. The company was acquired by UnitedHealth Group's OptumRx, and operations have been integrated under that brand. No publicly documented developer APIs are offered under the Diplomat Pharmacy name.

providers.name: Elixiron Immunotherapeutics
providers.description: Elixiron Immunotherapeutics (Cayman) Limited is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2017, with offices in Taipei, Taiwan and Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing precision immunotherapies for neuroinflammation, autoimmune disease and cancer. Its clinical pipeline is led by enrupatinib (EI-1071), a small-molecule CSF-1R inhibitor in development for Alzheimer's disease and other neurodegenerative indications, and EI-001, a fully human anti-interferon-gamma monoclonal antibody in Phase 2 for vitiligo, alongside preclinical EI-012 (anti-CD36) and EI-220 (mRNA) oncology programs. The company publishes a corporate and investor-relations website only: there is no developer portal, public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification of any kind on its own hosts.

providers.name: Endo International
providers.description: Endo International was a specialty pharmaceutical company best known for Xiaflex (collagenase clostridium histolyticum), branded urology and orthopedic products, and a large sterile-injectables and generics business (Par Pharmaceutical). Endo filed Chapter 11 in August 2022 amid mass opioid litigation tied to its legacy Opana ER franchise, and emerged in April 2024 as the private company Endo, Inc., owned by its former creditors. On July 31, 2025, Endo combined with Mallinckrodt; the merged group then separated in November 2025 into two independent companies — Keenova Therapeutics (specialty branded therapeutics, including the former Endo Xiaflex/urology/orthopedics portfolio and Mallinckrodt specialty brands) and Par Health (generics, sterile injectables, and pharmaceutical Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients manufacturing). Endo no longer operates as a standalone public-facing pharmaceutical company. There is no public developer program, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or technology API surface associated with Endo, the post-emergence Endo Inc, Keenova Therapeutics, or Par Health. Any references to "API" on the successor companies' sites refer to pharmaceutical Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, not software application programming interfaces.

providers.name: Epiodyne
providers.description: Epiodyne is a San Francisco-based pharmaceutical company using structure-based drug discovery to develop small-molecule opioid medicines precisely calibrated for minimal side effects and minimal addiction potential. Its pipeline targets pain management and opioid use disorder (OUD), engineering compounds with specifically tuned receptor functions to address the opioid crisis. The company is a venture-backed biotech portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or technology platform.

providers.name: Epizyme
providers.description: Epizyme, Inc. was a Cambridge, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company developing epigenetic therapies for cancer and other diseases. Its lead product, TAZVERIK (tazemetostat), is an oral EZH2 inhibitor approved by the FDA for epithelioid sarcoma and relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma. Epizyme was acquired by Ipsen in 2022. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub via the kleiner-perkins venture portfolio; the company operates no public developer program, API, or documentation surface, and its former corporate website (epizyme.com) is no longer serving a web presence though the domain remains registered and mail-active.

providers.name: EQRx
providers.description: EQRx was a biopharmaceutical company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2020 by Alexis Borisy with a mission to develop and deliver innovative, patent-protected medicines at radically lower prices. The company went public in 2021 through a SPAC merger with CM Life Sciences III and built an oncology and immunology pipeline anchored by in-licensed candidates such as aumolertinib and sugemalimab. In 2023 EQRx wound down its drug-development programs and was acquired by Revolution Medicines in an all-stock transaction. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (backed by a16z and GV); it never operated a public developer platform or API, and its web presence is no longer live.

providers.name: Eureka Therapeutics
providers.description: Eureka Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Emeryville, California, developing T-cell therapies for solid tumors and hematologic malignancies. The company was founded by Dr. Cheng Liu and is built on two proprietary platforms: E-ALPHA, a high-throughput human antibody discovery engine used to find binders against cancer-specific targets, and ARTEMIS, an engineered T-cell receptor platform (AbTCR) designed to deliver CAR-T-level potency with a reduced cytokine-release profile. Its clinical programs include ET140203 (ARYA-1 in adults, ARYA-2 in pediatrics) and ECT204 (ARYA-3) in advanced liver cancer, alongside a GPC2 ARTEMIS T-cell program for neuroblastoma licensed from the National Cancer Institute. Eureka publishes a corporate website, pipeline and technology overviews, a press-release archive with an RSS feed, and patient-facing trial information; as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Evelo Biosciences *
providers.description: Evelo Biosciences was a Flagship Pioneering-founded, GV-backed microbiome biotechnology company in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing orally delivered investigational medicines acting on the small intestinal axis. Following clinical failures of its lead candidates EDP1815 and EDP2939, the company announced dissolution in November 2023 and has been wound down. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a dissolved life-sciences portfolio record: the evelobio.com domain now serves only a parked catch-all error page and the company publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API surface of any kind.

providers.name: Exo Therapeutics
providers.description: Exo Therapeutics is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of crv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: FDA Regulations
providers.description: Federal regulations governing the safety, efficacy, and security of food, drugs, medical devices, and other products under FDA jurisdiction. Organizations adopt it to address specific technical or business challenges in their environments.

providers.name: Forty Seven *
providers.description: Forty Seven, Inc. was an immuno-oncology biotechnology company founded in 2015 to commercialize CD47 immune-evasion research licensed from Stanford University (Irv Weissman and colleagues). Its lead program was magrolimab, a monoclonal antibody targeting CD47 — the "do not eat me" signal tumor cells use to evade macrophage-mediated killing — studied in myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Backed by GV, the company was acquired by Gilead Sciences in 2020 for roughly $4.9 billion; the fortyseveninc.com domain now redirects to gilead.com. As a clinical-stage therapeutics company it exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Genesis Therapeutics
providers.description: Genesis Therapeutics (Genesis Molecular AI) is an AI-focused biotechnology company building GEMS (Genesis Exploration of Molecular Space), a generative and predictive AI operating system for small-molecule drug discovery. GEMS combines structure-based deep learning, language and diffusion models, and physics-based simulation (molecular dynamics and quantum chemistry) to generate and optimize molecules for complex targets, accelerating hit identification through lead optimization and candidate selection. In 2025 the company introduced Pearl, a next-generation foundation model for drug discovery. Headquartered in Burlingame, California with a laboratory in San Diego, Genesis has raised over $300M and partners with Eli Lilly, Gilead, Genentech, and Incyte while advancing its own therapeutic pipeline. It is not a public API provider: GEMS is a proprietary internal platform with no published developer portal, documentation, or API.

providers.name: Icahn Enterprises
providers.description: Icahn Enterprises L.P. is a diversified holding company engaged in the investment, energy, automotive, food packaging, real estate, home fashion, and pharmaceutical industries through its operating subsidiaries. The company does not currently publish public developer APIs; investor relations, SEC filings, and corporate communications are provided through its corporate website.

providers.name: Immunos Therapeutics
providers.description: Immunos Therapeutics is a privately held biotechnology company focused on harnessing the immune system to treat cancer and inflammatory diseases. The company develops immuno-oncology and immunomodulatory therapeutic candidates, advancing a preclinical and clinical pipeline supported by scientific and clinical advisory boards. Immunos Therapeutics is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As a therapeutics/drug-development company it operates in the life sciences rather than as a software API provider, and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer documentation at this time. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and portfolio discovery.

providers.name: Innovent
providers.description: Innovent Biologics (信达生物制药) is a biopharmaceutical company founded in 2011 and headquartered in the Suzhou Industrial Park, China, that discovers, develops, manufactures, and commercializes high-quality biologic medicines for the treatment of oncology, autoimmune, cardiovascular and metabolic, and ophthalmology diseases. Its portfolio includes the PD-1 inhibitor Tyvyt (sintilimab), developed in partnership with Eli Lilly, alongside a broad pipeline of monoclonal antibodies and other biologics. Innovent is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (01801.HK) and was surfaced through the Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China) portfolio. Innovent is a therapeutics company and does not publish a public developer API surface; this profile captures its corporate and domain-security identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Iolyx Therapeutics
providers.description: Iolyx Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Burlingame, California, working at what it calls the intersection of immunology and ophthalmology — "immuno-ophthalmology". The company develops immunomodulatory therapeutics that target ocular inflammation at its source, using what it describes as innovative pathways and tailored formulations for precise delivery to the relevant ocular tissues, positioned as an alternative to conventional steroids and broad immunosuppressants. Its lead asset, ILYX-002, is in trials for autoimmune-associated dry eye disease; the company announced Phase 2 results in May 2025 and, in December 2025, a strategic agreement with Laboratoires Théa to develop and commercialize ILYX-002 alongside Series B funding for its retinal pipeline. The stated pipeline spans front-of-eye indications (dry eye, ocular allergy, rosacea, uveitis) and back-of-eye indications (age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, posterior uveitis). Iolyx is a drug developer rather than a software vendor: it operates a six-page WordPress marketing site at iolyx.com and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Jacobio Pharma
providers.description: Jacobio Pharma (Jacobio Pharmaceutica) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering and developing novel small-molecule cancer therapies against historically "undruggable" oncology targets. Its pipeline spans 10+ clinical programs across six major tumor signaling pathways (including p53, RAS, RB, MYC, immune checkpoints, and tumor metabolism), advanced through proprietary allosteric drug-discovery and iADC platforms, more than 300 global patent applications, and 100+ clinical centers worldwide. Surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a corporate website but no public API or developer surface.

Its lead approved product is Kelopin (tolametinib), a MEK inhibitor for advanced NRAS-mutant melanoma. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners; no public developer or API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Kenvue

Everyday care is a powerful catalyst in making you feel better, inside and out. Kenvue's iconic brands include Tylenol, Neutrogena, Listerine, Aveeno, Band-Aid, and Johnson's.

providers.name: Kinaset Therapeutics
providers.description: Kinaset Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Medfield, Massachusetts, founded in 2020 by Robert Clarke (CEO), Roger Heerman (COO) and Frazer Morgan (CDO) to develop novel inhaled therapeutics for severe respiratory disease. Its lead candidate, frevecitinib (KN-002), is a dry-powder inhaled pan-JAK inhibitor — potent and balanced across JAK1, JAK2, JAK3 and TYK2 — designed as a non-invasive anti-inflammatory add-on to standard of care for all severe asthma patients regardless of the underlying cause of inflammation, and explored in COPD. The company completed a Phase 1/1b program (NCT05006521), received FDA IND clearance, and in July 2026 dosed the first patient in the Phase 2b PANAIRAMA trial (NCT07532265) after closing a $103M oversubscribed Series B in January 2026 led by RA Capital Management and Forge Life Science Partners, with EQT Life Sciences, Vivo Capital, Schroders Capital, Willett Advisors, Pictet Alternative Advisors, Sixty Degree Capital, Atlas Venture, 5AM Ventures and Gimv participating on roughly $143M raised to date. Kinaset is a drug developer, not a software company: its product is a clinical pipeline, and it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDKs, no webhooks and no machine-readable API contract. Its entire public surface is a 34-page Squarespace marketing and investor-news site whose robots.txt disallows every platform JSON view and blocks the major AI crawlers by user agent.

Its lead candidate, LOY-002, targets metabolic dysfunction in dogs aged ten and older and is progressing through FDA approval. The company serves veterinary professionals and dog owners with clinical and care resources and runs clinical trials; it publishes no developer API, documentation, SDKs, or public code repositories. The company operated in the rare-disease and epilepsy space of the life-sciences industry. providers.name: Mosanna
providers.description: Mosanna Therapeutics is a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company developing a nighttime nasal spray therapy for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Headquartered in Redwood City, California with an office in Basel, Switzerland, the company is pursuing a pharmacological alternative to mechanical CPAP devices by reactivating the upper-airway muscles that keep the airway open during sleep. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners, Mosanna operates a corporate marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Mozart Therapeutics
providers.description: Mozart Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Seattle, Washington, founded in 2020 to develop disease-modifying therapies for autoimmune and inflammatory disease. Its platform is built on the regulatory CD8 T cell (CD8 Treg) network — an upstream immune checkpoint that normally recognizes and eliminates the pathogenic immune cells that attack healthy tissue, and that becomes dysfunctional in autoimmune disease when inhibitory killer immunoglobulin-like receptors (KIR) block CD8 Treg activation. Rather than suppressing downstream inflammation, Mozart engineers bispecific CD8 Treg modulators intended to restore that checkpoint and re-establish long-term immune balance. Its pipeline comprises MTX-101, a KIR x CD8 bispecific antibody in Phase 1b study for type 1 diabetes, and MTX-201, a KIR x ICOS bispecific in preclinical development for inflammatory bowel disease. The company launched with a $55M Series A led by ARCH Venture Partners and Sofinnova Partners with participation from Eli Lilly, MRL Ventures Fund, Leaps by Bayer, Altitude Life Science Ventures and Alexandria Venture Investments, and later added a $25M extension including Pfizer Ventures, AbbVie Ventures, Ono Venture Investment and UPMC Enterprises. Mozart Therapeutics sells therapeutics, not software: it runs no developer program, publishes no API, SDK or machine-readable specification, and maintains no public source-code organization.

providers.name: Nested Therapeutics
providers.description: Nested Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2021 and headquartered at 1030 Massachusetts Avenue in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It discovers and develops novel, targeted, small-molecule precision medicines for patients with cancers driven by the RAS-MAPK pathway, using mutation clusters to identify druggable pockets that conventional target discovery misses. Its lead program, NST-628, is a pan-RAF/MEK non-degrading molecular glue cleared by the FDA for investigation in advanced solid tumors carrying RAS-MAPK genetic alterations. The company was launched with $125 million in financing from Versant Ventures and the life sciences investment division of Goldman Sachs Asset Management. Nested Therapeutics is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes a two-page marketing website and press-release PDFs, and operates no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Neuron23
providers.description: Neuron23 is a clinical-stage precision-medicine biotechnology company developing genetically targeted small-molecule therapies for neurological and immunological diseases, with a lead precision-medicine program focused on Parkinson's disease. It combines machine-learning-driven genetic biomarker discovery with drug development to match patients to the therapies most likely to help them. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund, Neuron23 is a therapeutics company that publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: NextPoint Therapeutics
providers.description: NextPoint Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based at 238 Main Street in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing precision immuno-oncology therapeutics built on its scientific work on the novel B7-H7/HHLA2 checkpoint axis. Its pipeline includes a T-cell engager engineered for an improved therapeutic index, an antibody-drug conjugate using proprietary linker technology, and a multi-functional checkpoint inhibitor, each aimed at tumors that upregulate B7-H7. The company publishes a seven-page corporate marketing site covering its science, pipeline, leadership, and news; it operates no developer program, publishes no API, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and is profiled here for network completeness rather than for an API surface.

providers.name: Nilo Therapeutics
providers.description: Nilo Therapeutics is a New York-based, preclinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering a differentiated approach to immunomodulation by targeting the neural circuits that regulate systemic inflammation. Building on seminal discoveries from the laboratories of Charles Zuker (Columbia University / HHMI), Ruslan Medzhitov (Yale), and Stephen Liberles (Harvard) that identified vagal neurons regulating systemic immune activation, and led by CEO Kim Seth, the company harnesses the body-brain axis to restore immune homeostasis centrally, moving beyond conventional immunosuppression to treat autoimmune and inflammatory disease. Nilo launched in 2025 with a $101M Series A co-led by DCVC Bio, Lux Capital, and The Column Group, with participation from Alexandria Venture Investments and the Gates Foundation. As a therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Nimbus Therapeutics
providers.description: Nimbus Therapeutics is a Boston-based biotechnology company, founded in 2009, that designs and develops small molecule medicines with exquisite selectivity across oncology, immunology, and metabolic indications. Its approach integrates structure-based and computational drug design (including cloud-based molecular simulation) with target selection, translational medicine, and clinical development. Nimbus is a private, VC-backed drug-discovery company and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Novotech
providers.description: Novotech is a global full-service Contract Research Organization (CRO) that partners with biotech and pharmaceutical companies across every phase of clinical drug development. Its services span clinical operations and project management, patient recruitment and site selection, early-phase trials (notably in Australia), regulatory and medical consulting, biometrics and data management, site management organization (SMO), and laboratory services. Novotech reports 4,450+ trials conducted across 7,260+ trial sites in 50+ countries, supporting 60+ drugs to market. Added to the API Evangelist network as a healthcare portfolio company of Hongshan; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical integration surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Olema
providers.description: Olema Oncology is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Francisco with operations in Cambridge, Massachusetts, focused on developing targeted therapies for cancer. Founded in 2006, the company works in endocrine-driven cancers, nuclear receptors, and mechanisms of tumor drug resistance, with a stated goal of transforming the metastatic breast cancer treatment paradigm. Its investigational pipeline includes palazestrant (OP-1250), an oral complete estrogen receptor antagonist and selective estrogen receptor degrader advancing through the Phase 3 OPERA program, and OP-3136, a KAT6 inhibitor in Phase 1 clinical trials. Olema trades publicly on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker OLMA. As a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, Olema does not currently publish a developer-facing API, developer portal, SDKs, or public API documentation; this profile captures its corporate identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Orapharma
providers.description: Orapharma is a specialty pharmaceutical company and a division of Bausch Health focused on oral healthcare, developing and commercializing products that help dental professionals improve and maintain periodontal and oral health. Its portfolio includes Arestin (minocycline HCl microspheres for the treatment of periodontitis) and the OSSIX bone-grafting and regeneration products. Headquartered in Bridgewater, New Jersey, Orapharma partners with dental professionals across the continuum of care. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API or portal at this time.

providers.name: Orna Therapeutics
providers.description: Orna Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company, founded in 2019 on research from MIT and built by MPM Capital, that engineers circular RNA (oRNA) paired with lipid nanoparticle delivery so a patient's own body generates cell therapies — its lead program ORN-252 is a CD19-targeting in vivo CAR-T designed for B-cell-driven autoimmune disease. Orna acquired ReNAgade Therapeutics in 2024, combining its circular RNA platform with ReNAgade's LNP delivery and RNA editing capabilities, and Eli Lilly announced a definitive agreement to acquire Orna on 2026-02-09 for up to $2.4B. Orna is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract, and as of this profile its own domain ornatx.com redirects in whole to Eli Lilly's subsidiaries page.

providers.name: PillPack
providers.description: PillPack is a full-service mail-order pharmacy that sorts each customer's medications by date and time, packages them into clearly labeled dose packets, and delivers them monthly with automatic refill management. The service coordinates directly with prescribing doctors and insurance providers, charges no service fee (customers pay only for their medications), and holds URAC Mail Service Pharmacy accreditation with NCPDP E-Scribe capabilities out of Manchester, NH. Founded in 2013 and acquired by Amazon in 2018, PillPack is now operated by the same team of licensed pharmacists behind Amazon Pharmacy, which the site increasingly directs customers toward for same-day delivery and additional savings. PillPack is a consumer-facing pharmacy service with no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: PineTree Therapeutics
providers.description: Pinetree Therapeutics, Inc. is a preclinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered at West Cambridge Scientific Park, 767C Concord Ave, Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing next-generation targeted protein degraders (TPDs) built on its proprietary AbReptor platform. AbReptor degrades membrane-bound and extracellular proteins through target co-engagement, induced endocytosis, endolysosome formation and lysosomal degradation, aiming to overcome drug resistance and tumor recurrence in oncology, with additional application in inflammation and immunology. The company is advancing trispecific degraders and ADC-integrated programs, closed a $17M Series A in July 2024, and has entered a licensing partnership with AstraZeneca. It is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Pliant Therapeutics
providers.description: Pliant Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery and development of integrin-based therapies for underserved areas of medical need. Leveraging a proprietary integrin drug discovery and delivery platform, its lead program PLN-101095 is a dual-selective avb8/avb1 integrin inhibitor being evaluated in the FORTIFY clinical trial for patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors, alongside additional pipeline programs in fibrosis and oncology. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, Pliant Therapeutics publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface; this profile captures corporate identity and web presence only.

providers.name: Quanta Therapeutics
providers.description: Quanta Therapeutics is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2018 and headquartered at 2 Tower Place in South San Francisco, California, with a second site in Radnor, Pennsylvania. It develops oral allosteric small-molecule medicines for RAS-driven cancers by targeting the protein-protein interactions that drive oncogenic RAS signaling, an approach the company describes as conformational blockade of RAS. Its discovery engine is a proprietary high-throughput Second Harmonic Generation (SHG) optical platform that detects subtle protein conformational changes and so surfaces allosteric modulators of signaling complexes that conventional binding assays miss. The clinical pipeline is a set of direct multi-KRAS inhibitors: QTX3034, a G12D-preferring oral multi-KRAS inhibitor in Phase 1 as monotherapy and in combination with cetuximab in KRAS G12D-mutant solid tumors; QTX3544, a G12V-preferring multi-KRAS inhibitor cleared for IND in January 2025; and QTX3046, which dosed its first patient in a Phase 1/1b trial in June 2024. Indications span pancreatic, colorectal, lung and endometrial cancers. The company announced a $60 million Series C in October 2021 and a Series D of over $50 million in May 2023 led by Avidity Partners alongside Sofinnova Investments, Vida Ventures, Surveyor Capital, Longitude Capital and AbbVie Ventures. Quanta Therapeutics runs no developer program and publishes no public API. Its corporate site is a single static HTML document served from Apache with anchor-based sections; probes for OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, llms.txt and every /.well-known/ discovery path returned HTTP 404, and no api./developer./docs. subdomain resolves.

providers.name: RAPT Therapeutics
providers.description: RAPT Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing oral small-molecule and antibody therapies for patients with inflammatory, immunologic, and oncologic diseases. Its pipeline centers on ozureprubart, a long-acting anti-IgE antibody candidate in Phase 2 trials for food allergies, alongside programs targeting key drivers of immune response. The company was acquired by GSK in January 2026. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network; as a life-sciences therapeutics company it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Ritivel
providers.description: Ritivel is an AI-native regulatory and medical-writing platform for life sciences organizations, backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch). Its AI agents automate the drafting of regulatory submission documents such as Common Technical Documents (CTD), Clinical Study Reports (CSR), INDs, and BLAs, turning work that typically takes weeks into minutes. The platform generates comprehensive first drafts in Microsoft Word format that follow FDA and ICH requirements, with word-level traceability of every statement back to source documents, integrations with SharePoint, Veeva, and Outlook for document retrieval and follow-ups, a regulatory search over FDA and ICH guidelines, and a privacy posture built around local deployment with no cloud storage. It serves pharma, biotech, medtech, CROs, and CDMOs. Ritivel is an end-user application and does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

providers.name: Sayre Therapeutics
providers.description: Sayre Therapeutics is a healthcare company founded in 2015 that brings innovative treatments for rare, orphan, and life-threatening diseases to India and the broader SAARC region. It works across clinical research, regulatory strategy, and commercialization and market access, partnering with global licensors to bring US-, EU-, and Japan-approved drugs, drug-delivery devices, and diagnostics to South Asian markets under local regulatory standards. Its portfolio spans special-access and commercially approved products, diagnostics, biosimilars, and niche generics. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes no public developer portal, API, or technical documentation.

providers.name: SCIWIND
providers.description: Sciwind Biosciences (Hangzhou Sciwind Biosciences Co., Ltd.) is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Hangzhou, China, with a US office in San Ramon, California, focused on discovering, developing, and delivering innovative therapeutics for weight management and metabolic disease. Its pipeline spans obesity, type 2 diabetes, and non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), led by the GLP-1 receptor agonist Ecnoglutide (advancing through Phase III trials). The company operates proprietary drug-discovery platforms including BiasVantage (biased agonist discovery), OralVantage (oral peptide delivery), and HaleVantage (half-life extension), with 14+ pipeline programs, 120+ researchers, and 110+ patents. Surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found no public API or developer platform surface.

providers.name: Shasqi
providers.description: Shasqi is a clinical-stage biotechnology company advancing cancer treatment through click chemistry. Its CAPAC (Click Activated Protodrugs Against Cancer) platform uses a pre-targeting approach that captures therapeutic payloads at the tumor via in-vivo click chemistry, separating tumor-targeting molecules from their drug payloads and reuniting them at the cancer site to maximize drug delivery while reducing systemic toxicity. The company builds on the 2022 Nobel Prize-winning click chemistry work and operates as a therapeutics developer rather than a technology or API platform. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio company; enrichment found no public developer API, SDK, or technical platform surface.

providers.name: Sinotau
providers.description: Sinotau (先通医药) is a Chinese pharmaceutical innovator specializing in the research, development, production, clinical application, and academic promotion of radiopharmaceuticals (nuclear medicine). Formally established in 2014, the company focuses on three therapeutic areas — oncology, neurology, and cardiology — and has brought its first innovative product, 欧韦宁 (Florbetaben Fluorine-18 injection for PET brain imaging), to market alongside a pipeline of 10+ products in development. Sinotau operates multiple R&D and production facilities, employs 400+ staff, and holds 80+ authorized patents. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. As a corporate radiopharmaceutical manufacturer, Sinotau publishes a corporate marketing website but no public developer platform, API, or technical documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: SpyBiotech
providers.description: SpyBiotech is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation vaccines against infectious diseases and cancer using its proprietary SpyTag/SpyCatcher "protein superglue" platform. The technology snaps target antigens onto virus-like particles (VLPs) to produce highly immunogenic vaccines with greater ease and speed. An Oxford University spinout backed by GV, its pipeline includes candidates such as SpyVLP01 targeting human cytomegalovirus (hCMV). This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; SpyBiotech publishes a corporate marketing website but no public developer or product API surface.

providers.name: SURGE Therapeutics
providers.description: SURGE Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing intraoperative cancer immunotherapy. Founded on research from Dr. Michael Goldberg's laboratory at Harvard Medical School, the company's SURGERx platform is an injectable, biodegradable hydrogel placed directly at the site of surgical tumor resection to provide extended, localized release of immunotherapy — addressing the surgery-induced inflammation that suppresses the immune system and allows residual disease to reawaken. Its lead program, SRG-514, completed Phase 1 dose escalation in breast cancer patients undergoing surgery and is being prepared for a registrational trial, with an additional IND cleared for a Phase 1/2a study in bladder cancer. SURGE has raised a $26M Series A and a $32M Series B. It is a therapeutics developer, not a software company, and publishes no developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Syremis Therapeutics
providers.description: Syremis Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Tel Aviv, Israel and Boston, Massachusetts, developing best-in-class oral small-molecule medicines for serious mental health conditions. Its neuropsychiatric pipeline is rooted in clinically validated mechanisms including muscarinic M1/M4 agonism and next-generation NMDA antagonism; lead program ST-905 is a dual M1/M4 agonist in Phase 1 for schizophrenia, with ST-901 also spun out from Clexio Biosciences. The company launched publicly in December 2025 with a $165M Series A co-led by Dexcel Pharma and Third Rock Ventures, with participation from Bain Capital Life Sciences, GV (Google Ventures), QVT, and Pictet. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of GV. This company publishes no public API, developer, or event surface at this time.

Its lead program, TSHA-102, targets Rett syndrome and has completed dosing in the REVEAL pivotal trial. The company operates as a therapeutics developer and publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or technical integration surface; it was surfaced as a GV portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: Tokaido Health
providers.description: Tokaido Health is an AI-native medication steerage platform anchored in behavioral economics that helps employers and health plans cut pharmacy costs. It identifies same-or-better medications that cost less - via site-of-care steerage, biosimilar substitution, formulary optimization, and polypharmacy reconciliation - and pairs recommendations with incentives that get members to switch, layering on top of the existing PBM and benefits stack. Founded in 2025 in San Mateo, CA; raised $25M in May 2026 led by Norwest Venture Partners. No public API surface is published.

providers.name: Verve Therapeutics
providers.description: Verve Therapeutics is a Boston-based clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a pipeline of in vivo gene editing medicines designed to treat cardiovascular disease with a single, one-time treatment. Its programs use base editing and CRISPR technology to durably switch off disease-driving genes, led by VERVE-102 (targeting PCSK9 to lower LDL cholesterol), alongside VERVE-201 (ANGPTL3) and VERVE-301 (LPA). Verve was acquired by Eli Lilly in July 2025 in a deal worth up to $1.3 billion. As a therapeutics/research company it publishes no public developer API; this profile is maintained as a company identity record in the API Evangelist network. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of GV.

providers.name: Vicinitas Therapeutics
providers.description: Vicinitas Therapeutics is a biotechnology company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. It operates in the therapeutics and drug-discovery space (vicinitastx.com) and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface. This profile records what is verifiable about the company and remains a lead awaiting any future API footprint.

providers.name: Vir Biotechnology
providers.description: Vir Biotechnology is a clinical-stage immunology company that engineers antibodies into medicines targeting serious infectious diseases and cancer. Its programs span chronic hepatitis delta, hepatitis B, oncology, and prior work on COVID-19 and Ebola, built on a next-generation antibody platform and the licensed PRO-XTEN protease-releasable masking technology. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network. This is a corporate/investor-facing life-sciences company; enrichment probes found no public developer, API, or partner-integration surface.

providers.name: Visterra
providers.description: Visterra is a Waltham, Massachusetts biologics research company developing antibody-based therapeutics for patients with immune-mediated and other difficult-to-treat diseases. It combines computational design, artificial intelligence, and experimental research with agile preclinical development and manufacturing. Visterra publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company tracking and enrichment.

providers.name: Waltz Health
providers.description: Waltz Health is a Chicago-based digital health company founded in 2021 by Mark Thierer (former CEO of OptumRx and Catamaran) and Jonathon Thierer, building AI-driven prescription drug pricing marketplaces that help consumers, payers, pharmacy benefit managers, pharmacies, and self-insured employers make better-informed, lower-cost decisions on prescription care. Its Marketplace Search product is a multi-card search engine that compares medication prices across every major discount and savings program, and Waltz Connect is an end-to-end solution that lowers the cost of specialty medications through a network of national and regional specialty pharmacies that compete on price and clinical outcomes. The company raised a $35M Series A led by GV and, in August 2025, merged with EVERSANA to form a combined pharmaceutical commercialization and drug-access platform, with Mark Thierer appointed CEO of EVERSANA. Waltz Health has no public developer API program; this profile captures company identity and live domain-security posture.

providers.name: Zenasbio
providers.description: Zenas BioPharma is a global clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and delivering transformative treatments for patients with autoimmune and rare diseases. Its lead candidates are obexelimab, a bifunctional monoclonal antibody that inhibits B-cell activity without depleting B cells, and orelabrutinib, an oral central-nervous-system-penetrant BTK inhibitor. The company serves patients, caregivers, investors, and job seekers through its corporate website; it publishes no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or technical integration surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners.

providers.name: Dvlp Medicines
providers.description: DVLP Medicines is a drug-development software company building an end-to-end, configurable platform that moves molecules from discovery to commercialization with speed. The platform pairs a single data repository for pharmaceutical assets with specialized AI agents for pharma operations, document automation, knowledge synthesis, and decision support for portfolio management. It is positioned as a software co-pilot for drug development and a marketplace connecting project leaders with investors and outsourced R&D and manufacturing vendors, targeting underserved therapeutic markets such as new antibiotics for antimicrobial resistance and rare-disease therapies. DVLP Medicines is a portfolio company of DCVC (Computational Bio & Chem), first funded in 2022. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; the company publishes a marketing site but no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Eli Lilly
providers.description: Eli Lilly and Company is a Fortune 500 global pharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells human pharmaceutical products in therapeutic areas including diabetes, oncology, immunology, and neuroscience. Eli Lilly does not currently publish a public developer API portal; the company exposes selected machine learning models through its Lilly TuneLab platform to partner biotechs but does not offer general purpose, self-serve APIs.

providers.name: 1200 Pharma
providers.description: 1200 Pharma LLC is a privately held pre-clinical drug discovery company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Culver City, California, with roots in Pasadena. It was launched by Caltech chemist Brian Stoltz, UCLA translational oncologist Dennis Slamon and chief executive David Licata, and it pairs Caltech medicinal-chemistry methodology with UCLA biomarker-driven screening assays to identify novel small-molecule oncology candidates — including KRAS and CDK inhibitors — at a fraction of the industry-average cost and timeline. The company employs roughly 20-50 people, has filed patents covering indole-based anti-cancer compounds, and has raised approximately $14.1 million from Kairos Ventures, Vest Coast Capital, OCV Partners, Alexandria Venture Investments, Pasadena Bio and the National Institutes of Health. Its product is drug intellectual property and discovery partnerships, not software: no developer program, public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind could be found, and no api/docs/developer hostname exists under its domain. At the time of profiling its only web property, 1200pharma.com, was not being served — the Cloudflare edge in front of it terminated every TLS handshake and answered plain HTTP with error 1001 — so the corporate site itself could not be read.

providers.name: Abdera Therapeutics
providers.description: Abdera Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in South San Francisco, California, with research operations in Vancouver, British Columbia. It was launched in 2021 out of adMare BioInnovations with AbCellera as a founding partner and has raised roughly $148 million from investors including Versant Ventures, Foresite Capital, Johnson & Johnson Innovation (JJDC), Qiming Venture Partners USA, RTW Investments and venBio. The company engineers precision radiopharmaceuticals for solid tumours on its proprietary Radio Optimized Vector Engineering (ROVEr) platform, which pairs antibody-derived targeting vectors with potent alpha-emitting radioisotopes such as actinium-225. Its lead candidate, ABD-147, targets delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3) and is in a Phase 1 trial (NCT06736418) in small cell lung cancer and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma under FDA Fast Track designation; a second program, ABD-320, targets 5T4. Abdera's product is a drug candidate, not software. It runs no developer program and publishes no API, developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind. As of 2026-09-06 the company's own corporate site at www.abderatx.com was additionally unreachable, returning a Flywheel "Unknown Domain" host error on every path behind a TLS certificate that expired on 2026-07-19.

providers.name: ACELYRIN, Inc.
providers.description: ACELYRIN, Inc. (Nasdaq: SLRN) was a late-stage clinical biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Agoura Hills, California, focused on accelerating the development and commercialization of medicines in immunology. Its lead candidates were izokibep, an anti-IL-17A small protein therapeutic, and lonigutamab, a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody against IGF-1R. It completed a $540M IPO in May 2023, and on May 21, 2025 it merged with a subsidiary of Alumis, Inc. and survives as a wholly owned Alumis subsidiary. Its corporate domain acelyrin.com now 301-redirects to alumis.com. The company is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it published no developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface, or machine-readable specification, and no GitHub organization exists under the ACELYRIN name.

providers.name: ADEL, Inc.
providers.description: ADEL, Inc. (주식회사 아델) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Seoul, South Korea, founded in 2016 as a spin-off from the Asan Medical Center / University of Ulsan College of Medicine by Professor Seung-Yong Yoon. ADEL develops antibody therapeutics, companion diagnostics and delivery platforms for Alzheimer's disease and other neurodegenerative conditions. Its lead candidate ADEL-Y01 is a humanized monoclonal antibody selectively targeting tau acetylated at Lysine-280 (acK280), in a global first-in-human Phase 1 study under a US FDA-cleared IND; in December 2025 ADEL granted Sanofi exclusive worldwide rights to ADEL-Y01 in a deal worth up to USD 1.04 billion including an USD 80 million upfront payment. The wider pipeline includes ADEL-Y03 (a beta-2 microglobulin antibody), ADEL-Y04 (an ApoE4-targeting antibody), the ADEL-D01 tau pT217 diagnostic antibody, and two proprietary platforms — BTS (Brain Targeting System) for blood-brain-barrier penetration and ADTAC (Autophagic Degradation Targeting Chimera) for targeted protein degradation. The company is research-and-development driven and sells no software product: it publishes no developer portal, public API, SDK, webhook catalog or machine-readable specification of any kind. Its only web surface is the corporate marketing site at adelpharm.com.

providers.name: Arthrosi Therapeutics
providers.description: Arthrosi Therapeutics, Inc. is a late-stage clinical biotechnology company founded in 2018 and headquartered in San Diego, California, by a team of gout specialists who previously led first-generation urate-transporter development at Ardea Biosciences. Its lead candidate, pozdeutinurad (AR882), is a once-daily oral next-generation URAT1 inhibitor in two fully enrolled replicate global Phase 3 trials (REDUCE 1 and REDUCE 2) for progressive and tophaceous gout, backed by roughly $299M in venture financing including a $153M Series E led by Prime Eight Capital. Sobi (Swedish Orphan Biovitrum) completed its acquisition of Arthrosi on 9 February 2026. Arthrosi is a drug developer, not a software company: it operates a WordPress corporate site with company, leadership and news pages, and publishes no developer portal, public API, SDK, package or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Bambusa Therapeutics
providers.description: Bambusa Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in the Boston Seaport, founded in 2024 by Shanshan Xu and Helmut Jeggle to develop next-generation bispecific antibodies for immunological and inflammatory (I&I) diseases. Its antibody-engineering platform combines half-life extension with high-concentration subcutaneous delivery, and its pipeline spans dermatology, respiratory, gastroenterology and rheumatology — led by BBT-001 (IL-31 x IL-4Ralpha, in a Phase 1b/2a atopic dermatitis trial) and BBT-002 for COPD. The company raised a Series Seed in 2024, an approximately $90M Series A led by RA Capital Management in February 2025, and an oversubscribed Series A-2 in November 2025. It is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor, and publishes no public API, SDK or developer program.

providers.name: Entact Bio
providers.description: Entact Bio is a preclinical-stage biotechnology company based in Watertown, Massachusetts, developing a new class of small-molecule precision medicines called Enhancement-Targeting Chimeric (ENTAC) molecules. Where targeted protein degradation removes disease-causing proteins, Entact Bio works in the opposite direction: its ENTAC molecules recruit deubiquitinases (DUBs) to strip ubiquitin chains from beneficial proteins in order to extend their half-life, relocate them, or otherwise restore their function. The company's proprietary Encompass platform combines biological, chemical, and computational tools to identify disease targets amenable to protein enhancement across oncology, autoimmune disease, and rare genetic disorders. Entact Bio launched in December 2022 with an $81 million Series A co-led by Qiming Venture Partners USA and venBio Partners, with participation from Abingworth, Brandon Capital, and others. It is a therapeutics research organization and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Faraday Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Faraday Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was a Seattle, Washington clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2014 as a spinout of Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, built on the elemental-reducing-agent research of Dr. Mark Roth. It developed therapies intended to prevent and treat cardiac and skeletal muscle loss after acute critical illness, led by FDY-5301 — a proprietary intravenous formulation of sodium iodide designed to neutralize reactive oxygen species and limit reperfusion injury in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention for anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The company raised roughly $120M from an investor group led by ARCH Venture Partners and Polaris Partners. Its Phase 3 trial read out in late 2025 and failed to meet its primary or secondary endpoints, and Faraday announced in February 2026 that it had ceased operations and was winding down the business. Faraday never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and its faradaypharma.com website is no longer served. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Henry Schein
providers.description: Henry Schein is a worldwide distributor of medical and dental supplies including vaccines, pharmaceuticals, financial services and equipment.

providers.name: Korro Bio
providers.description: Korro Bio, Inc. (Nasdaq: KRRO) is a Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing a new class of genetic medicines based on programmable RNA editing. Its proprietary OPERA (Oligonucleotide Promoted Editing of RNA) platform pairs data-driven oligonucleotide design and machine-learning optimization with linker chemistry and tissue-directed delivery to recruit the body's own ADAR enzymes and make a precise, transient single-base edit to a native mRNA transcript — editing RNA rather than DNA so the change is tunable and reversible. The company was created and incubated by Atlas Venture with New Enterprise Associates in October 2019, raised a $91.5M Series A and a $116M Series B, and became public in 2023 through a merger with Frequency Therapeutics alongside a $117M private placement. Its pipeline targets liver and central nervous system indications and includes KRRO-110 (the REWRITE Phase 1/2a study in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency), KRRO-111 and KRRO-121, which holds EMA orphan drug designation for urea cycle disorders. Korro Bio sells therapeutics, not software: it operates no developer program, publishes no API, SDK or machine-readable specification, and maintains no public source-code organization.

providers.name: Latigo Bio
providers.description: Latigo Biotherapeutics, Inc. ("Latigo Bio") is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Thousand Oaks, California, developing novel non-opioid medicines for acute and chronic pain. Its lead candidates LTG-001 and LTG-321 are oral NaV1.8 sodium-channel inhibitors targeting pain at its peripheral source without the addiction risk of opioids; LTG-001 holds FDA Fast Track designation and reported positive Phase 2b results in post-abdominoplasty acute pain, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in July 2026. The company was founded on human-genetics-validated targets and uses in-house AI/ML and structure-based drug design to optimize potency and selectivity. It debuted in 2024 with a $135M Series A and closed a $150M Series B in March 2025, backed by Westlake Village BioPartners, 5AM Ventures, Foresite Capital and Corner Ventures. Latigo is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.
