providers.name: Myrtelle
providers.description: Myrtelle, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Wakefield, Massachusetts, developing gene therapies for myelin-based disorders of the central nervous system. Its lead program, MYR-101 (rAAV-Olig001-ASPA), is a first-in-class oligotrophic recombinant adeno-associated virus gene therapy for Canavan disease, a rare and fatal childhood genetic brain disease caused by mutations in the ASPA gene. The program is licensed exclusively worldwide from Pfizer Inc., holds Orphan Drug, Fast Track and Rare Pediatric Disease designations in the US with similar designations in Europe, and has reported Phase 1/2 interim results in Nature Medicine. Myrtelle is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable API contract, and is profiled here for network completeness only.

providers.name: Pfizer
providers.description: Pfizer is a Fortune 500 American multinational pharmaceutical and biotechnology corporation that researches, develops, and manufactures medicines and vaccines for a wide range of medical disciplines.

providers.name: SCG Cell Therapy
providers.description: SCG Cell Therapy Pte. Ltd. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Singapore, with operations across Singapore, China and Germany, developing novel immunotherapies for infectious diseases and the cancers they cause. The company targets the most common cancer-causing infections — Helicobacter pylori, human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) — and is advancing a pipeline of TCR-engineered T cell therapies, antibodies and therapeutic vaccines built on its proprietary GianTCR platform. Lead programs include SCG101, a first-in-class autologous HBV-specific TCR-T therapy targeting hepatitis B surface antigen in HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma, and SCG142, a next-generation HPV E7-specific TCR-T therapy for HPV-associated solid tumors that received FDA IND clearance. SCG covers the full value chain from drug discovery and manufacturing through clinical development and commercialization. It is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor, and publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Selkirk Pharma
providers.description: Selkirk Pharma, Inc. is a privately held U.S. contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) in Spokane, Washington, specializing in the aseptic fill/finish of sterile injectable drug products — vaccines, biologics and small molecules — for clinical and commercial supply. Founded in 2018, it operates a purpose-built aseptic campus at 9110 W Granite Avenue in the Pacific Northwest Technology Park, roughly half a mile from Spokane International Airport, running unidirectional personnel and material flow, single-use systems, SKAN isolator technology and Bausch+Strobel VarioSys dose-filling lines rated to about 3,600 vials per hour under EU GMP Annex 1. Services span aseptic filling, in-house analytical chemistry and microbiology, sterility testing, finished-product inspection, regulatory support and supply-chain services, plus a ClinFAST program that compresses fill/finish timelines for clinical-trial material. The build-out drew roughly $150M led by Spokane's Cowles Company with other Washington State investors, and Colleen Dixon was named chief executive in July 2024. Selkirk Pharma sells contract manufacturing capacity, not software: it operates no developer program, publishes no web API, SDK or machine-readable specification, and maintains no public source-code organization. (In this sector "API" ordinarily means active pharmaceutical ingredient; Selkirk fills and finishes drug product and publishes no web API.)

providers.name: Shoreline Biosciences
providers.description: Shoreline Biosciences was a San Diego, California clinical-stage biotechnology company developing off-the-shelf, allogeneic cell therapies from induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), principally iPSC-derived natural killer (iNK) cells and macrophages engineered for oncology indications. It raised roughly $140M, acquired Editas Medicine's iNK cell franchise and related gene-editing technologies in 2023, and signed collaborations with Kite Pharma (Gilead) and BeiGene with headline values above $4B. Therapeutics, not software, were the product: no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification was ever published. As of this profiling pass the company's own domain, shorelinebio.com, no longer serves a website — it answers HTTP 404 with a Squarespace "Website Expired" holding page — and the company is tracked here only as a secondary-market entity.

providers.name: Vita Therapeutics
providers.description: Vita Therapeutics is a Baltimore, Maryland cell engineering company, spun out of Johns Hopkins University in 2019 and formally founded in 2020, that develops induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) derived cellular therapies for neuromuscular disease and solid tumors. Its programs pair an autologous approach with an allogeneic, universal hypoimmunogenic approach, and include VTA-100 and VTA-110 for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy and related muscular dystrophies such as FSHD. The company raised a $31M Series B led by Cambrian BioPharma and Solve FSHD and operates from the University of Maryland BioPark. It is a clinical-stage biotechnology company: it sells no software, runs no developer program, and publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Zurex Pharma
providers.description: Zurex Pharma, Inc. is a privately held specialty pharmaceutical and medical technology company founded in 2008 and headquartered in Middleton, Wisconsin, developing a portfolio of patented antimicrobial formulations intended to prevent healthcare-acquired infections. Its products are physical, regulated goods rather than software: ZuraPrep, a single-use pre-surgical skin antiseptic submitted to the FDA as NDA 210872 in June 2018; ZuraGard for peri-operative and catheter exit-site antisepsis; ZurAsept, a catheter lock solution; and ZuraLac, a teat sanitizer for dairy cattle. Backed by Baird Venture Partners, the State of Wisconsin Investment Board, Peak Ridge Capital and Wisconsin Investment Partners. The company publishes no developer program, no API and no machine-readable API artifacts of any kind, and as of this pass its own domain serves no website.

providers.name: General Proximity
providers.description: General Proximity is a biotechnology company pioneering next-generation "proximity medicines" that control biological processes by inducing proximity between molecular targets. Its multi-target OMNITAC platform is used to discover and advance novel therapeutics, including an oncology collaboration with Daiichi Sankyo. The company is backed by investors including Felicis and Y Combinator, and has drawn investment from Freemind and Daewoong Pharmaceutical. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; General Proximity is a drug-discovery company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time.

providers.name: IMS Health Holdings
providers.description: IMS Health Holdings was a leading global information and technology services company providing clients in the healthcare industry with end-to-end solutions before merging with Quintiles in 2016 to form IQVIA. No standalone public API is offered under the IMS Health Holdings brand; current API and data products are available through IQVIA.

providers.name: Medly Pharmacy
providers.description: Medly Pharmacy (Medly Health Inc.) was a Brooklyn, New York digital pharmacy founded in 2017 by Marg Patel, a second-generation pharmacist. It operated a hybrid model — physical retail pharmacy locations paired with free same-day prescription delivery — supported by a consumer mobile app for refills, prescription status and pharmacist chat, and a prescriber-facing e-prescribing workflow it marketed to physician practices. The company raised a $100M Series B in July 2020, expanded into several US metros, and in 2021 acquired the health-and-wellness retailer Pharmaca. It never published a developer program, public API, SDK, machine-readable specification or partner integration reference; the platform was an internal product, not a product sold to developers. Medly Health filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on 9 December 2022 along with 31 affiliates, agreed on 9 February 2023 to sell its remaining prescription files, inventory and intellectual property to Walgreens for $19.35M, wound down all retail and e-commerce operations by 31 March 2023, and converted to a Chapter 7 liquidation on 26 April 2023. In September 2024 the SEC charged three former executives, including the founder, in connection with the company's capital raises. The medly.com domain is now controlled by the acquirer and blanket-redirects every path to walgreens.com. What survives publicly is the company's engineering open source — the GitHub `medly` organization and its npm and Maven Central packages — none of which is an API client. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: PRA Health Sciences
providers.description: PRA Health Sciences was a global contract research organization (CRO) headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina, providing outsourced clinical development services to pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies. On July 1, 2021 ICON plc completed its acquisition of PRA Health Sciences in a cash-and-stock transaction valued at approximately $12 billion, forming one of the world's largest healthcare research organizations. Following the acquisition the PRA Health Sciences brand has been fully retired and operations were merged into ICON. The legacy prahs.com domain redirects to iconplc.com / icongroup.com and no PRA-branded developer programs, public APIs, SDKs, or technical documentation remain.

providers.name: Vineti
providers.description: Vineti was an enterprise software company for cell and gene therapy supply chain management, headquartered in San Francisco and founded in 2016. Its Personalized Therapy Management (PTM) platform — sold as PTM Enterprise and PTM Essentials — orchestrated the patient-centric supply chain behind autologous and allogeneic cell therapies, gene therapies and personalized cancer vaccines: chain of identity, chain of custody, apheresis and manufacturing scheduling, clinical-site workflows, and regulatory reporting. PTM was delivered as a configurable aPaaS on AWS, with HIPAA compliance certified by Avertium and GAMP-aligned validation. Vineti was named a World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer and raised a $35M Series C in 2020. The PTM software was acquired by Johnson & Johnson in 2023 to continue supporting its commercial therapy rollouts and clinical trials, and Vineti ceased to operate as an independent company: vineti.com no longer resolves and the domain now sits on Johnson & Johnson name servers. This profile is retained as a historical record — there is no live API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Gilead Sciences
providers.description: Gilead Sciences is a research-based biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, and commercializes innovative therapeutics in areas of unmet medical need including HIV, viral hepatitis, oncology, and inflammatory diseases.

providers.name: Hospira
providers.description: Hospira was a global specialty pharmaceutical and medication delivery company providing injectable drugs and infusion technologies before being acquired by Pfizer in 2015. No public APIs are offered under the Hospira brand.

providers.name: Janssen Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Janssen Pharmaceuticals was a Belgian pharmaceutical company founded in 1953 by Paul Janssen and acquired by Johnson & Johnson in 1961. The company specialized in psychiatry, neurology, oncology, immunology, and infectious disease medicines, developing approximately 70 new active pharmaceutical substances over its history. In 2024 the Janssen brand was retired and the pharmaceutical operations were rebranded as Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine. As such, Janssen no longer operates as a standalone brand and does not maintain its own public APIs.

providers.name: Omnicare
providers.description: Omnicare is a long-term care pharmacy services company providing pharmacy services to long-term care facilities, senior living communities, and other healthcare providers. Customer-facing portals (Omniview, MyOmniview) exist for clients but no public developer APIs have been documented at this time.

providers.name: yuanxinjituan
providers.description: Yuanxinjituan (Beijing Yuanxin Technology Group Co., Ltd. / 圆心科技集团) is a Chinese healthcare-technology company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Beijing, dedicated to delivering value across the full patient care cycle. It operates an integrated online-and-offline platform spanning three core scenarios — medical consultation, medication, and payment — connecting doctors, patients, pharmaceutical companies, and insurers. Its businesses include the Miaoshou (妙手) internet hospital, hospital-side and DTP pharmacies (圆心药房), a prescription-sharing platform, pharmaceutical distribution, and the Yuanxin health-insurance arm (圆心惠保). Backed by Tencent, Sequoia China, and Qiming Venture Partners, Yuanxin is one of China's largest full-chain service providers for the commercialization of innovative drugs and has pursued a Hong Kong Stock Exchange main-board listing. The company presents a consumer/enterprise healthcare surface; no public developer API, open platform, or documentation was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Acesion Pharma
providers.description: Acesion Pharma is a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company based in Frederiksberg, Denmark, developing novel therapies for atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common cardiac arrhythmia. The company pioneers small-molecule SK ion channel inhibition as a differentiated mechanism to treat AF safely and effectively. Its lead program AP31969 entered Phase 2 clinical trials in January 2026, building on earlier work on the cardioversion candidate AP30663. Acesion Pharma is backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners. As a pharmaceutical R&D company it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation; this profile captures its corporate identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Ai Vivo
providers.description: AI VIVO (AIVIVO LTD) is a Cambridge, England based drug-discovery company that combines systems pharmacology with artificial intelligence to accelerate the identification and de-risking of therapeutic candidates. Its "Organome" platform simulates biological processes at the target, cell, organ, and organism levels and ranks drug candidates by their phenotypic effects at the tissue level, without relying on prior knowledge of the disease or compounds. The approach gained recognition in 2020 when the platform ranked roughly 90,000 compounds for COVID-19 and surfaced dexamethasone as a top candidate weeks before its clinical benefit was widely reported. AI VIVO is backed by DCVC and other life-science and applied-AI investors. As of this profile the company publishes a minimal public web presence (a home and contact page) and exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK.

providers.name: ARMO BioSciences *
providers.description: ARMO BioSciences was a clinical-stage immuno-oncology biopharmaceutical company based in Redwood City, California, developing biologic therapeutics that activate a patient's own immune system to fight cancer. Its lead candidate was pegilodecakin (AM0010), a PEGylated recombinant human interleukin-10 (IL-10) evaluated across solid tumors. Backed by GV and Kleiner Perkins, the company IPO'd on NASDAQ in 2018 and was acquired by Eli Lilly and Company that same year for approximately $1.6 billion; its former web domain now redirects to lilly.com. As a life-sciences therapeutics developer it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio/acquisition record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Arsanis *
providers.description: Arsanis was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in the life-sciences sector, focused on developing monoclonal antibody immunotherapies to prevent and treat serious infectious diseases. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network as a company stub. Arsanis operated as a therapeutics developer rather than a software or API provider, and the company no longer exists as an independent entity; its public web presence at arsanis.com is no longer served. This profile is retained as a portfolio-graph lead with no active developer, API, or documentation surface to enrich.

providers.name: Babylon Bio
providers.description: Babylon Bio (Babylon Biosciences) is a San Francisco-based drug discovery and development company founded in 2023 and backed by Lux Capital. Staffed by experienced medicinal chemists and biologists with a track record of discovering FDA-approved medicines, the company develops therapeutics that rescue essential functions in the brain rather than clearing emergent pathology, leveraging a proprietary high-throughput assay platform with an early focus on neurodegenerative disease including Alzheimer's. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As a private, pre-commercial biotech it publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Bestcomm
providers.description: Bestcomm (Bestcomm Pharmaceutical) is a China-based pharmaceutical company backed by IDG Capital, surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. It operates in the healthcare / life-sciences sector and raised venture funding alongside IDG Capital and regional investors. As a pharmaceutical manufacturer it has no known public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or programmatic API surface; this profile remains a company lead rather than an API provider. It is distinct from the unrelated BestComm Networks wireless-LAN company.

providers.name: Bipar Sciences
providers.description: BiPar Sciences was a Brisbane, California biopharmaceutical company developing a tumor-selective class of PARP (poly ADP-ribose polymerase) inhibitors for cancer therapy. Its lead candidate, BSI-201 (iniparib), was in mid-stage trials for advanced breast, ovarian, and other tumors. Backed by Canaan Partners, Vulcan Capital, PolyTechnos, Asset Management Company, and Quantum Technology Partners, BiPar was acquired by Sanofi-Aventis for roughly $500 million in April 2009 and no longer operates as an independent company. It was surfaced as a Canaan Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment finds no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Calixa Therapeutics
providers.description: Calixa Therapeutics was a privately held, San Diego-based biopharmaceutical company focused on developing antibiotics to treat serious infections caused by multi-drug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial pathogens. Its lead compound, CXA-201 (later ceftolozane/tazobactam), was an intravenous therapy for serious hospital-acquired Gram-negative infections. Calixa was acquired by Cubist Pharmaceuticals in December 2009 for approximately $92.5 million (plus up to $310 million in milestone payments) and no longer operates as an independent company. It has no public developer or API surface. This profile exists in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub associated with canaan-partners; there are no API artifacts to enrich because it is a defunct pharmaceutical company, not an API provider.

providers.name: Cell Pathways
providers.description: Cell Pathways, Inc. (CPI) was a development-stage pharmaceutical company headquartered at 702 Electronic Drive, Horsham, Pennsylvania, focused on the research and development of products to treat and prevent cancer. Incorporated in Delaware in July 1998 (as Cell Pathways Holdings, Inc., renamed Cell Pathways, Inc. in February 2001), it developed a class of compounds it called selective apoptotic anti-neoplastic drugs (SAANDs), designed to induce selective apoptosis — programmed cell death — in precancerous and cancerous cells without affecting normal cells. Its lead candidate was Aptosyn (exisulind), studied in precancerous lesions such as colonic polyps and cervical dysplasia and later in prostate, lung, and breast cancer; the company also imported, promoted, and sold Gelclair Concentrated Oral Gel into oncology and dental markets, and had previously marketed Nilandron. It traded on the Nasdaq National Market (Commission File No. 000-24889) and employed approximately 34 people full-time as of March 1, 2003. In February 2003 Cell Pathways signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger to be acquired by OSI Pharmaceuticals, Inc. in a stock-for-stock exchange; stockholders approved the merger on June 10, 2003, and the company filed a Form 15-12G on June 12, 2003 terminating its Exchange Act registration with one holder of record. OSI Pharmaceuticals was itself acquired by Astellas Pharma and deregistered on June 18, 2010. Cell Pathways predates the API economy entirely, never operated a developer program or public API surface, and no longer exists as an operating entity. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Civitas Therapeutics
providers.description: Civitas Therapeutics was a privately held biopharmaceutical company founded in 2009 (Chelsea/Cambridge, Massachusetts) that developed inhaled therapeutics using the proprietary ARCUS dry-powder pulmonary delivery platform. Its lead program, CVT-301, was an inhaled levodopa therapy for the rapid relief of OFF episodes in Parkinson's disease patients. The company was acquired by Acorda Therapeutics in 2014 for approximately $525 million and no longer operates as an independent entity. It is a life-sciences / drug-development company with no public developer platform, API, SDK, or technical integration surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and retained in the API Evangelist network for provenance.

providers.name: Combinatorx
providers.description: CombinatoRx, Inc. was a Cambridge/Boston, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company (SEC CIK 0001135906, SIC 2834 Pharmaceutical Preparations, incorporated in Delaware) that pursued combination drug discovery — screening pairs of approved drugs for synergistic therapeutic effects. It registered with the SEC in 2002 and traded publicly following its 2005 IPO. The company was renamed Zalicus Inc. in September 2010 after its combination with Neuromed Pharmaceuticals, and renamed again to EPIRUS Biopharmaceuticals, Inc. in July 2014 after merging with EPIRUS. EPIRUS was delisted in September 2016 (Form 25-NSE) and its SEC registration was formally revoked on 2024-05-14. The company is defunct: it operated no developer program and published no public API, SDK, or developer documentation, and combinatorx.com is now a parked NameBright listing unrelated to the original company. This profile is retained as a historical record of a Canaan Partners portfolio company and has no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Dermira
providers.description: Dermira was a biopharmaceutical company focused on medical dermatology, developing and commercializing treatments for chronic skin conditions such as primary axillary hyperhidrosis (Qbrexza / glycopyrronium) and atopic dermatitis (lebrikizumab). Headquartered in Menlo Park, California and originally backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners, the company went public on NASDAQ (DERM) in 2014 and was acquired by Eli Lilly and Company in 2020. Its assets and operations are now part of Eli Lilly; the dermira.com domain redirects to lilly.com. Dermira did not operate a public developer program, API, or developer portal, so this profile carries company identity only and has no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Durata Therapeutics
providers.description: Durata Therapeutics was a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company founded in 2009 around anti-infective assets acquired from Pfizer's Vicuron division, headquartered first in Morristown, New Jersey and from 2012 in Chicago, Illinois. Its lead candidate was dalbavancin, a long-acting semisynthetic lipoglycopeptide antibiotic taken into Phase III trials from 2011 for acute bacterial skin and skin-structure infections and later marketed as Dalvance. The company was backed by Canaan Partners and was acquired by Actavis (now Allergan) on November 17, 2014 for approximately $675 million, at which point it ceased to operate as an independent entity. Durata Therapeutics published no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API artifacts; its corporate domain duratatherapeutics.com no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Encoded Therapeutics
providers.description: Encoded Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing next-generation gene therapies for neurological disorders, translating precision genetic science into transformative genetic medicines. Its Genetic Medicines Product Engine supports a pipeline led by ETX101, an investigational AAV gene therapy for SCN1A-positive Dravet Syndrome, alongside additional research programs. Backed by GV, Menlo Ventures, and SoftBank Vision Fund, the company is added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences profile. As a clinical-stage therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity for the network.

providers.name: Envisia
providers.description: Envisia (Envisia Therapeutics, Inc.) was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina, spun out of Liquidia Technologies to apply PRINT (Particle Replication In Non-wetting Templates) particle-engineering to sustained-release ophthalmic therapeutics. Its lead candidate, ENV515 (travoprost) extended-release, was an intracameral implant intended to lower intraocular pressure in glaucoma patients for months from a single administration. The company was venture-backed by Canaan Partners, New Enterprise Associates, Morningside, and Batterson Venture Capital, and was acquired by Aerie Pharmaceuticals in October 2016. As a therapeutics company it exposes no public developer, API, or documentation surface, and its former web domains no longer resolve; this profile is retained as a VC-portfolio lead record with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Eon Laboratories
providers.description: Eon Laboratories is a pharmaceutical manufacturer that develops, manufactures, and markets a broad range of generic pharmaceutical products. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a generic-drug maker rather than a software or API producer, Eon Laboratories publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specifications, so this profile carries company identity only and no API artifacts. The record will be revisited if the company later exposes a developer or partner API surface.

providers.name: Flexus Biosciences
providers.description: Flexus Biosciences was a South San Francisco / San Carlos, California biotechnology company founded in 2013 to develop small-molecule cancer immunotherapies, most notably inhibitors of the IDO/TDO immunosuppressive pathway (lead IDO1 program F001287). Backed by Kleiner Perkins and The Column Group, it was acquired by Bristol-Myers Squibb in February 2015 for up to roughly $1.25 billion (about $800M upfront) to expand BMS's immuno-oncology pipeline. The company no longer operates independently; its domain redirects to the Bristol-Myers Squibb acquisition announcement. It publishes no public developer portal, documentation, or API, so this profile carries company identity only and no technical API artifacts.

providers.name: Halda Therapeutics
providers.description: Halda Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company and Yale University spinout developing oral, targeted cancer therapies built on its proprietary RIPTAC (Regulated Induced Proximity TArgeting Chimera) platform, a novel "hold and kill" modality for the precision treatment of solid tumors. Its lead program, HLD-0915, is a first-in-class oral RIPTAC therapeutic in development for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), with earlier-stage candidates spanning breast, lung, and other tumor types. Backed by investors including Canaan Partners, Halda was acquired by Johnson & Johnson in 2025 for approximately $3.05 billion in cash, with its platform folded into Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine's oncology pipeline. As a therapeutics developer, Halda operated no public developer platform, API, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity and portfolio-graph record rather than an API producer.

providers.name: i-Incubator Healthcare
providers.description: i-Incubator Healthcare is a pharmaceutical innovation incubator established by IDG Capital and officially launched in Shanghai (Xuhui District) in 2024. It operates an "incubation + empowerment" model to develop innovative drug-research programs across oncology, immunology, and metabolic disease areas, pairing global innovation perspectives with China-based execution to advance projects to international quality standards. It is backed by a dedicated, long-horizon (15-year) incubation fund. Surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital; this is a research/biotech venture with no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: IDEC Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: IDEC Pharmaceuticals is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: healthcare. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: immune-path
providers.description: Immune-Path (Yidao Biotechnology (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. / 怡道生物) is a China-based vaccine biotechnology company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Suzhou. The company develops human vaccines across recombinant protein antigen, novel viral vector, and messenger RNA (mRNA) platforms, backed by its own vaccine adjuvant technology. Its clinical and preclinical pipeline includes a recombinant zoster (shingles) vaccine produced in CHO cells, a nine-valent recombinant HPV vaccine expressed in Pichia pastoris, a respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine, a therapeutic gastric cancer vaccine, and a COVID-19 vaccine. Immune-Path is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It is a life-sciences drug developer with no public developer, API, or software surface; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kelun-Biotech
providers.description: Sichuan Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (Kelun Botai, HKEX: 6990), a Chengdu-based subsidiary of Sichuan Kelun Pharmaceutical (SZSE: 002422) established in 2016, is an innovative biopharmaceutical company focused on the research, development, manufacturing, and commercialization of novel drugs. It specializes in antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and other conjugated therapies across both large-molecule and small-molecule modalities, targeting oncology and autoimmune diseases. The company operates several core drug-discovery platforms and maintains a pipeline of 30+ candidates with multiple approved and clinical-stage programs. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network; as a pharmaceutical manufacturer it publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Legit Patents
providers.description: Legit (listed by Seedcamp as "Legit Patents", 2016 cohort, legit.ai) was a Cambridge, Massachusetts startup applying natural-language processing to scientific and patent literature, which it developed into an on-demand expert network for the life sciences. Its product let pharmaceutical, biotech and medical-device teams search a corpus the company described as more than two million experts backed by roughly forty million data points, then pay a flat fee per reply to message key opinion leaders directly instead of scheduling calls — marketed for R&D, business development and licensing (BD&L), strategic alliances and integration management. The company is no longer operating: substantive legit.ai content disappears from the web archive after 2021, its LinkedIn company page returns HTTP 404, and the legit.ai domain is now parked on GoDaddy/Afternic and listed for sale (Afternic nameservers, a null MX record and an SPF "-all" policy). No public API, developer portal, documentation or machine-readable specification was ever published; see review.yml for the full probe record.

providers.name: LongBio Pharma
providers.description: LongBio Pharma (Suzhou/Shanghai, founded 2020) is a Chinese clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the in-house discovery and development of innovative antibody and fusion-protein therapeutics for allergic, autoimmune, and complement-mediated diseases. Its lead programs include the anti-IgE antibody LP-003 for chronic spontaneous urticaria and asthma. Co-founded by Dr. Bill Nai-chau Sun (co-founder of Tanox and co-inventor of Omalizumab/Xolair), LongBio raised a Series B2 round led by Qiming Venture Partners and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (01779.HK) in June 2026. It is a pharmaceutical drug developer with no public developer or API surface; this profile was surfaced as a Qiming portfolio company and completed an enrichment pass.

providers.name: Matrix Pharmaceutical
providers.description: Matrix Pharmaceutical is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Medir
providers.description: Medir is a South Korean digital-health company behind Medb (메듭), a non-face-to-face (telemedicine) and prescription-drug delivery platform that connects patients, doctors, hospitals and pharmacies. Through the Medb mobile app, patients receive 100% video consultations with physicians and have their prescribed medications delivered to their door — often within roughly 30 minutes to two hours — with no separate service fee beyond the standard consultation charge. Medir is a portfolio company backed by 500 Global. The business operates as a consumer mobile application (iOS and Android) and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network pending any future API surface.

providers.name: Mendra
providers.description: Mendra is an AI-native biopharma company focused on developing breakthrough medicines for rare and ultra-rare pediatric diseases. It partners with R&D-stage biotech companies to accelerate clinical development and commercialization, handling regulatory, clinical, and reimbursement strategy while prioritizing the needs of patients and families. Founded by a team with experience from BioMarin, Palantir, and other pharma and biotech companies, Mendra launched with an $82 million Series A round and is backed by 8VC and Wing Venture Capital. The company operates a corporate marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Millennium Pharma
providers.description: Millennium Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company founded in 1993 in Cambridge, Massachusetts, that pioneered a genomics-based, platform approach to drug discovery and development. Backed early on by Mayfield, the company built its reputation on large research and development alliances with major pharmaceutical partners and on discovering and commercializing medicines for cancer and other diseases. Millennium was acquired by Takeda Pharmaceutical Company in 2008 and now operates as the Takeda Oncology unit. It is a therapeutics and drug-discovery organization, not an API or developer-platform provider, and exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Millennium Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Millennium Pharmaceuticals was a biopharmaceutical company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, focused on oncology and inflammation, best known for developing the cancer drug Velcade (bortezomib). Backed early by Kleiner Perkins, it was acquired by Takeda Pharmaceutical Company in 2008 for $8.8B and its brand was retired to "Takeda Oncology" in 2013; it no longer operates as an independent company. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio stub. This is a research/company profile with no independent developer API surface — the pipeline confirmed the provider publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or event/webhook surface.

providers.name: Minghui Pharmaceutical
providers.description: Minghui Pharmaceutical is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: healthcare. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Minova Pharma
providers.description: Nanjing Minova Pharmaceutical Technology Co., Ltd. (南京迈诺威医药科技有限公司) is a drug-discovery and pharmaceutical R&D company founded in February 2021 and headquartered in Nanjing, China. The company focuses on the discovery, development, and industrialization of novel drugs for mental diseases and disfiguring (cosmetic/dermatological) diseases, operating in the consumer-pharmaceutical space as both a drug R&D house and supplier. Its stated capabilities span early drug discovery, compound/drug screening, and druggability (developability) research. Surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Minova Pharma publishes a corporate marketing website but exposes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Mynvax
providers.description: Mynvax is a clinical-stage vaccine biotechnology company based in Bengaluru, India, developing recombinant, thermostable vaccines for respiratory viral infections. Spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), the company applies protein-stabilization and structure-based antigen design to create thermotolerant COVID-19 and influenza vaccine candidates aimed at affordable distribution in low- and lower-middle-income countries without deep cold-chain requirements. Mynvax is a life-sciences research company and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation portal, or technical integration surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and is maintained in the API Evangelist network for discovery.

providers.name: Neumora
providers.description: Neumora Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company pioneering a new era of precision medicines to restore brain health and wellbeing. It develops therapeutics for brain diseases and neuropsychiatric conditions, applying a precision-medicine approach to neuroscience drug discovery and development. Neumora was surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. As a therapeutics company it maintains a corporate and investor web presence but exposes no public developer API, SDK, CLI, or documentation surface: probing its domain for /.well-known/ discovery documents, an OpenAPI/Swagger spec, an llms.txt, and developer/docs paths returned no machine-readable API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Normunity
providers.description: Normunity is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel anti-cancer therapies that work at the interface of the immune system and the tumor. In collaboration with the Lieping Chen lab at the Yale School of Medicine, Normunity has identified a novel class of "Immuno-smart targets" — tumor-specific, cell-surface proteins co-opted by cancer cells to drive local immune suppression — and is building a pipeline of biologic medicines including therapeutic antibodies, bispecific antibodies, and payload-carrying biologics. Its lead program, NRM-823, is a T cell engager that has entered clinical trials. Normunity is backed by Canaan Partners. This is a corporate/scientific company with no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface.

providers.name: novamab
providers.description: Novamab (洛启生物) is a Shanghai-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company specializing in VHH (nanobody) antibody drug development for respiratory and inflammatory diseases such as asthma, COPD, and IBD. Its platforms span inhaled antibodies, oral antibodies, and dual/multi-specific antibodies alongside integrated drug formulation and manufacturing. Surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment confirmed the company publishes a corporate website but no developer API, documentation portal, SDKs, or other machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Novast Laboratories
providers.description: Novast Laboratories is a pharmaceutical development and manufacturing company (CDMO) headquartered in Nantong, Jiangsu Province, China, founded in 2005 by Dr. Guohua Zhang and a multinational management team. Novast specializes in high-barrier, difficult-to-formulate generic and specialty pharmaceuticals, including ultra-low-dose hormonal and extended- / modified-release oral products built on proprietary drug-delivery technologies. It is noted as one of the first China-based pharmaceutical companies to gain U.S. FDA approval for finished drug products marketed in the United States, and provides contract development and manufacturing services to generic and innovator companies. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Novast is a physical pharmaceutical manufacturer and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Novome
providers.description: Novome Biotechnologies is a DCVC-backed biotechnology company based in South San Francisco developing genetically engineered microbial medicines (GEMMs) - live bacterial therapeutics designed to colonize the gut and treat chronic conditions such as enteric hyperoxaluria and other GI and metabolic diseases. As a therapeutics developer, Novome is a research-and-drug-development organization rather than a software or API provider; the enrichment pass found no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: NowRx
providers.description: NowRx Inc. was a Silicon Valley technology-enabled pharmacy that paired proprietary prescription-fulfilment software (marketed as QuickFill), robotic dispensing inside low-overhead micro-fulfilment centers, and its own last-mile courier fleet to offer free same-day and same-hour delivery of prescription medications across California and Arizona. Founded in 2015 and led by co-founder and CEO Cary Breese, it raised roughly $30M — an unusually large share of it from retail investors through SeedInvest equity crowdfunding — and was last marked at about a $275M valuation before running out of money. The company wound down in late 2022: Alto Pharmacy acquired its California pharmacy patient business effective 2022-11-30 and Capsule took its Arizona patient files, with patients transferred automatically. NowRx never operated a public developer program. No api., developer., docs. or app. host under nowrx.com resolves or has ever been archived, its GitHub organization now holds zero public repositories, and the only surviving first-party engineering artifacts are two npm packages under the @nowrx scope — both vendored forks of third-party React Native libraries, last published in January 2022. The nowrx.com domain is no longer the company's: since late December 2023 it has served an unrelated WordPress health-content site under registrar privacy, so it is deliberately NOT wired here as a Website pointer. This profile is retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: Oration *
providers.description: Oration (Oration PBC, product OrationRx) was a Foster City, California prescription-savings SaaS that helped self-insured employers and their employees find the lowest-priced medications, analyzing over $1B in prescription drug purchases. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), Andreessen Horowitz, DCVC, Chicago Ventures and others (~$11.2M raised). The company was acquired by PokitDok in June 2017; its own domains (oration.io, orationrx.com) no longer resolve and no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface remains. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical life-sciences / pharmacy-benefits portfolio lead.

providers.name: Orbital Therapeutics
providers.description: Orbital Therapeutics was a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company developing next-generation RNA medicines, combining circular and linear RNA, targeted delivery, and AI-guided design across immunomodulation, in vivo CAR-T cell therapy, next-generation vaccines, and protein therapeutics. Its lead program, OTX-201, targeted autoimmune disease through B-cell depletion. Founded out of Beam Therapeutics and backed by ARCH Venture Partners, a16z Bio + Health, and Newpath Partners, the company raised a $270M Series A in 2023. In October 2025 Bristol Myers Squibb agreed to acquire Orbital Therapeutics for $1.5 billion; orbitaltx.com now redirects to bms.com. As a therapeutics developer, Orbital publishes no public developer platform, API, or machine-readable API surface, so this record is an identity-only profile in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: oricell
providers.description: Oricell Therapeutics (原启生物) is a Shanghai-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing cell-based immunotherapies for cancer, including GPC3-targeted CAR-T (Ori-C101) for advanced liver cancer and GPRC5D-targeted CAR-T (OriCAR-017) for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma. It operates proprietary OriAb antibody-discovery, OriCAR T-cell persistence, and cell-manufacturing (CMC) platforms. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners. As a clinical-stage biotech it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or technical developer surface; this profile is retained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Pardes Bio
providers.description: Pardes Biosciences was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing novel therapeutics to treat and prevent viral diseases. Founded in 2020 and based in Carlsbad, California, it used structure-based drug design and a tunable, reversible covalent chemistry platform. Its lead candidate, PBI-0451, was an oral direct-acting antiviral for SARS-CoV-2. The company was acquired in 2023 and no longer operates independently. It has no public API, developer program, or technical integration surface, and its former domain (pardesbio.com) is now a parked/registrar page.

providers.name: Pathios Therapeutics
providers.description: Pathios Therapeutics is a clinical-stage oncology and immunology drug discovery and development company based in Oxfordshire, United Kingdom, founded in 2017. The company develops small-molecule inhibitors of the pH-sensing G protein-coupled receptor GPR65 to counteract the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment; its lead asset PTT-4256 is a first-in-class GPR65 inhibitor now in a Phase 1/2 clinical trial. Backed by Canaan, Brandon Capital, and a strategic investment from Bristol Myers Squibb, Pathios is a research-stage biotech with no public API, developer platform, or technical integration surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and processed by the enrichment pipeline, which confirmed there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Peninsula Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Peninsula Pharmaceuticals is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Pozen
providers.description: POZEN Inc. was a specialty pharmaceutical company headquartered in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, founded in 1996 and focused on developing therapeutics for pain and pain-related conditions, most notably acute migraine. It was best known for the products Treximet (sumatriptan/naproxen) and Vimovo (naproxen/esomeprazole). POZEN traded publicly on NASDAQ under the ticker POZN and in 2016 combined with Tribute Pharmaceuticals to form Aralez Pharmaceuticals. Pozen was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As a pharmaceutical company it operated no public developer program, API, or SDK surface; an enrichment pass confirmed no API artifacts exist to harvest.

providers.name: Ricerca Biosciences
providers.description: Ricerca Biosciences is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: healthcare. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Semnur Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Semnur Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing non-opioid pain-management therapies. Its lead program, SP-102 (SEMDEXA), is a novel, non-opioid, preservative-free and particulate-free injectable corticosteroid gel formulation intended to treat moderate-to-severe chronic radicular pain (sciatica). Semnur is a subsidiary of Scilex Holding Company and is headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area, California. As a pharmaceutical R&D company it publishes a corporate website, investor presentation, and scientific publications, but exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Shanghai Desano Pharmaceutical Group
providers.description: Shanghai Desano Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. is a Chinese pharmaceutical company established in 1996 and headquartered in Shanghai's Zhangjiang High-Tech Park. It develops and commercializes medications addressing global public health needs, specializing in anti-AIDS (antiretroviral) and anti-malaria drugs, steroid hormone drugs, and nucleic acid drugs, with operations spanning R&D, manufacturing, regulatory registration, and international distribution across multiple production bases in Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Jiangxi. Note: in this company's domain "API" means Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (drug chemistry), not a web/developer API. Desano publishes no developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, developer portal, or other machine-readable API surface, so the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline has no technical artifacts to produce for this provider. It was surfaced as a false-positive lead from the Qiming venture portfolio.

providers.name: Silicon Therapeutics
providers.description: Silicon Therapeutics was a Boston-based biotechnology company that built an integrated, physics-based drug-discovery platform combining quantum mechanics, molecular simulation, and machine learning to design small-molecule medicines against historically intractable targets. Founded in 2015, it was acquired by Roivant Sciences in 2021 to form the basis of Roivant's computational discovery engine; its former site (silicontx.com) now redirects to roivant.com. The company is a computational drug-discovery firm with no public API, developer platform, SDK, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Sirtris Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Sirtris Pharmaceuticals is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Sunshine Lake Pharma
providers.description: Sunshine Lake Pharma (Guangdong East Sunshine Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., also known as HEC Pharm) is a Chinese pharmaceutical company established in 2003 and part of the Dongyangguang (HEC) Group. It engages in drug research, development, production, and commercialization across innovative drugs, improved formulations, generics, and biosimilars, focused on infections, chronic diseases, and oncology. Notable products include oseltamivir phosphate (influenza), sofosbuvir-based hepatitis C therapy, and insulin glargine (diabetes). It is a manufacturer with no public developer or API surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Teligene
providers.description: Teligene (Suzhou Teligene Biotechnology Co., Ltd.) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2011 in Suzhou, China by Dr. Zhang Dawei, a former chief scientist at Amgen. The company focuses on the design, research and industrialization of innovative small-molecule targeted drugs for oncology, with a pipeline addressing lung cancer, breast cancer, and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Teligene US LLC is a wholly owned US subsidiary advancing these candidates through clinical development. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of idg-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as a drug-development biotech it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Teneobio
providers.description: Teneobio was a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a new class of biologics, Human Heavy-Chain Antibodies (UniAb), for the treatment of cancer, autoimmunity, and infectious diseases. Its TeneoSeek discovery platform combined genetically engineered animals (UniRat, OmniFlic), next-generation sequencing, bioinformatics, and high-throughput vector assembly. Teneobio was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. Amgen acquired Teneobio in October 2021 for $900 million upfront plus up to $1.6 billion in contingent milestone payments; the company no longer operates independently and publishes no live developer surface. This is a life-sciences / therapeutics company with no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: The Pill Club
providers.description: The Pill Club was a US direct-to-consumer telehealth and pharmacy service for birth control and reproductive health, delivering prescription contraception and sexual-health products by mail. The brand has been consolidated into Nurx (a Thirty Madison company): its domain thepillclub.com now 301-redirects to nurx.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer, API, or documentation surface was found for either the legacy brand or its Nurx successor; this is a consumer healthcare service with no external API program.

providers.name: ThirtyFiveBio
providers.description: ThirtyFiveBio is an Oxford, UK biotechnology company founded in 2021 to develop first-in-class small-molecule inhibitors of G protein-coupled receptor 35 (GPR35) for the treatment of gastrointestinal diseases, including ulcerative colitis, inflammatory bowel disease, and digestive-tract cancers. The company was incubated by the M:M Bio (Molecule to Medicine) drug-discovery ecosystem together with Canaan Partners, and is backed by AbbVie Ventures, Mayewell Capital, and Innovate UK. It is a preclinical drug-discovery company with plans for first-in-human trials, not a software or API provider; this profile carries no developer API surface.

providers.name: Tizona Therapeutics
providers.description: Tizona Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing first-in-class cancer immunotherapies by translating novel scientific insights into new medicines. Its lead program, TTX-080, is a first-in-class HLA-G antagonist in clinical trials for advanced solid tumors. Tizona is a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. As a pharmaceutical drug-development company it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or other machine-readable API surface; this profile is retained as a network company record rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Tobira Therapeutics
providers.description: Tobira Therapeutics is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of canaan-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Unnatural Products
providers.description: Unnatural Products (UNP) is a Santa Cruz, California biotechnology company founded in 2017 by UC Santa Cruz alumni Cameron Pye and Joshua Schwochert. The company operates a drug-discovery platform for synthetic macrocyclic peptides, combining data science, machine learning, and parallel chemical synthesis to rapidly optimize potency, selectivity, and passive membrane permeability against traditionally "undruggable" targets that sit between small molecules and biologics. UNP works primarily through pharmaceutical research collaborations, including partnerships with Novartis, Merck, Argenx, and BridgeBio, and has raised approximately $38.4M. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Wing Venture Capital, it exposes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Verastem
providers.description: Verastem Oncology (Verastem, Inc.) is a development-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing novel therapies for cancers driven by the RAS/MAPK pathway, including KRAS-mutant tumors. Its work includes the first FDA-approved treatment for KRAS-mutant recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer, plus a pipeline targeting KRAS G12D inhibition. As a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and enriched with verified identity only.

providers.name: Vincentage
providers.description: Vincentage (Vincentage Pharma Co., Ltd.) is a clinical-stage biotech founded in 2021 and headquartered in Suzhou, China, developing novel small-molecule drugs for metabolic and cardiometabolic diseases including type 2 diabetes, obesity, and MASH. Its lead candidate is VCT220 (also known as CX11), an oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist; worldwide rights (excluding Greater China) to CX11 were acquired by Corxel Pharmaceuticals. Investors include IDG Capital, Everest VC, Shenzhen Capital Group, Galaxy Industry Group, and Kunshan Asia Aroma. Surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as a drug-discovery pharmaceutical company it publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical artifacts.

providers.name: Vivace Therapeutics
providers.description: Vivace Therapeutics is a clinical-stage, oncology-focused biotechnology company based in the San Francisco Bay Area, developing small-molecule cancer therapeutics that target the Hippo-YAP signaling pathway. Its lead candidate, VT3989, is in clinical trials for mesothelioma and other solid tumors. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a private therapeutics developer, Vivace publishes clinical-trial, scientific-publication, and corporate content, but exposes no public developer portal, API, SDK, documentation, or code repositories.

providers.name: Acureon Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Acureon Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was a private United States biopharmaceutical company founded in 2006 in the western suburbs of Philadelphia (Berwyn / Wayne, Pennsylvania), focused on specialty therapeutics intended to improve patient outcomes in the hospital areas of infectious disease, transplant and intensive care, by acquiring and commercializing novel and late-stage development drugs. It was backed by Domain Associates, New Enterprise Associates and Alta Partners. The company is defunct: it closed in 2008, filed nothing with the SEC after a single 2006 Form D (CIK 0001365869), and its former domain acureonpharma.com was re-registered by an unrelated party in November 2022 and now serves an unrelated medical-loan content site. Acureon published no API, developer program, SDK or machine-readable specification while it operated, and there is no first-party surface left to profile.

providers.name: Arkuda Therapeutics
providers.description: Arkuda Therapeutics, Inc. was a privately held, preclinical-stage biotechnology company based in Watertown, Massachusetts, founded in 2018 by Gerhard Koenig, Ph.D. and Duane Burnett to develop small-molecule enhancers of lysosomal function for neurodegenerative disease. Its lead biology targeted progranulin (GRN) and lysosomal dysfunction in frontotemporal dementia (FTD-GRN), Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease. Arkuda closed a $44M Series A in November 2019 and a $64M Series B in February 2022, backed by Atlas Venture, Cormorant Asset Management, Pfizer Ventures, abrdn plc, Mission BioCapital and Eli Lilly and Company. On 27 February 2024 it entered an option and asset purchase agreement with Johnson & Johnson, and on 9 January 2025 Johnson & Johnson (through Janssen Pharmaceuticals) exercised that option and acquired the entire portfolio of lysosomal function enhancers. Independent operations concluded thereafter; founder and CEO Gerhard Koenig became CEO of Augustine Therapeutics in January 2025. Arkuda was a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it never operated a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract, and both of its former domains have since lapsed.

providers.name: Capstan Therapeutics
providers.description: Capstan Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in San Diego, California, developing in vivo cell engineering medicines built on a proprietary targeted lipid nanoparticle (tLNP) platform that delivers mRNA and other RNA payloads to specific cell types inside the body. Its lead candidate CPTX2309 is an anti-CD19 in vivo CAR-T therapy in Phase 1 for B cell-mediated autoimmune disease, intended to achieve deep B cell depletion without lymphodepleting chemotherapy. AbbVie completed its acquisition of Capstan on 19 August 2025 for up to $2.1 billion. The company's own domain now redirects to AbbVie and its DNS is served by AbbVie nameservers; it operates no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Concentric Analgesics
providers.description: Concentric Analgesics, Inc. is a San Francisco based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing non-opioid pain therapeutics. Its lead candidate, vocacapsaicin (CA-008), is a first-in-class prodrug that converts to capsaicin, a TRPV1 agonist that selectively desensitizes pain-conducting nerve fibers without sensory numbness or motor weakness, given as a single local injection during surgery. The program holds FDA Fast Track designation (2017) and Breakthrough Therapy designation (2018), and has been evaluated in Phase 2 trials in bunionectomy, total knee arthroplasty and open ventral hernia repair. The company is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or other machine-readable surface, and as of this check its corporate website is an expired Squarespace account that returns HTTP 404 for every path.

providers.name: Intarcia Therapeutics
providers.description: Intarcia Therapeutics, Inc. was a Boston-headquartered clinical-stage biopharmaceutical and drug-delivery company, founded in 1997 and once valued at roughly $5.5B, that developed the Medici Drug Delivery System — a matchstick-sized subdermal osmotic mini-pump engineered to stabilize therapeutic proteins and peptides at body temperature and release them continuously for months from a single placement. Its lead candidate, ITCA 650, delivered the GLP-1 receptor agonist exenatide for type 2 diabetes over three- to six-month intervals. The FDA issued complete response letters on the ITCA 650 new drug application in 2017 and again in 2020, after which the company ran out of capital, laid off staff, closed its Boston, Hayward (CA) and Durham (NC) sites and liquidated its manufacturing and laboratory equipment at auction. Its remaining assets — the Medici platform and ITCA 650 — were acquired by i2o Therapeutics in August 2023, and FDA published a final decision refusing to approve the ITCA 650 application on 2024-08-23. Intarcia was a drug-device developer rather than a software company: its corporate site carried only Medici System, Pipeline, Newsroom, About, Leadership and Careers sections and never published a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification of any kind. As of 2026-08-23 both intarcia.com and intarciatherapeutics.com resolve to an Atom.com domain-broker parking page that offers the names for sale and returns HTTP 404 on every path, and no developer-facing subdomain resolves. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Metacrine
providers.description: Metacrine, Inc. was a San Diego, California clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2014 to develop differentiated therapies for liver and gastrointestinal disease. It built a proprietary farnesoid X receptor (FXR) platform on a distinct chemical scaffold and advanced two oral, once-daily FXR agonists — MET409 and MET642 — through Phase 1 and Phase 2 trials in non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), alongside exploratory work in inflammatory bowel disease. Backed by ARCH Venture Partners, Polaris Partners, venBio and EcoR1 Capital, it raised a $36M round in 2015 and a $65M Series C in June 2018 before pricing an initial public offering on 2020-09-15 of 6,540,000 shares at $13.00, for roughly $85.0M gross, and listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market as MTCR. Equillium, Inc. agreed to acquire the company in an all-stock transaction announced 2022-09-06, but the two mutually terminated the merger agreement on 2022-12-23. The board approved a Plan of Dissolution on 2023-01-24; Nasdaq issued a minimum-bid-price delisting notice on 2023-01-31, trading was suspended on 2023-02-09 and delisting took effect 2023-03-13; the FXR program assets were sold under a February 2023 term sheet for up to $4.0M in cash plus assumed liabilities; stockholders approved the dissolution on 2023-03-23; and the company filed a Certificate of Dissolution with the Delaware Secretary of State on 2023-03-24, effective on filing under DGCL Section 275. Metacrine was a drug developer, not a software vendor, and it never published a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface, or machine-readable specification of any kind. Its domain metacrine.com has since lapsed and is parked. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Vascular Therapies
providers.description: Vascular Therapies, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Cresskill, New Jersey, developing Sirogen, a proprietary sirolimus formulation delivered from a bioabsorbable collagen implant placed perivascularly at the time of surgery. The product is aimed at reducing surgical stenosis and improving arteriovenous fistula maturation and patency in end-stage renal disease patients who need hemodialysis vascular access. Sirolimus for dialysis vascular access carries FDA Fast Track status and Orphan Drug designation in both the United States and the European Union. The company ran the Phase 3 ACCESS trial (243 ESRD patients across 20 US sites) and the multinational Phase 3 ACCESS 2 trial, whose topline results presented in April 2025 did not meet the primary clinical fistula maturation endpoint. Vascular Therapies is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it ships a drug-device combination product through clinical trials and regulatory review, and publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Dechert
providers.description: Dechert LLP is a global law firm founded in 1875 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with "more than 900 lawyers" across 22 offices in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia (Wikipedia cites roughly 1,000 attorneys in 20 offices; the firm itself emphasizes a global footprint spanning the U.S., Europe, Asia, and the Middle East). The firm is known for market-leading practices in financial services and investment management, private equity, private credit, mergers and acquisitions, international arbitration, intellectual property, life sciences, white collar enforcement, and antitrust. Dechert publishes deep thought-leadership through its OnPoint series, Crypto Bytes, FSR Radar, THE CRED, and ReTorts; produces multiple podcasts (Dechert 4 Real, Committed Capital, Dechert On Reg); and operates proprietary information platforms including DAMITT (Dechert Antitrust Merger Investigation Timing Tracker), World Compass, World Passport, Dechert Direct, and a Box Portal. Despite these data-driven products, Dechert does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, GraphQL endpoint, webhook surface, status page, changelog, or developer portal, and does not publish an RSS feed for OnPoint or any blog series — its only public-facing subscription mechanism is an email preference form.
